title: PrivacyFlow: Privacy in AI Agents through Information Flow Analysis and Consequence-Aware Risk Management
summary: Autonomous LLM agents executing multi-step workflows over personal data often misalign with user privacy expectations and leak sensitive, out-of-context information. Although Contextual Integrity (CI) formalizes this problem, existing benchmarks and defenses rarely operationalize CI for realistic multi-step task sequences in evolving environments. In this work, we first introduce agentic PrivacyBench, a benchmark of 5873 tasks in 986 task sequences with dynamic environment updates and CI-grounded allow-sets for sensitive information. We also introduce PrivacyFlow, a defense that separates deliberative privacy planning (System 2) from task execution (System 1), treating each sharing decision as a structured risk-management problem. Before execution, PrivacyFlow traces the provenance and purpose of each planned data flow, models recipient background knowledge, and simulates what external actors could infer. This allows us to model the downstream consequences of disclosure, including inference attacks and context-dependent harms. It then weighs the remaining disclosure risk against task utility and executes a minimized plan, blocks it, or consults the user. Across six models, PrivacyFlow significantly reduces step-level privacy failures and raises the share of completed task sequences without a detected privacy violation by 22--55 percentage points. We further highlight a new privacy--utility--autonomy tradeoff: allowing PrivacyFlow to proactively prompt the user in case of uncertainty can increase authorized task completion at the cost of shifting decision effort back to the user. Our results suggest that proactive CI reasoning can substantially improve agentic privacy and motivate further study of this tradeoff.

title: Characterizing LLM Agent Behaviors in Module Shadowing Environments
summary: LLM agents operating in untrusted workspaces face the risk of untrusted code execution during routine tasks, yet final reports and workspace states alone cannot reliably establish whether execution occurred. We introduce an evaluation framework that codes observation, reasoning, execution, and response behaviors from agent trajectories and aligns them with independent environmental records to reconstruct execution histories and verify final reports. We apply this framework to module shadowing, in which a local file is loaded in place of a trusted module during import, enabling untrusted code execution without adversarial prompts. Across 90 trials with 15 models, the payload executed in 51% of direct shadowing trials and 87% of indirect shadowing trials. Even explicit recognition of the shadowing mechanism did not ensure prevention, as the payload ran in 10 of the 29 trials with recorded recognition. These failures were often omitted from final reports, as 49 of the 62 triggered trials ended without mention of the security issue. Three reports even denied execution, including one from a trial in which independent logs recorded 19 payload executions. Final workspace states also obscured prior execution when agents deleted or overwrote the payload marker in 10 triggered trials. These findings demonstrate that combining behavioral coding with independent environmental auditing enables rigorous and transparent evaluation of agent safety.

title: MetaVul: Agentic Harness Discovery for Vulnerability Detection
summary: LLM agents are increasingly used to automate vulnerability detection, but reliable detection is challenging because agents must distinguish subtle, security-relevant fixes from benign code variation. While underlying LLM capability has improved significantly, the accuracy of the agent still depends heavily on the harness: the code that defines the scaffolding around the LLM. Harnesses are typically fixed, and largely hand-written, limiting adaptation to evaluator feedback. Additionally, when harnesses are static, improvements on one dataset or model may not transfer to others. To address these challenges, we introduce MetaVul, a self-improving framework for harness discovery in vulnerability detection. Starting from a seed structured reasoning scaffold, MetaVul uses a workflow-based optimization loop to iteratively refine the harness using feedback from paired vulnerable and patched functions, while preserving the structured reasoning and verdict format. At each iteration, it searches over the history of prior harnesses, with access to their trajectories, logs, and metrics, and it returns a set of Pareto-optimal harnesses. We apply MetaVul to discover agent harnesses for various architectures. A validation set (202 pairs) is used for optimization, while an unseen dataset (430 pairs) is kept as the held-out set. We test whether harnesses learned from one model transfer to others not seen during optimization. Results on both frontier and small LLMs show that the optimized harnesses improve pairwise vulnerability detection up to 23.3 percentage points on the validation set and up to 25.8 points on the held-out set with a Pareto-frontier harness. Harnesses learned with one model also transfer to others. We show that harnesses optimized with one model transfer to another, improving held-out pairwise accuracy by 14.7 points without further optimization.

title: Li$^{2}$SAO: Lifting Light Singl-Rollout Asynchronous RL Optimization via Group-Relative Actor-Critic Bootstrapping
summary: Asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) is becoming a mainstream paradigm for post-training large language models (LLMs), as it improves training efficiency by updating the model as rollouts arrive. Recent work argues that group-wise sampling in GRPO does not naturally fit asynchronous RL training because rollout lengths follow a long-tailed distribution, and proposes Single-rollout Asynchronous Optimization (SAO) to improve stability and off-policy behavior, especially on agentic tasks. However, SAO relies on a closed-source value model obtained from scaling value pretraining. In this paper, we analyze GRPO and LiSAO, our lightweight reproduction of SAO without the pretrained value model, on single-turn reasoning and multi-turn agentic tasks. We find that GRPO outperforms LiSAO on reasoning tasks, while the reverse holds on agentic tasks. Since the value model of LiSAO is not yet well trained , LiSAO lags behind GRPO substantially in early training steps. To address this issue, we propose Li$^{2}$SAO, which Lifts Light Single-rollout Asynchronous Optimization with group-relative actor-critic bootstrapping: while the critic is cold, a group-relative advantage trains the actor and a group-centered return trains the critic, after which training switches to single-rollout GAE. Experiments show that Li$^{2}$SAO catches up with or surpasses GRPO in early training and further raises the later performance ceiling. Code is available at https://github.com/jd-cc-coder/Li2SAO.

title: Bayesian Distribution System State Estimation with Flow Matching
summary: Medium-voltage feeders have few real-time measurements, so distribution system state estimation (DSSE) rests on pseudo-measurements of the secondary substations, a prior in Bayesian terms. Weighted least squares keeps the power flow exact but reduces this prior to a mean and variance, while supervised deep learning estimators also learn the power flow and are tied to one measurement set. We propose PoSE (posterior sampling for state estimation), which keeps the Bayesian structure of DSSE and learns only what the distribution system operator does not know, namely the distribution of substation injections, modelled by a neural network trained with flow matching on historical data. The power flow equations, grid topology and measurements enter only at sampling, through a noise-aware Kalman-type correction. The neural network therefore never approximates the power flow, but every posterior sample is a physically consistent operating point, and one trained prior serves any measurement set, noise level and topology. On the IEEE 33-bus feeder, PoSE lowers the probabilistic injection error (CRPS) by 6.7-7.5% against a full-covariance Gaussian prior in all 12 tested settings. It provides reliable uncertainty: the 90% intervals contain the true injection almost exactly as often as exact posterior samples would, whereas those of supervised estimators contain it in only 37-78% of cases. On the 240-bus unbalanced three-phase Iowa feeder, it gives the lowest injection, voltage and branch-current errors of all estimators. A fast variant matches this accuracy at 0.2-0.6s per snapshot and, without retraining, beats Gaussian priors and retrained supervised estimators on seven reconfigured topologies.

title: Don't Just Impute, Detect: Task-Aware Diffusion Pipelines for Edge Anomaly Detection
comments: 11 pages, 6 figures. Accepted at the 33rd IEEE International Conference on High Performance Computing, Data, and Analytics (HiPC 2026)
summary: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) edge pipelines routinely lose contiguous blocks of multi-sensor data to network dropouts and hardware faults. The standard remedy is a disjointed "impute-then-detect" pipeline whose imputer is trained only for Mean Squared Error (MSE). Such an imputer fills a missing block with the most probable normal pattern: a partially observed anomaly is smoothed back toward normality, and boundary artifacts on normal data raise false alarms. We call this imputation bias and propose the Task-Aware Diffusion Refiner (TADR), a conditional diffusion refiner trained against the loss landscape of a frozen downstream detector. Because back-propagating through the sampling trajectory is intractable, the task-aware terms act on the one-step clean-window estimate that the noise prediction already yields, so training costs no more than plain diffusion training. Under strict Point-to-Point evaluation over five seeds with paired significance tests, TADR raises F1 by $0.338$ over the unrefined detector on SMD ($p = 0.0015$), and the anomaly enhancement objective alone contributes $0.463$ in ablation. We also characterise when the method helps: the gain tracks the continuous, mutually redundant channels available and the anomaly evidence the outage removes, and it is absent on telemetry datasets dominated by one-hot command channels and on PSM. At ten sampling steps TADR runs in $41.4$ ms per window on a single CPU core, sustaining about $24$ concurrent 1 Hz streams from a $4.03$ MB model. Code and per-seed results are available at https://github.com/int-park422/TADR.
comment: 11 pages, 6 figures. Accepted at the 33rd IEEE International Conference on High Performance Computing, Data, and Analytics (HiPC 2026)

title: RiskyPy: Toward Model-Calibrated Prompt Generation for Joint Security and Functionality Evaluation of LLM-Generated Code
summary: Evaluating approaches that improve the security of LLM code generation requires datasets that jointly assess security and functionality and remain adapted to the capabilities of the models being studied. However, existing benchmarks are costly to produce and are generally not calibrated to a chosen range of model capabilities. We introduce RiskyPy, an automated pipeline that generates security-oriented code-generation datasets calibrated to model proficiency using functionality and vulnerability canaries. We instantiate RiskyPy for Python using domains covering 18 CWEs from the 2025 CWE Top 25, producing 101 prompts. Experiments on Qwen3-4B and Seed-Coder-8B show that the generated tasks remain functionally accessible, with 57-72% of prompts yielding functional code, while only 5-10% of generations are free of Bandit findings, leaving room for joint evaluation of security and functionality of security improvement approaches.

title: Unsupervised Feature Selection Using Local Intrinsic Dimensionality -- Extended Version
comments: Preprint submitted to Elsevier Pattern Recognition
summary: High dimensionality degrades both the efficiency and the effectiveness of learning algorithms, and in many applications no class labels are available to guide dimensionality reduction. This paper proposes LIDFS, an unsupervised feature selection method based on Local Intrinsic Dimensionality (LID). The method builds on the formal equivalence between LID and the indiscriminability of distance measures. The data matrix is transposed so that each feature is treated as a point, and the LID of each feature is estimated by maximum likelihood from the distances to its $k$ nearest neighboring features. Features with lower LID exhibit greater local discriminability and receive higher importance scores. A refinement step then retains one representative per feature neighborhood and demotes locally redundant features. The result is a complete ranking from which any number of features can be selected without rerunning the procedure. LIDFS does not use any information about labels or the number of classes, and runs in $\mathcal{O}(d^2 n)$ time for $n$ instances and $d$ features. LIDFS is compared with classic and state-of-the-art methods and a random baseline on 23 high-dimensional datasets, the classic benchmark collection. The evaluation uses classification accuracy and AUC with five downstream classifiers, as well as clustering accuracy and normalized mutual information, over both full and aggressive selection ranges. LIDFS ranks first in the supervised evaluations and first or tied second in the clustering-based evaluations. It belongs to the top statistical group together with methods that require the number of classes, and it runs faster than its closest competitor. Several recent methods, by contrast, fail to outperform the random baseline. A sensitivity analysis shows that small neighborhood sizes yield the best results.
comment: Preprint submitted to Elsevier Pattern Recognition

title: Apriel Voice 27B Preview: An Open Model for Speech, Reasoning, and Tool Use
summary: A capable voice assistant must do more than recognize words; it must understand requests, reason over context, sustain conversations, and act through tools. We present Apriel Voice 27B Preview, an open speech-language model that unifies these capabilities within a shared reasoning backbone while retaining text and image input modalities. Built on the post-trained Gemma 4 26B-A4B checkpoint, Apriel Voice directly processes speech and generates both responses and tool calls without requiring a separate dialogue model. We introduce a two-stage training procedure to adapt the model to speech. The first stage establishes the speech interface, while the second jointly adapts the projector and backbone through supervised fine-tuning, text replay, and source-dependent cross-entropy and forward Kullback--Leibler divergence supervision. Automatically constructed speech-conditioned dialogues provide conversational training data, while local teacher serving, overlapping teacher and student computation, and fused full-vocabulary losses enable efficient online distillation. In thinking mode, Apriel Voice achieves a score of 98.90 on Big Bench Audio, 81.13 on Speech-BFCL, and a task success rate of 65.51% on $τ$-Voice, with a mean latency of 1.91 seconds. It also achieves 51.27% English EVA accuracy and 74.13% experience pass@1. Finally, we deploy Apriel Voice 27B Preview on a custom serving platform to support interactive voice interactions.

title: Certified Behavioral Retention for Continual Adaptation with Held-Out Anchors
comments: 11 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Continual Learning in the Era of Foundation Models and Embodied Agents (CL4M / CL4FMAgents)
summary: Continual adaptation requires deciding not only how to update a model, but whether to commit an update without exceeding a declared budget for changes to protected behavior. We introduce Certified Anchor-Based Adaptation (CABA), a candidate-agnostic post-update gate that reserves historical observations from candidate optimization, compares old and candidate policies on frozen representations, and selects the largest tested interpolation coefficient whose worst-anchor forward KL divergence remains within budget. The finite check requires neither action labels nor complete trajectories. We develop a theory-led certification framework that separates measured anchor retention from conditional off-anchor guarantees. Under explicit representation-coverage and Lipschitz assumptions, an accepted update satisfies a uniform behavioral-divergence bound on protected support. The analysis gives regularity bounds for affine softmax heads, probabilistic coverage and compression guarantees, interpolation monotonicity conditions, grid-resolution bounds, and trajectory-level and sequential-composition guarantees. In a controlled UCI Human Activity Recognition study used as a non-stationary sensor-policy proxy, CABA reduces mean forgetting from 1.01 percent for unconstrained adaptation to 0.00 percent at budget epsilon = 0.05, while reducing final average accuracy from 93.04 percent to 88.48 percent. The experiment illustrates a retention-plasticity trade-off and does not establish foundation-model or robotic performance. CABA provides an auditable retention check for candidate generators exposing comparable policy distributions and a declared update path, while deployment also requires separate evidence of current-task utility.
comment: 11 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Continual Learning in the Era of Foundation Models and Embodied Agents (CL4M / CL4FMAgents)

title: Prevented is Not Protected: What Attack Success Rate Hides about RAG
summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is vulnerable to knowledge poisoning, where adversaries manipulate retrieved evidence to influence model outputs. Existing defenses are primarily evaluated using attack success rate (ASR), which obscures defense-induced failures and the mechanisms behind apparent attack prevention. To address this issue, this work introduces \textbf{Aligned RAG Evaluation}, a matched-query protocol that jointly examines clean and poisoned responses, with and without defense. By combining matched conditions analysis, LLM-judge endorsement, and retrieval dependence controls, the proposed framework distinguishes prevented from introduced failures, target mentions from LLM endorsement, and single-passage influence from evidence composition. Experiments on HotpotQA and Natural Questions reveal that existing defenses can introduce unexpected target-positive answers, although they can prevent some attacks, while evaluation criteria can also change defense rankings. Our findings expose critical blind spots in ASR-based evaluation and motivate a more comprehensive assessment of RAG poisoning defenses. The code and the evaluation artifact are available at https://github.com/chxhana/aligned-rag-eval.

title: CLIC: Closed-Loop Intent Consistency for Securing LLM-Driven Control in Open RAN
summary: With the progressive capabilities of large language models (LLMs), researchers are finding ways to integrate them into the control loops of Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) to enable slicing and resource management through user intents. However, integration of LLMs in the O-RAN control loop via the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) makes the system vulnerable to \textit{runtime prompt injection threats}, which manipulate control decisions without violating interface authentication, and \textit{residual virtual prompt injection (VPI)} attacks that plant trigger mechanisms to silently steer the behaviour during fine-tuning. Existing studies address only the runtime threat and do not enforce consistency across the full control path, i.e. from the certified A1 intent, through the multi-step LLM trajectory, to the final E2 action. We propose a closed-loop intent-consistency layer (CLIC) that jointly mitigates both threats. The proposed CLIC defines a formal consistency score using a small quantized language model, which is deployed as a Non-RT rApp for model-integrity certification along with a Near-RT xApp for runtime enforcement. We implement CLIC on the OpenAI Cellular (OAIC) platform and evaluate it under domain-adapted JailbreakBench, AdvBench, and VPI workloads. The experimental results show that the proposed CLIC reduces the attack success rate from 0.92 to 0.29 and residual VPI attacks from 0.37 to 0.04, while improving isolation and fairness at slightly higher latency costs, i.e. approximately 27 ms.

title: What It Costs to Trust a Source: A Reproducible Method for Institutional Assessment of Author Disambiguation
summary: Records of research outputs are curated with care by universities, and the effort is shaped by the external sources from which candidate records are drawn. The curation required before the author identities in such sources can be trusted is examined, and a reproducible method for estimating its cost is set out. Four tests are described; two can be run on public data alone, and two are conducted against an institution's own curated record, taken from Symplectic Elements Discovery portals. The method is demonstrated on OpenAlex and Dimensions across 30 institutions. Of the publications attributed to matched researchers, 50.4\% were confirmed by the institutional record for OpenAlex and 69.6\% for Dimensions, and fewer trusted researcher profiles were retained from OpenAlex at a matched confidence threshold in each of the 30 institutions. Carried through to effort, integrating OpenAlex requires 1.5 times the person-days of review and entry of Dimensions even when each feed is filtered at the threshold that minimises the amount of review required.

title: Mage-VL-Cowork: A Full Training Recipe to Learn Hybrid Computer Use From Evolved Harnesses
summary: Effective computer-use agents (CUAs) should seamlessly combine visual GUI interaction with code and terminal execution within a single policy. We present Mage-VL-Cowork, a 4B hybrid CUA trained from a general multimodally aligned checkpoint through an end-to-end, progressive five-stage curriculum across midtraining, SFT, and RL. To power this curriculum at scale, Mage-CUA-Forge replaces per-task agent construction with reusable, skill-conditioned generation workflows and application-specific preparers, synthesizing 293,806 desktop and web tasks across 6,915 skills while reducing recurring per-task expenditure by 82.6%. Rather than directly distilling a default teacher, we evolve the teacher harness and instantiate specialized CUA harnesses to yield high-quality trajectories alongside stage-specific supervision. Mage-VL-Cowork-4B finally climbs to 66.0% on OSWorld-Verified through different training stages with more efficient reasoning cost, achieving state-of-the-art performance at its parameter size and pushing forward the frontier of on-device intelligence.

title: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
comments: Authors are listed in alphabetical order. Project page: https://worldbridge-jd.github.io/
summary: Achieving the broad task generalization of embodied models in physical environments remains a central challenge in robot learning. We study this challenge in World Action Models (WAMs) through two complementary capabilities: video generalization, which predicts the visual evolution of new tasks, and action generalization, which translates these predictions into executable behavior through a video-to-action bridge. By varying video and action supervision for tasks outside an initial training set, we examine their respective contributions to task transfer. On RoboTwin 2.0, using only in-distribution video-action supervision yields a 25.07% success rate on out-of-distribution tasks. Introducing videos of these tasks without their action labels raises success to 55.90%, while adding just one action-labeled demonstration per task further improves it to 70.70%. These findings suggest that broader video coverage enables task transfer by leveraging existing inverse-dynamics capabilities, while even sparse action supervision further strengthens those capabilities. Guided by this perspective, we introduce WorldBridge, a WAM with separate video and action experts connected through structured attention and trained with joint flow matching. WorldBridge incorporates visual memory at two temporal scales and action forcing, alongside a unified data processing pipeline that standardizes and filters heterogeneous robot trajectories and egocentric hand-derived supervision. Across multiple manipulation benchmarks, WorldBridge achieves state-of-the-art performance among the compared methods, including 96.23% on RoboTwin 2.0 full data setting and 80.9% on clean to random setting, 82.8% on RoboCasa GR1 TableTop, and 57.6% on DOMINO Level-1. Our study highlights the complementary roles of video prediction and action grounding in developing robots that generalize across tasks.
comment: Authors are listed in alphabetical order. Project page: https://worldbridge-jd.github.io/

title: Safin-1.5: Safety-Native Architecture and Verifiable Reasoning for Recursive Safety Improvement
summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) enables large language models to advance their capabilities through successive updates, but these updates can also introduce new risks and weaken existing safeguards. In line with the AI-45° Law, we pursue Safety RSI, in which safety develops as an intrinsic capability alongside general model capabilities through continual risk discovery and repair, while preserving utility and limiting over-refusal. We introduce Safin-1.5, a model built on a safety architecture and trained through recursive safety improvement, with an inference-time harness that extends its capabilities to formal reasoning. Our approach comprises three components: i) The safety architecture combines persistent safety states with hazardous-knowledge disentanglement. The former retains and selectively invokes safety knowledge, while the latter relocates targeted hazardous knowledge into removable experts, enabling its removal with minimal impact on general capabilities. ii) Recursive safety improvement establishes a discovery-evaluation-repair loop. The loop identifies new vulnerabilities and uses experimental feedback to develop repair strategies. It accepts updates only when they improve safety while preserving general capabilities and limiting over-refusal. iii) The formal reasoning harness combines the model's language understanding with symbolic inference and verification. Proof-obligation-guided semantic bridging recovers missing relations in formal representations, enabling symbolic solvers to construct checkable proofs under formalized premises and accepted semantic bridges. Experimental results demonstrate that Safin-1.5 achieves safety and reasoning performance, outperforming frontier models.

title: PathoJev: Efficient Pathology Decisions from Shared Visual Context
summary: Pathology workflows require multiple visual judgments about the same slide, from identifying tumor type to assessing grade and invasion. Generating and parsing a separate textual response for each structured question adds latency between visual evidence and usable decisions. Building on the System One paradigm, we introduce PathoJev, a pathology model that directly predicts answer probabilities for whole-slide and region-level assessment. PathoJev encodes each slide once and evaluates independent question suffixes in batches over the shared visual context. Reusing the hybrid backbone's recurrent states further limits the computation that grows with slide-context length for each additional question. Across three whole-slide benchmarks, the 9B and 27B models achieve mean accuracies of 77.2% and 78.1%, exceeding SlideChat by 5.4 and 6.3 percentage points. Both scales also maintain competitive accuracy on five ROI benchmarks. On WSI-Bench, the 9B model runs 9.1x faster than SlideChat. Shared context accelerates eight-question workloads by 6.9x and 5.9x over separate prefix encoding, rising to 11.2x and 8.9x for 64 questions. These results provide a reusable probabilistic interface for combining multiple visual judgments in whole-slide and local tissue assessment. Code: https://github.com/ChyaZhang/PathoJev.

title: "Shall We Approve?" Consequence-Aware Approval for Autonomous Coding Agents
summary: Coding agents increasingly rely on automated approvers to decide whether a proposed shell command may run. Existing approvers, from rule-based checkers to guardrail models and deployed permission classifiers, base their decisions on the text of the request and command. Yet a command's behavior depends on the code it invokes and the state of the workspace, and systems that observe file changes leave the assessment to the agent or a human after execution. We present Caper, a consequence-aware approval mechanism that pre-executes each command in a snapshotted sandbox, provides an independent approver with a bounded report of its observed effects, commits allowed commands, and rolls back blocked ones with a reason the agent can act on. Compared with six existing systems, Caper achieves the lowest harmful-outcome rate on SABER (6.7% versus at least 14.8%) and YoloFS-Ext, a benchmark we build in which harmful behavior is hidden inside invoked tools (7.8% versus at least 35.3%), while blocking 1.0% of the safe twins of the dangerous tasks in YoloFS-Ext.

title: DyCraft: An Agentic System for Long-Horizon 4D Scene Generation
summary: While frontier coding agents can generate high-quality 3D scenes and articulated assets, they struggle to create coherent long-horizon animations. When equipped with general-purpose harnesses, they frequently produce physically implausible outputs, generating objects that interpenetrate, lack physical support, or move unnaturally. Such bare agents struggle to repair these errors because they default to scripting the full animation in one pass, making it difficult to verify their work and disentangle complex spatiotemporal constraints. Drawing on the practice of human animators, we introduce DyCraft, a system for animated 3D scene generation that breaks animation into steps that coding agents can more reliably solve. DyCraft first expands the user's prompt into a detailed plan and builds a static scene. It then creates a 3D storyboard of key animation poses, where each frame is a static 3D scene that the agent can build and debug in isolation. Storyboarding decomposes the problem into pairs of verified start and end states, allowing the agent to author local motion between them with a collection of motion authoring tools. We evaluate DyCraft on 24 long-horizon, multi-shot animation tasks covering humanoid robots, human and animal characters, and physical mechanisms. Compared with a native GPT-6 agent in Codex and prior agentic baselines, DyCraft substantially reduces physical violations and generates higher-quality animated 3D scenes that are more often preferred by human raters.

title: AutoHebb: Self-Modifying Neural Networks that Zero-Shot Infer and Continually Learn
summary: Humans and animals have a unique capacity to generalize and learn in novel circumstances, including "0-shot" inference (ZI) and continual learning (CL) -- two powerful cognitive abilities. Despite this importance, efforts to model ZI and CL are seriously limited in several ways. First, existing models typically lack components critical to ZI and CL in the brain, namely, strong inductive biases (for ZI) and autonomous control of learning (for CL). Second, models can be less tractable to analysis if model components are overly complex (lacking simplicity), or too task-restricted if model components are overly bespoke (lacking expressivity). Here we introduce autonomous Hebbian networks ("AutoHebb"), a class of online learning feedforward neural networks that realize strong inductive biases and autonomously controlled learning, and are both simple and expressive. Unlike standard models that learn via externally controlled optimization (e.g. gradient descent), AutoHebb networks combine external feedback with internally generated activity to produce a global learning signal ('neuromodulator') fed back to the network. The neuromodulator in turn gates a biologically grounded local learning rule (3-factor Hebbian rule) that updates networks' plastic weights. Using meta-learning to search for fixed (non-plastic) weights, we find that AutoHebb networks (1) succeed on ZI tasks, (2) show emergent (untrained) ZI/CL abilities, (3) admit reverse-engineering into explicit algorithms, and (4) outperform modern learning models on ZI/CL tasks. Lastly, performance comparisons to related models implied an essential role for three model components: meta-learning, Hebbian plasticity, and autonomous control of learning. These findings indicate that AutoHebb may be useful in hypothesis generation, analysis, and discovery of biologically grounded forms of learning and generalization.

title: More Rules, Longer Lists? Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on a Hidden-Rule Curriculum
summary: Self-evolving agents rewrite a persistent state from feedback, but it is largely untested whether this lets them learn a rule nobody told them. An agent can also pass by writing down each correction as an exception, and its list then grows with every new rule. We introduce CLR-Bench, a Curriculum of Latent Rules benchmark. Each chain adds one hidden rule per level on top of the earlier ones. A rule acts on an opaque label that stands for a named grouping published on the Web, such as the founding members of an airline alliance. The task gives one example value, practice feedback reveals one more member and one non-member, and the test checks unseen members and similar non-members. Probes certify that the base model knows the members of each grouping and does not guess it without feedback, and that the evidence identifies the grouping once labels are read as named groupings. An automated pipeline builds chains from a new data domain, and we release 20 chains over 10 domains. We evaluate six recent self-evolution methods. With the certifying model they barely learn. The best gain at most 5 points over a frozen agent and exclude only 6-12% of the unseen members from the count, fewer than the 20% reached by simply keeping the raw practice history. A fixed lesson that states the named-grouping convention lifts the same methods by 14.5 to 16.5 points. Their states hold the revealed member in 75-98% of cases and almost never the class name, and when practice exposes a member the list misses, they add that member to the list. With the stronger GPT-6-Sol, ACE and Dynamic Cheatsheet learn from feedback alone. They reach 78% accuracy and solve 59-60% of the single cells, against 53% and 8% with the certifying model, and they surpass the raw history. CLR-Bench therefore measures how well an agent learns, and this ability differs across models.

title: TAPE: Learning General Audio Effect Representations
comments: Submitted to Transactions of Machine Learning Research; 25 pages, 5 figures, 18 tables
summary: Musicians and mixing engineers often can decipher the signal processing chain they hear on a reference recording, then adapt it to new material. We present TAPE (Transformations of Audio Parameter Embeddings), which estimates this processing from the processed reference audio alone. An encoder trained to identify processors in eight major effect families maps the reference to an embedding. A differentiable digital signal processing (DSP) chain decodes the embedding into editable parameters in one forward pass and applies them to a different unprocessed recording. Its modules are equalization, compression, waveshaping, a small residual network, and reverberation. TAPE achieves lower spectral error than DeepAFx-ST, the previous state of the art for single-step regression, and lower spectral error than per-example search over a chain approximating ST-ITO's, while running 275$\times$ faster than that search. Because the decoder outputs DSP parameters, its chain can also run causally: a C++ implementation with the trained weights processed 128-sample buffers 1.8$\times$ faster than real time, with no missed deadlines.
comment: Submitted to Transactions of Machine Learning Research; 25 pages, 5 figures, 18 tables

title: Personalised 3D Mnemonics for Vocabulary Learning in Context
summary: Augmented reality (AR) can support vocabulary learning by placing mnemonic cues in the physical contexts where new words are encountered. Prior work has augmented real objects with bilingual labels, audio, keywords, and 3D visualisations of those keywords interacting with the objects, but these cues are typically predefined by system designers. This limits scalability and reduces learners' ability to construct personal mnemonic links. By grounding mnemonics in objects that learners already recognise, use, and associate with prior experiences, a system could connect new vocabulary to existing mental models rather than requiring learners to adopt designer-defined associations. We outline a proof of concept and a storyboard of a generative AR approach in which learners create personalised 3D mnemonics by transforming familiar objects in their surroundings into situated mnemonic anchors. We position this concept within a timeline of related work and argue that recent advances in generative 3D asset creation enable a new design point: personalised 3D mnemonics that do not merely place content in the physical learning environment, but modify familiar real-world objects so that they become part of the mnemonic itself.

title: Retrieve-then-Disambiguate: Scalable Reviewer Discovery
summary: The growing number of scientific submissions is straining the peer review process, while a large pool of relevant researchers remains unidentified and is therefore not considered as potential reviewers. We formulate the discovery of these researchers as a retrieval problem: given a submission, we retrieve and rank researchers based on domain similarity. We present retrieve-then-disambiguate, an open-source algorithm that identifies domain relevant researchers for a query submission by retrieving similar publications from the scientific literature and resolving ambiguous author names into unique researcher identities. We evaluate the algorithm on 500 astronomy and physics publications. We use ORCID-linked first authors, coauthors, and cited researchers as proxy labels to evaluate the recovery of researchers with known connections to each query publication. When retrieving the top 500 most similar papers, the algorithm recovers roughly 68\% of first authors, 60\% of coauthors, and 45\% of cited researchers. Our code is available at https://github.com/deepthought-initiative/Retrieve-then-Disambiguate.

title: Uniform Non-Deterministic Semantics for Ciuciura's $mbC^n$-Hierarchy
summary: We introduce a uniform non-deterministic semantics for the hierarchy of paraconsistent systems mbC^n introduced by Ciuciura. The proposed construction generalizes Omori's three-valued semantics for mbC^1 to all systems of the hierarchy. We prove soundness and completeness of the semantics with respect to the corresponding axiomatizations and show that the consequence relations of the systems mbC^n cannot be characterized by finite deterministic matrices.

title: Beyond Plausible Prediction: Safety Sufficiency in Web World Models
summary: Web world models increasingly predict the consequences of candidate actions before agents act, yet a plausible predicted future does not necessarily support the correct safety decision. In a matched human evaluation of 3,000 predictions from ten frozen open models, 86.1% are judged semantically plausible. However, several models exhibit highly asymmetric authorisation behaviour, combining low false-safe execution with poor recall of clarifiable ASK cases and a strong preference for BLOCK. This motivates safety sufficiency: whether a predictive interface preserves and exposes the policy-decisive information required to distinguish actions that may be EXECUTED, require clarification through ASK, or should be BLOCKED. We introduce SafeWebWorld, a benchmark for evaluating safety sufficiency across five web-safety domains through action-conditioned futures, policy-decisive evidence, and policy-conditioned decisions. Under a controlled Security-Aligned Supervised Fine-Tuning protocol, evidence preservation can improve substantially while authorisation-sensitive decisions deteriorate. To determine whether this deterioration reflects loss of authorisation-sensitive score structure or a failure of the decision readout, we introduce Latent Authorisation Recovery (LAR). Frozen-score recalibration reveals substantial but backbone-dependent recovery, while paired recovery provides only a modest additional gain. Yet within-family and matched-authorisation evaluations remain poor, showing that aggregate recoverability does not imply robust fine-grained authorisation behaviour. Overall, plausible prediction, evidence preservation, and aggregate recovery are each insufficient on their own to establish robust authorisation.

title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
summary: Across coding, web, and tool-use tasks, language-model agents are now routinely trained with the same recipe: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to learn the interface, then multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) to master it. Code-as-policy (CaP) casts robot manipulation in the same form, as the policy writes code against robot APIs and reads back the results, so the same recipe should apply. Yet existing CaP agents sidestep training: they either prompt closed frontier models or delegate manipulation to pre-trained vision-language-action models (VLAs) and high-level skills, while small open vision-language models (VLMs) fail outright. We present CaPtain, an open post-training pipeline that turns a small open VLM into a capable CaP agent, with no VLA, frontier model, or privileged state at test time. CaPtain trains and deploys the policy inside CaPtain-Harness, which exposes low-level perception, geometry, and guarded-motion primitives across simulation and real hardware. We first align the base model via SFT on synthetic trajectories generated with GPT-6 Astra, then apply multi-turn RL. Multi-turn RL must credit tens of agent requests, whose physical effects often surface turns later, from a single end-of-episode outcome. We therefore introduce a physical critic that reads privileged simulator state, never seen by the policy, and credits each request by how much it changes the predicted chance of success. Starting from Qwen3.5-4B (0% zero-shot), CaPtain-4B reaches 55.4% held-out LIBERO success after SFT and 73.8% after RL. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 78.5%, surpassing several frontier-model agents, and its RL gains persist across three perturbation suites (+17.6 to +21.2 points). Without target-domain training, it attains 83.3% on SimplerEnv WidowX, exceeds frontier models on CaP-Bench, and runs on a real robot after simulation-only adaptation. We release all code, data, and model weights.

title: On Some Logics Intermediate Between S4.2 and S4.3 Defined by the Notion of Independence
summary: Hamkins and Loewe described modal logic S4.2 through the notion of sets of independent buttons - statements that are possibly necessary - and switches - necessarily contingent statements. In this article we investigate logics intermediate between S4.2 and S4.3 that are defined through a different notion of independence. We provide an axiomatic description of such logics, state some basic facts and prove various completeness and decidability results.

title: Drone-PUR: From Visual Clue Discovery to Understanding and Reasoning in UAV Scenes
summary: The reasoning capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) can be limited by incomplete or inaccurate visual observations in the general domain. In unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) scenes, small targets, subtle attributes, and changing viewpoints further complicate perception and understanding. Therefore, we introduce Drone-PUR, a dataset and benchmark organized around visual clue discovery, interpretation, and integration, corresponding to the three capability dimensions of perception, understanding, and reasoning. Reasoning samples are designed to require models to combine multiple visual clues to derive visually grounded conclusions. Its 11 tasks provide 175k training and 20k test samples spanning single images, image sequences, cross-modal images, and multiple viewpoints. All test samples undergo human review. Evaluating 22 general-purpose VLMs reveals persistent limitations in spatial judgment and cross-modal and cross-view reasoning. Across models, stronger perception is associated with better reasoning, while single-task fine-tuning further reveals selective bidirectional transfer between these capabilities. To examine domain adaptation, we develop UAV-PUR from Qwen3-VL through staged fine-tuning with auxiliary supervision. Its 4B and 8B variants improve overall multiple-choice accuracy by 18.33 and 17.52 percentage points over their pretrained counterparts, respectively. The dataset and project resources are available at https://drone-pur.github.io.

title: A Basic Modal Logic for the Abstract Treatment of Quantum Mixed States
summary: Quantum logic has developed in various directions since its inception. However, many existing logical approaches either focus only on pure states, or use Hilbert-space models in which the abstract relationship between pure states, mixed states, and probabilities is not made explicit. In this work, we introduce a model designed to handle quantum mixed states abstractly. Furthermore, we construct a proof system for the proposed logic and establish its completeness with respect to the intended semantics.

title: On the Reconstruction of Orthomodular Logic via Restricted Negation
summary: Orthomodular logic has long been studied as a fundamental logical framework within quantum logic. In addition to its lattice-theoretic foundations, various formulations have been proposed that incorporate specialized implication connectives and more complex logical connectives. In this study, we reconstruct orthomodular logic by introducing a connective referred to as restricted negation, which has received comparatively little attention in the existing literature. We demonstrate that this connective provides a natural and expressive basis for formulating the core principles of orthomodular logic. Furthermore, as a main result, we construct a new proof system for orthomodular logic founded on this connective.

title: On Łukasiewicz Topological Semantics
summary: In this paper, we propose fuzzy topological semantics for Łukasiewicz valued modal logic, based on the standard Łukasiewicz algebra. Within this setting, formulas are interpreted as fuzzy sets of truth values, while the modal operators are realized through fuzzy interior and closure operators. We define a Kripke-induced fuzzy Alexandroff topology and establish a precise correspondence between Łukasiewicz fuzzy Kripke semantics and its topological counterpart. The proposed topological semantics validates the S4 modal axioms that include reflexivity, transitivity, monotonicity, normality, and the necessitation of truth.

title: Merging and Evolution of Data Bases: A Many-Logic Approach
summary: A new approach to information-based logics using many-logic modal structures (MLMSs) was recently proposed by Martins et al. In such a setting, it is possible to have worlds with different underlying logics within the same frame, all anchored to a base lattice that contains the semantics of each logic as a down-complete sublattice. In this paper, we take the lattice L6, defined by the six-valued semantics of the logic of evidence and truth LET + K , as our base lattice. We also consider four-, three-, and two-valued formal systems associated with down-complete sublattices of L6. These logics are capable of representing paracomplete, paraconsistent, and classical contexts with six, four, three, and two informational scenarios, respectively. As applications of MLMSs, we will discuss the merging and temporal evolution of databases whose underlying logics are two-, three-, four-, and six-valued. We will also investigate inconsistency measures in this context.

title: Restricted Peirce's Law and Natural Deduction
summary: The constructive logic JP' is known to be the weakest logic between intuitionistic and minimal logic that satisfies Glivenko's theorem. In spite of this natural and desirable formal property, the motivation for its notion of negation remains rather elusive: it can be characterised by a restriction of Peirce's law or by the double negation of ex falso quodlibet, neither of which is very intuitive. In order to have an alternative perspective on this negation, we study in this paper a couple of  natural deduction systems for JP'. We first present a system that is normalisable and satisfies a restricted form of the subformula property. Then a modification of this system is introduced, whose rules satisfy the separation of connectives and the full subformula property. Afterwards we turn our attention to a typed lambda-calculus, with respect to which our natural deduction enjoys the Curry-Howard correspondence, followed by a concluding discussion.

title: Paraclassical Logics with Two Negations
summary: We study three paraclassical propositional logics with two negations, CLoaN, CLouN, and CLauN, obtained by pairwise combining the one-negation systems CLuN, CLaN, and CLoN.  CLuN's negation  is glut-tolerant and paraconsistent, CLaN's negationis gap-tolerant and paracomplete, and CLoN's negation is both paraconsistent and paracomplete. We provide sound and complete two-valued non-deterministic semantics for each of the two-negations systems. We then focus on CLauN, the system containing the primitive dual pair of CLaN and CLuN negations. In this setting, we show deductive relationships between different negations expressible in CLauN; we show two diferent ways to recapture classical logic by means of translations, locally and globally; and we show a duality results for the multiple conclusion consequence relation of the logic.

title: Normalisation for a Neutral Free Logic with Definite Descriptions
summary: In this paper, we present a natural deduction system for a strong Kleene-based neutral free logic with definite descriptions. The system combines a three-valued propositional basis with free quantification, identity, existence, and rules for definite descriptions. The main result is a normalisation theorem for a proof-theoretically equivalent restricted formulation of the system; we also establish a corresponding modified subformula property for its fragment.

title: Cyclic Nonassociative Bilinear Logic With Additive Constants as Extension of Full Nonassociative Lambek Calculus
summary: Cyclic Linear Logic (CyMALL, CyBL) is a compromise between Commutative Linear Logic (MALL) and Noncommutative Linear Logic (Bilinear Logic, BL). We do not admit commutativity of the tensor, but we still admit only one De Morgan negation. MALL and its variants are natural extensions of Full Lambek Calculus (FL). Abrusci proved that CyBL is not a conservative extension of FL, if we admit additive constants in these logics. In this paper we show that Cyclic Nonassociative Bilinear Logic (CyNBL) with both additive constants is a strongly conservative extension of Full Nonassociative Lambek Calculus with only one additive constant - the upper bound - and that this holds even in the presence of an arbitrary set of nonlogical axioms.

title: Quantifying Linepack Storage Potential of Hydrogen Networks
comments: 23 pages, 6 figures, submitted to the International Journal of Hydrogen Energy
summary: Future hydrogen systems depend on large-scale storage to balance supply and demand. Hydrogen networks can store energy in the pipelines themselves, but the potential of this linepack storage has not been quantified comparably to dedicated storage facilities. We transfer metrics established for conventional storage, such as volume capacity and full-cycle equivalents, to hydrogen networks. To evaluate them, we formulate an optimization problem maximizing linepack storage utilization, subject to non-convex PDE-based constraints describing transient gas flow. We solve the optimization problem over a full-year horizon to capture seasonal variations and to assess the interaction with cavern storage. For computational tractability, we propose a simulation-informed sequential convex programming approach with adaptive time stepping that reduces problem size by up to 98% at accuracy comparable to fixed-resolution methods. For the GasLib-40 topology with German scenario data, the network provides a volume capacity of 24 million normal cubic meters at 28 full-cycle equivalents per year.
comment: 23 pages, 6 figures, submitted to the International Journal of Hydrogen Energy

title: Tight Lower Bounds for Distributional Paging
summary:
Distributional paging seeks a polynomial-time eviction rule that competes with the optimal \emph{online} policy $\mathrm{OPT}$ when requests come from a known stochastic source. Two algorithms by Lund, Phillips, and Reingold [FOCS, 1994] are canonical. Their randomized \emph{dominating distribution} algorithm, for Markov sources, evicts a page drawn from a distribution over the cache satisfying pairwise linear inequalities; their deterministic \emph{median} algorithm, for sources with independent inter-arrival times across pages, evicts the cached page with the largest lower median of its conditional next-request time. Their original guarantees of $4$ and $5$ were recently improved to $2$ and $4$ by Pabbaraju and Vakilian [ICALP 2025].
  We show that neither improved constant can be reduced in its respective source model. For Markov paging, we give two complementary factor-$2$ lower-bound constructions, each with an explicit polynomial-time dominating selector. A directed-cycle family has ratio $2k/(k+1)$, while a recurrent four-page family with cache size three has ratio $2-4\varepsilon/3$.
  For the independent inter-arrival model, we show that the median algorithm is not $c$-competitive for any $c<4$. These are separate results for distinct stochastic models. Matching the known upper bounds, they establish tight competitive ratios of $2$ and $4$, respectively, improving on previous lower bounds of $1.5907$ and $1.511$.

title: On the NP-Hardness of Rank-Metric Minimum Distance and Syndrome Decoding, at Every Rate
comments: A longer version of this manuscript has been submitted for publication
summary: In this work, we investigate the hardness of computing minimum distance, as well as the hardness of syndrome decoding, for rank-metric codes. It is known (Gaborit and Zémor, IEEE TIT 2016) that for $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-linear rank-metric codes of length $N$, minimum distance when $m=O(N)$ and syndrome decoding when $m=O(N^2)$ are NP-hard under randomized reductions. We obtain a derandomization of these results and a bit more. We show that for any fixed small $\varepsilon>0$, for $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-linear rank-metric codes of length $N$ with $m=O(N^{1+\varepsilon})$, the problems of minimum distance, nearest codeword, and syndrome decoding are NP-hard under deterministic reductions. Further, we can prescribe the rate; that is, if we restrict to codes having any fixed rational rate $R\in(0,1)$, then the NP-hardness for all three problems persists. Our main technical contribution is simple, and possibly of independent interest. The reduction of Gaborit and Zémor (IEEE TIT 2016) relies on a distance-preserving embedding of a Hamming-metric code into a rank-metric code, obtained by multiplying its coordinates by a uniformly random vector. We show that we can choose an explicit vector from a slightly larger extension field.
comment: A longer version of this manuscript has been submitted for publication

title: From Teleoperation to Long-Horizon Dexterity: Evaluating Visuomotor Skills and Offline Proxies for Dexterous Manipulation
summary: Imitation learning policies are intended to make robotic manipulation robust to variations in object pose, appearance, and environment that challenge pre-programmed motion. However, real-world performance remains difficult to predict, as conventional optimization signals such as validation loss show no consistent relationship with robot success. To identify the design choices that govern real-world performance, 281 imitation-learning policies spanning seven policy families were evaluated in approximately 1,700 real-robot trials of RJ45 connector grasping and insertion using a five-fingered robotic hand. Controlled ablations showed that observation and action representations dominated conventional optimizer and sampling choices. For point-cloud policies, region-of-interest cropping, representation in the robot-base frame, and normalization within the point encoder each improved success by 70-100 percentage points. For the vision-language-action policy, absolute rather than relative action prediction improved insertion success by up to 70 percentage points. Skill decomposition, multi-view perception, and recovery demonstrations were associated with the strongest-performing systems, although their effects were not independently isolated. Of 67 offline metrics evaluated, only five measures of predicted-motion smoothness and directness reliably correlated with insertion success (r = -0.70 to -0.80), and only within a single policy family. These results identify representation choices as key determinants of real-world imitation-learning performance and show that offline metrics can shortlist policies, but cannot replace real-robot evaluation.

title: Arithmetical Characterizations of Two Intuitionistic Logical Principles
summary: This paper investigates the role of negation in arithmetic by analyzing subsystems based on subminimal logic. We introduce NA^PR, a system of subminimal arithmetic equipped with all primitive recursive functions, and answer the following four questions: (1) Can we develop reasonable arithmetic within NA^PR? (2) Can we characterize logical rules Absorption of Negation (An) and Ex Falso Quodlibet (ECQ) by arithmetical principles? (3) Are there strict differences in deductive power among NA^PR, MA^PR, and HA? (4) Do MA^PR and MA, and NA^PR and NA have a similar mutual interpretability relationship as HA? We show the following: First, Heyting Arithmetic (HA) is shown to be a conservative extension of NA^PR for positive formulas. Based on NA^PR, we prove that (ECQ) is equivalent to the definability of disjunction, and that (An) is equivalent to a variant of the least number principle. Furthermore, using the constant domain neighbourhood semantics, we show that the systems NA^PR, MA^PR (written as NA^PR+(An)) and HA (written as NA^PR+(An)+(ECQ)) form a strictly increasing hierarchy of strength. Finally, we demonstrate the essential role of primitive recursive functions in weak arithmetic using classical countermodels.

title: Tableaux Rules for Theories of Definite Descriptions in Positive Free Logic with Some Philosophical Remarks
summary: While Russell's theory of definite descriptions, expressions of the form 'the F', is almost incontrovertible in classical logic, in free logic matters stand differently. Several alternatives have been proposed. In Lambert's hierarchy, the weakest theory is his minimal free theory of definite descriptions (MFD), which only says that anything is the F iff it is the unique existing F, the strongest one is a chosen object theory in which all improper definite descriptions refer to the same object (FD2). Intermediate is Lambert's FD1, which adds ix(x = t) = t as an axiom to MFD. MFD is very weak. FD2 is very strong. One might hope to find intermediate systems in which ix(x = t) = t is provable from more fundamental principles. The present paper considers one avenue where one might hope to find them and closes it. Two theories, FDA and FDH, will be considered that are motivated by considerations from proof-theoretic semantics. The former turns out to be equivalent to FD2, the latter to have unreasonable consequences. A third theory, similarly motivated, is also not viable. The philosophical upshot of this is briefly discussed.

title: Circumventing the Computational Hardness of Computational Arbitrage
summary: AI model marketplaces host providers with heterogeneous costs and capabilities. These differences create an opportunity for computational arbitrage (Olmedo et al., 2026), in which an intermediary purchases inference from a portfolio of models and resells it to users at a profit. Beyond creating profit opportunities for the arbitrageur, computational arbitrage offers financial value to both consumers and providers and could therefore significantly influence AI model markets. While prior work empirically demonstrates the feasibility of computational arbitrage for small model pools, scaling it to large marketplaces requires arbitrage strategies that are both computationally tractable and inexpensive to identify and deploy. In this work, we formalize computational arbitrage as an allocation problem and prove that it is generally NP-hard. However, we show that the optimal allocation can be computed efficiently under a natural diminishing-returns condition on how model performance scales with inference spending. We further develop a sample-efficient method for estimating model performance from limited data, reducing the upfront cost of identifying arbitrage strategies. Our analysis also yields several economic insights: at the optimum, every funded model delivers the same marginal utility per dollar; arbitrage directs revenue away from providers offering little utility relative to their prices; and it rewards complementary specialization.

title: EgoHSI3R: Online 4D Hand-Scene Interaction Reconstruction from Egocentric Video
summary: Egocentric videos offer an abundant source of hand-scene interactions for embodied learning, which requires recovering hands, camera, and scene consistently in a shared 3D world. Existing methods focus on either camera-frame hands or world-space hand trajectories, without jointly recovering the scene pointmaps or interaction information. Building a complete reconstruction from such specialized predictions therefore typically requires per-sequence optimization. We propose EgoHSI3R, a unified feed-forward framework for online 4D hand-scene interaction reconstruction from egocentric monocular video. To jointly recover these components, it maintains a recurrent scene representation that accumulates geometric evidence over time and provides a shared world space and scale. We introduce hand-centric prompts that fuse pretrained hand priors and local scene context, while MANO vertex queries attend to scene features to predict dense per-vertex contact. These designs enable a single network to jointly estimate camera motion, dense scene geometry, world-space bilateral MANO hands, and per-vertex hand contact. Despite operating causally, EgoHSI3R achieves the lowest world-space hand joint error on ARCTIC among the evaluated methods, while offering faster inference than existing world-space hand reconstruction pipelines and competitive camera and scene reconstruction accuracy.

AI.title_translation: EgoHSI3R：基于第一人称视频的在线4D手部-场景交互重建
AI.tldr: EgoHSI3R是一个统一的前馈框架，用于从第一人称单目视频在线重建4D手部-场景交互，它能同时估计相机运动、场景几何、世界空间中的手部姿态和每顶点接触，并在ARCTIC数据集上实现了最低的世界空间手部关节误差和更快的推理速度。
AI.motivation: 现有方法在手部-场景交互重建方面存在局限性，它们通常只关注相机坐标系下的手部或世界空间中的手部轨迹，未能联合恢复场景点云图或交互信息，并且通常需要针对每个序列进行优化才能获得完整的重建。
AI.method: 本文提出了EgoHSI3R，一个统一的前馈框架，用于从第一人称单目视频进行在线4D手部-场景交互重建。该方法通过维护一个循环场景表示来随时间积累几何证据，提供共享的世界空间和尺度。它引入了以手为中心的提示，融合预训练的手部先验和局部场景上下文，同时MANO顶点查询关注场景特征以预测密集的每顶点接触。这些设计使单个网络能够联合估计相机运动、密集场景几何、世界空间中的双边MANO手部模型以及每顶点手部接触。
AI.result: EgoHSI3R在ARCTIC数据集上取得了最低的世界空间手部关节误差，优于所有评估方法。此外，它比现有的世界空间手部重建管线提供了更快的推理速度，并在相机和场景重建精度方面具有竞争力。
AI.conclusion: EgoHSI3R成功地提供了一个高效且准确的在线4D手部-场景交互重建解决方案，克服了现有方法的局限性，实现了手部、相机和场景在共享3D世界中的一致恢复。
AI.translation: 第一人称视频为具身学习提供了丰富的手部-场景交互来源，这需要在一个共享的3D世界中一致地恢复手部、相机和场景。现有方法侧重于相机坐标系下的手部或世界空间中的手部轨迹，而没有联合恢复场景点云图或交互信息。因此，从这些专业化预测构建完整的重建通常需要针对每个序列进行优化。我们提出了EgoHSI3R，一个统一的前馈框架，用于从第一人称单目视频进行在线4D手部-场景交互重建。为了联合恢复这些组件，它维护了一个循环场景表示，该表示随时间积累几何证据，并提供共享的世界空间和尺度。我们引入了以手为中心的提示，融合了预训练的手部先验和局部场景上下文，同时MANO顶点查询关注场景特征以预测密集的每顶点接触。这些设计使单个网络能够联合估计相机运动、密集场景几何、世界空间中的双边MANO手部模型以及每顶点手部接触。尽管是因果操作，EgoHSI3R在评估方法中在ARCTIC数据集上实现了最低的世界空间手部关节误差，同时提供了比现有世界空间手部重建管线更快的推理速度，并在相机和场景重建精度方面具有竞争力。
AI.summary: EgoHSI3R是一个新颖的统一前馈框架，专为从第一人称单目视频进行在线4D手部-场景交互重建而设计。该方法通过维护循环场景表示来累积几何证据，并利用手部中心提示融合预训练先验和局部场景上下文，同时MANO顶点查询预测密集的每顶点接触。这使得它能够联合估计相机运动、密集场景几何、世界空间中的MANO手部模型以及手部接触。实验结果表明，EgoHSI3R在ARCTIC数据集上实现了最低的世界空间手部关节误差，并提供了比现有方法更快的推理速度和竞争性的重建精度。
AI.keywords: 第一人称视频, 手部-场景交互, 4D重建, 在线, MANO
AI.comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于提出了一个统一的、前馈的在线框架，能够从第一人称视频中同时重建4D手部-场景交互的所有关键组件，包括相机、手部和场景几何，并解决了一致性和效率问题。其循环场景表示和手部中心提示是关键的技术贡献，显著提高了世界空间手部重建的精度和速度，对于具身学习和人机交互领域具有重要意义。

title: How Global Is Anycast?: Evaluating Performance Gaps
summary: Anycast networks aim to reduce latency by directing users to nearby service sites. However, users can still experience high latency even when accessing services via anycast. Some anycast deployments are localized and intended to serve a specific geographic region, while others are globally distributed to support users worldwide, with the expectation of consistently low latency across locations. In practice, latency can remain poor for certain users due to factors such as routing inefficiencies and peering relationships. These inefficiencies are often more pronounced in regions such as Africa, Asia or South America, where Internet connectivity is generally less mature than in North America or Europe. Despite this, there has been no in-depth analysis of anycast performance in these continents. In this paper, we examine the latency experienced by users in these regions when accessing anycast networks. We analyze more than 10,000 anycast prefixes, quantify the severity of latency problems, and show that clients in Africa, Asia, and South America experience substantially higher latency than those in North America. We also investigate the underlying causes of this performance gap.

AI.title_translation: Anycast有多全球化？：评估性能差距
AI.tldr: Anycast网络旨在降低延迟，但非洲、亚洲和南美洲的用户仍面临显著更高的延迟，这主要是由于路由效率低下，且这些区域的性能此前缺乏深入分析。
AI.motivation: Anycast网络旨在通过将用户导向附近的服务站点来降低延迟，但某些用户（尤其是在互联网连接不如北美或欧洲成熟的非洲、亚洲和南美洲地区）仍会经历高延迟。尽管存在这种现象，但这些大陆的Anycast性能尚未得到深入分析，因此本研究旨在填补这一空白，调查这些区域的延迟问题。
AI.method: 本研究检查了非洲、亚洲和南美洲用户在访问Anycast网络时所经历的延迟。论文分析了超过10,000个Anycast前缀，量化了延迟问题的严重性，并调查了造成这种性能差距的根本原因。
AI.result: 研究发现，非洲、亚洲和南美洲的客户端在访问Anycast网络时，其延迟显著高于北美洲的客户端。论文量化了延迟问题的严重性，并揭示了造成这种性能差距的潜在原因。
AI.conclusion: Anycast网络的性能并非在全球范围内一致，非洲、亚洲和南美洲的用户由于路由效率低下和对等关系等因素，在访问Anycast服务时会经历比北美用户更高的延迟。
AI.translation: Anycast网络旨在通过将用户导向附近的服务站点来降低延迟。然而，即使通过Anycast访问服务，用户仍可能经历高延迟。一些Anycast部署是本地化的，旨在服务特定的地理区域，而另一些则是全球分布式，以支持世界各地的用户，并期望在所有位置提供一致的低延迟。实际上，由于路由效率低下和对等关系等因素，某些用户的延迟可能仍然很差。这些效率低下在非洲、亚洲或南美洲等地区通常更为明显，这些地区的互联网连接通常不如北美或欧洲成熟。尽管如此，这些大陆的Anycast性能尚未得到深入分析。本文中，我们检查了这些地区用户在访问Anycast网络时所经历的延迟。我们分析了超过10,000个Anycast前缀，量化了延迟问题的严重性，并表明非洲、亚洲和南美洲的客户端比北美洲的客户端经历显著更高的延迟。我们还调查了造成这种性能差距的根本原因。
AI.summary: 本论文评估了Anycast网络的全球有效性，该网络旨在降低用户延迟。文章关注了在互联网基础设施不成熟地区（特别是非洲、亚洲和南美洲）用户所经历的高延迟这一被忽视的问题。通过分析超过10,000个Anycast前缀，研究量化了显著的延迟差异，揭示了这些大陆的用户面临比北美地区用户差得多的性能，并深入探讨了这些性能差距背后的原因。
AI.keywords: Anycast, 延迟, 性能差距, 全球互联网, 网络效率
AI.comments: 该论文揭示了Anycast网络在全球服务质量方面存在的一个关键差异，对全球相当一部分人口产生了影响。其关注未被充分研究的地区（非洲、亚洲、南美洲）并量化性能差距，为网络运营商和研究人员提供了宝贵的见解，有助于改善全球互联网的公平性和效率。

title: Spatial Atlas-Informed Loss Ensembles for Whole-Body PSMA PET/CT Metastasis Segmentation
summary: Existing whole-body PSMA PET/CT prostate metastasis segmentation methods generally rely on images alone, without explicitly incorporating where metastases tend to occur. We investigate whether a population metastasis atlas can improve lesion detection when integrated into model training. We constructed voxel-wise mean and standard deviation maps from 375 expert-annotated training scans and used them to weight the cross-entropy loss of an nnU-Net. The additional penalties for missed lesions and false positives depend on spatial atlas statistics and diminish as predictions become confidently correct. Seven configurations were compared on validation data; three were combined by majority voting into SAILS (Spatial Atlas-Informed Loss enSemble). We compared SAILS with a baseline nnU-Net and inference-time atlas fusion on AutoPET~III (110 disease-positive cases) and Deep-PSMA (100 external cases). No atlas or registration is needed at inference. Results: On AutoPET~III, SAILS improved whole-body Dice (0.531 vs. 0.520; p=0.006), reduced missed-lesion volume (9.5 vs. 12.1 cc/case; p<0.01), and increased pooled lesion sensitivity (0.857 vs. 0.843; p=0.004). On Deep-PSMA, SAILS detected 126 additional reference lesions (sensitivity 0.769 vs. 0.751; p<0.001), without a significant whole-body Dice change (-0.009; p=0.36). High-risk bone Dice improved in both cohorts (0.576 vs. 0.552 and 0.667 vs. 0.653; both p<0.01). False-positive volume increased by 2.3 and 18.2 cc/case, respectively (p<0.001). Atlas-weighted training improves lesion detection, especially in high-risk bone, without test-time atlas registration, but increases false positives.

AI.title_translation: 基于空间图谱引导的损失集成用于全身PSMA PET/CT转移灶分割
AI.tldr: 该研究提出SAILS方法，将转移灶空间先验图谱融入训练损失函数，在推理无需配准的前提下有效提升了PSMA PET/CT前列腺癌转移灶（特别是骨转移）的检测敏感度。
AI.motivation: 现有的全身PSMA PET/CT前列腺癌转移灶分割方法通常仅依赖图像本身，缺乏对转移常发解剖部位等先验信息的显式引入。
AI.method: 从375例专家标注的训练扫描中构建体素级均值和标准差图谱，利用其对nnU-Net的交叉熵损失进行加权，对漏诊病灶和假阳性的惩罚依赖于空间图谱统计，并在预测趋于高度自信且正确时逐渐衰减；验证集上对比7种配置，将其中3种通过多数投票集成构建SAILS（空间图谱引导的损失集成模型）；该方法在推理时无需任何图谱或配准。
AI.result: 在AutoPET III数据集上，SAILS提高了全身Dice（0.531 vs. 0.520，p=0.006），降低了漏诊体积（9.5 vs. 12.1 cc/例，p<0.01），并提高了总病灶敏感度（0.857 vs. 0.843，p=0.004）；在Deep-PSMA外部数据集上多检出126个参考病灶（敏感度0.769 vs. 0.751，p<0.001），全身Dice无显著差异；两数据集的高危骨转移Dice均有提升（分别提升至0.576与0.667，均p<0.01）；但假阳性体积分别增加了2.3和18.2 cc/例（p<0.001）。
AI.conclusion: 基于图谱加权的训练方法能够在无需测试阶段图谱配准的前提下改善病灶检出能力（尤其是高危骨骼转移），但会导致假阳性有所增加。
AI.translation: 现有的全身PSMA PET/CT前列腺癌转移灶分割方法通常仅依赖图像本身，未显式结合转移灶倾向发生部位的信息。我们探究了将人群转移灶图谱整合进模型训练中是否能够改善病灶检出。我们从375例经专家标注的训练扫描中构建了体素级的均值和标准差图谱，并用其对nnU-Net的交叉熵损失进行加权。对漏诊病灶和假阳性的额外惩罚依赖于空间图谱统计量，并在预测变得可信且正确时逐渐减小。在验证集上对比了7种配置，并将其中3种通过多数投票组合成SAILS（空间图谱引导的损失集成）。我们在AutoPET III（110例阳性病例）和Deep-PSMA（100例外院病例）上对比了SAILS与基线nnU-Net及推理期图谱融合方法。推理阶段无需图谱或配准。结果显示：在AutoPET III上，SAILS提升了全身Dice（0.531 vs. 0.520；p=0.006），减少了漏诊病灶体积（9.5 vs. 12.1 cc/例；p<0.01），并提高了汇总病灶敏感度（0.857 vs. 0.843；p=0.004）。在Deep-PSMA上，SAILS额外检测到126个参考病灶（敏感度0.769 vs. 0.751；p<0.001），且全身Dice无显著变化（-0.009；p=0.36）。在两个队列中，高危骨转移的Dice均获得提升（分别为0.576 vs. 0.552和0.667 vs. 0.653；均p<0.01）。假阳性体积分别增加了2.3和18.2 cc/例（p<0.001）。图谱加权训练能够在无需测试期图谱配准的前提下改善病灶检出（尤其是高危骨转移），但会增加假阳性。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种空间图谱引导的损失函数集成方法（SAILS），用于全身PSMA PET/CT前列腺癌转移灶分割。该方法利用375例标注扫描构建的病灶发生概率图谱加权训练nnU-Net，使模型在推理阶段无需图谱配准。实验证明，该方法能显著提高病灶敏感性并改善高危骨转移检测，但假阳性率略有上升。
AI.keywords: PSMA PET/CT, 转移灶分割, 空间图谱, 损失函数集成, 骨转移
AI.comments: 该研究的创新之处在于将先验的人群转移病灶空间图谱统计量无缝整合到模型训练的损失函数中，避免了推理阶段繁重且容易出错的图谱配准工作；其重要性体现在有效提升了高危骨骼等区域的微小病灶敏感度与检测表现；局限性在于该方法在提高敏感度和减少漏诊的同时，显著增加了假阳性体积。

title: How a group that cannot communicate knows itself by its enemy
comments: 6 pages main text; 35-page SI Appendix included as an ancillary file. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23743441
summary: Teams that cannot communicate seem stuck with what each member sees. We show that their opponent can tell them the rest. Silent hunters, jammed robots and traders who never meet all face an adversary that reacts to the group as a whole; every member can read that reaction, a tell, and learn what no member knows alone. One tell can do the work of a message from every member. The adversary would rather hide, but hiding interferes with its own task, and a team that commits in advance to how it will respond decides how much hiding is worth. A committed team never loses when its opponent cares more about its own goals, and does as well as a fully informed team exactly when the opponent's stake outweighs any gain from lying. Below that point the team learns more by trusting less: in a solved Gaussian model it obtains the truth by promising not to use all of it and keeps the cost the opponent would have paid to conceal; an exact test decides when this holds in finite games. How a team spreads its trust matters too. A lone uninformed member with a full-support prior needs a private coin, but with additive squared-error losses two interchangeable members who respond differently replace it, and a small discount on trust insures against misjudging the enemy. Information, on this view, is not only gathered or aggregated; it is produced by how a team commits to respond.

AI.title_translation: 无法沟通的群体如何通过敌人了解自己
AI.tldr: 本文研究了无法内部沟通的团队如何通过观察其对手的反应来获取集体信息，并指出团队的承诺响应方式可以产生信息。
AI.motivation: 无法沟通的团队受限于每个成员的个体认知，本文旨在展示其对手如何提供关键信息，帮助团队了解自身。
AI.method: 本文采用理论建模方法，包括一个已解决的高斯模型和有限博弈中的精确测试，来分析团队如何从对手的反应中获取信息。
AI.result: 对手的一个“信号”可以起到每个成员传递信息的作用。当对手更关心自身目标时，一个有承诺的团队永不失败，并且当对手的利害关系大于撒谎收益时，其表现与完全知情的团队一样好。在此之下，团队通过更少信任学习更多。在高斯模型中，通过承诺不完全使用信息来获取真相，并保留对手为隐藏信息所支付的成本。团队如何分配信任也很重要。两个可互换且反应不同的成员可以替代一个拥有完全支持先验的单独不知情成员，并且对信任的小幅折价可以防止误判敌人。
AI.conclusion: 信息不仅仅是收集或聚合的；它是通过团队承诺如何响应而产生的。
AI.translation: 无法沟通的团队似乎受限于每个成员所看到的一切。我们展示了它们的对手可以告诉它们其余的信息。沉默的猎人、被干扰的机器人和从未见面的交易员都面临着一个对整个群体做出反应的对手；每个成员都可以读取这种反应，即一个“信号”，并学习到没有任何成员单独知道的信息。一个信号可以完成每个成员发送消息的工作。对手宁愿隐藏，但隐藏会干扰其自身任务，而一个事先承诺如何响应的团队决定了隐藏的价值。当对手更关心自身目标时，一个有承诺的团队永不失败，并且当对手的利害关系大于任何撒谎收益时，其表现与完全知情的团队一样好。低于这个点，团队通过更少信任学习更多：在一个已解决的高斯模型中，它通过承诺不完全使用所有信息来获取真相，并保留对手为隐藏信息所支付的成本；一个精确测试决定了这在有限博弈中何时成立。团队如何分配信任也很重要。一个拥有完全支持先验的单独不知情成员需要一个私人硬币，但对于附加平方误差损失，两个反应不同的可互换成员可以替代它，并且对信任的小幅折价可以防止误判敌人。在这种观点下，信息不仅仅是收集或聚合的；它是由团队承诺如何响应而产生的。
AI.summary: 本文探讨了无法内部沟通的团队如何通过分析其对手的反应来获取集体信息。研究表明，对手为了实现自身目标而产生的“信号”可以揭示团队成员单独无法获取的信息。通过预先承诺其响应策略，团队可以利用对手隐藏信息的成本，甚至在某些情况下表现得与完全知情的团队一样好。文章提出，信息并非仅仅被收集或聚合，而是通过团队的承诺响应方式而“产生”。
AI.keywords: 无法沟通的团队, 对手, 信息生成, 承诺策略, 博弈论
AI.comments: 本文提出了一种新颖的视角，即在缺乏内部沟通的情况下，外部对抗者的反应可以成为团队获取自我认知和集体信息的重要来源。其创新之处在于将对抗性互动视为一种信息生成机制，而非仅仅是信息对抗。这种观点对于理解非中心化系统、博弈论和信息不对称环境下的决策具有重要意义。局限性可能在于其理论模型的普适性，以及在实际复杂情境中如何准确识别和利用“信号”的挑战。

title: Structural Exposure and Subsequent Neighborhood Stability in Temporal Networks: Evidence and Limits of Generalizability
summary: Can temporal path based structural exposure serve as a reliable indicator of subsequent local neighborhood stability across different temporal networks? We investigate this question using the completed observational results from 12 networks spanning face to face nteraction, communication, online activity, and urban mobility. Exposure aggregates source node structural mass along time respecting paths; the outcome is Jaccard neighborhood turnover between later, nonoverlapping windows, with greater turnover indicating lower stability. Six complementary analyses examine the direction and consistency of exposure-turnover associations, proximity to high mass nodes, functional response shapes, distance decay kernels, alternative mass definitions, and temporally ordered changes in source mass. The evidence is heterogeneous rather than uniformly negative or positive. In the primary association analysis, two networks retained positive coefficients after within question false discovery rate adjustment, indicating lower subsequent stability at higher exposure, whereas no negative association survived that adjustment. The pooled proximity coefficient was not distinguishable from zero, and significant mass change associations appeared in opposite directions across networks. More flexible functional, kernel, and mass choices yielded only modest cross validated improvements over simpler comparators; available temporal randomizations also gave model dependent contrasts. The study therefore does not establish structural exposure as a directionally consistent, network independent stability indicator. It also cannot establish a lack of predictive value relative to a no exposure baseline, because that specific comparison and independent cross network validation were unavailable. Incomplete null simulations, unrecorded covariance estimation fallbacks constrain inference.

AI.title_translation: 时序网络中的结构暴露与后续邻居稳定性：泛化性的证据与局限性
AI.tldr: 该论文研究发现，基于时序路径的结构暴露无法作为跨不同时序网络的、方向一致且独立于网络的局部邻居稳定性可靠预测指标，其表现出高度的异质性。
AI.motivation: 探讨基于时序路径的结构暴露是否可以作为跨不同时序网络的后续局部邻居稳定性的可靠指标，并检验其泛化性与局限性。
AI.method: 利用覆盖面对面互动、通信、在线活动和城市移动的12个完整观测时序网络，通过六项互补分析（包括暴露-周转关联的方向和一致性、高质量节点邻近度、函数响应形状、距离衰减核、替代质量定义以及源质量的时序有序变化），系统考察结构暴露与后续邻居周转之间的关系。
AI.result: 证据呈现异质性：在主关联分析中，仅有2个网络在校正后保持正相关（高暴露对应较低稳定性），未发现经校正的负相关；汇聚的邻近度系数与零无异；显著的质量变化关联在不同网络间呈现相反方向；更灵活的函数、核和质量选择仅带来 modest 的改进。
AI.conclusion: 结构暴露不能作为跨时序网络、方向一致且独立于网络的局部邻居稳定性通用指标，其预测表现出高度的异质性和局限性。
AI.translation: 基于时序路径的结构暴露能否作为跨不同时序网络的后续局部邻居稳定性的可靠指标？我们利用涵盖面对面互动、通信、在线活动和城市移动的12个网络的完整观测结果来研究这个问题。暴露沿着遵循时间路径聚合了源节点的结构质量；结果是后来、不重叠窗口之间的雅卡尔（Jaccard）邻居周转率，周转率越大表明稳定性越低。六项互补分析检验了暴露-周转关联的方向和一致性、与高质量节点的邻近度、功能响应形状、距离衰减核、替代质量定义以及源质量的时序有序变化。证据是异质性的，而非完全消极或积极。在主要的关联分析中，经过错误发现率调整后，两个网络保持了正系数，表明在较高暴露下随后的稳定性较低，而没有负相关性在该调整中存活。汇聚的邻近度系数与零没有区别，显著的质量变化关联在不同网络中表现出相反的方向。更灵活的功能、核和质量选择与更简单的比较器相比，仅在交叉验证中带来了适度的改进；可用的时序随机化也给出了依赖于模型的对比。因此，该研究并未将结构暴露确立为方向一致、独立于网络的稳定性指标。相对于无暴露基线，它也不能确定缺乏预测价值，因为该特定比较和独立的跨网络验证不可用。不完整的零模拟、未记录的协方差估计回退限制了推断。
AI.summary: 该论文通过研究12个跨领域的时序网络，评估了基于时序路径的结构暴露作为后续邻居稳定性指标的可靠性。通过六项互补分析，作者发现证据具有高度异质性，未能确立结构暴露是一个方向一致、与网络无关的稳定性通用预测指标。
AI.keywords: 时序网络, 结构暴露, 邻居稳定性, 泛化性, 实证研究
AI.comments: 该论文探讨了时序网络中基于时序路径的结构暴露对后续邻居稳定性的预测能力。创新之处在于利用了12个跨领域的真实时序网络进行大规模实证检验，并进行了多维度的稳健性分析；局限性在于结果呈现高度异质性，未能确立结构暴露作为通用、方向一致的稳定性指标的有效性。

title: The nodally bound-preserving finite element method for the transport equation
summary: Numerical approximations of transport problems, even when stabilised, often violate the bounds respected by the exact solution. Depending on the problem being solved, this can produce non-physical results, such as negative densities or higher-than-unity concentrations. Various bound-preserving numerical methods exist, yet they are usually either conditionally stable or only first-order accurate. In this context, the present work extends the nodally bound-preserving finite element method to the linear transport equation. As a baseline discretisation we use the least-squares finite element method, which is instrumental in achieving unconditional stability for second-order time stepping. It also leads to symmetric algebraic systems, thereby enabling simple, efficient solvers, which we further enhance through Anderson acceleration. Unconditional stability is proved for the backward Euler and Crank--Nicolson discretisations. We also derive error estimates for the fully discrete second-order scheme and provide various numerical examples, including two-phase incompressible flows.

AI.title_translation: 输运方程的节点保界有限元方法
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种用于输运方程的节点保界有限元方法，实现了无条件稳定和二阶精度，避免了非物理结果的产生。
AI.motivation: 现有的保数值输运问题解的边界的方法通常存在条件稳定或仅有一阶精度的局限，容易产生非物理结果（如负密度），因此需要发展一种无条件稳定且高精度的保界数值方法。
AI.method: 采用最小二乘有限元方法作为基准离散化手段，结合后向欧拉和Crank-Nicolson时间步进格式，并利用Anderson加速技术提高求解器效率。
AI.result: 证明了后向欧拉和Crank-Nicolson离散化的无条件稳定性，导出了全离散二阶格式的误差估计，并通过包含两相不可压缩流在内的多个数值算例验证了方法的性能。
AI.conclusion: 本文成功将节点保界有限元方法扩展至线性输运方程，证明了其无条件稳定性，导出了误差估计，并通过数值算例验证了其有效性。
AI.translation: 输运问题数值近似即使在稳定化后，也常常违反精确解所满足的边界条件。根据所求解的问题，这可能会产生非物理结果，例如负密度或大于1的浓度。现有的各种保界数值方法通常要么是条件稳定的，要么仅有一阶精度。在此背景下，本工作将节点保界有限元方法推广到了线性输运方程。作为基准离散化，我们使用了最小二乘有限元方法，这对于实现二阶时间步进的无条件稳定性起到了关键作用。它还导出了对称代数系统，从而实现了简单、高效的求解器，并通过安德森加速（Anderson acceleration）对其进行了进一步增强。证明了后向欧拉和Crank-Nicolson离散化的无条件稳定性。我们还推导了全离散二阶格式的误差估计，并提供了各种数值算例，包括两相不可压缩流。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种针对输运方程的节点保界有限元方法。通过采用最小二乘有限元离散化，该方法实现了无条件稳定性和二阶精度，并能产生对称代数系统以支持高效求解。理论证明和数值算例（包括两相不可压缩流）验证了其有效性和优越性。
AI.keywords: 输运方程, 有限元方法, 保界性, 无条件稳定, 最小二乘法
