title: Beyond Scarcity: When Encoder Adaptation Is Worthwhile
summary: Long-tailed recognition often learns a shared representation before correcting the classifier for class imbalance. Once the classifier has been rebalanced, however, final accuracy does not reveal whether further encoder adaptation remains worthwhile. Standard imbalance benchmarks obscure this question because they jointly vary the number of distinct examples available to rare classes and the frequency with which those examples shape the representation. We introduce a controlled evaluation framework that separates unique support from representation allocation and estimates the incremental value of encoder updates through matched classifier-only and full-network continuations from a common corrected model. The framework combines stage-specific controls, multiple representation and adaptation objectives, whole-distribution metrics, and hierarchical inference over class assignments, support reconstructions, and optimization runs. Across the controlled study, the same low-support regime moves from one in which classifier-only training is adequate to one in which encoder adaptation yields a practically meaningful benefit solely as representation allocation becomes more imbalanced. The transition persists across classifier corrections, representation objectives, normalization and augmentation controls, and ImageNet-scale evaluation, while preserving frequent-class accuracy. Under the prespecified one-percentage-point operating margin, the two regimes are separated by simultaneous confidence bounds. These results show that benchmark construction can alter a post-correction training decision and that support size alone does not characterize the remaining value of representation adaptation.

title: Capability-Conditioned Graph Control Barrier Functions for Zero-Shot Safe Navigation of Heterogeneous Mobile Robot Teams
summary: Multi-robot systems are increasingly deployed as heterogeneous fleets with diverse kinematic and actuation capabilities. While graph control barrier function (GCBF) methods provide a scalable framework for decentralized safe control, existing approaches typically assume homogeneous robot dynamics. Methods that directly encode robot classes can distinguish known types, but do not represent state-dependent motion capabilities or naturally transfer to unseen robot models. To address this challenge, we propose the Capability-Conditioned Heterogeneous Graph Control Barrier Function (CC-HGCBF), defined in a shared second-order reference-point operational space. This formulation provides a common geometric representation of safety across heterogeneous robots while retaining their model-specific dynamics and admissible control constraints. To enable zero-shot transfer, we introduce the Radial Capability Field (RCF), a compact, fixed-dimensional representation of each robot's state-dependent finite-horizon reachable velocity set. Conditioning the shared graph barrier and decentralized policy on the RCF enables them to adapt to changes in robot state, kinematic constraints, and control limits without relying on predefined robot identities. We jointly train the barrier and policy using proactive safety labeling and neural CBF-QP supervision, and evaluate them on mixed teams containing both seen and unseen robot models. Experiments demonstrate scalable safe coordination and zero-shot transfer to robot models and capability variations withheld during training. Physical-robot experiments further demonstrate zero-shot deployment to unseen kinematic models without retraining.

title: Beyond Response Scoring: An AI-aware Cognitive Supervision Framework for Automated Mathematical Short Answer Grading
summary: Transformer-based language models have achieved remarkable success in automated short answer grading (ASAG). However, current methods in ASAG struggle to comprehend, reason about and evaluate complex mathematical answers involving symbols and formulas. These score-only methods fail to generalize across diverse responses and skill states associated with identical scores. Moreover, they ignore the potential upward bias introduced by generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) usage in assessing students' performance and knowledge mastery. To address these limitations, we propose AICG (AI-aware Cognitive-supervised Grading), a two-branch multi-task framework. The first branch combines RoBERTa-based regression, ordinal, and classification heads for individual-answer grading. The second branch uses an expert-designed Q-matrix to associate responses with assessed skills and jointly predicts G-DINA-derived skill mastery and learning gain. Through the shared encoder, these skill-level targets provide cognitive supervision for answer grading beyond score labels. AICG further uses a Gen-AI detector, trained through supervised contrastive pretraining followed by linear classification, to estimate assistance probabilities and convert them into reliability weights, attenuating unreliable cognitive evidence during learning assessment. We conduct experiments on 49,402 instructor-graded responses spanning 19 academic semesters. Relative to RoBERTa regression, AICG reduces mean absolute error (MAE) by 50.3% and improves quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) from 0.798 to 0.927. Ablations identify Q-matrix-guided cognitive supervision as the primary source of improvement, while AI-aware weighting further reduces overall MAE by 4.2% over the unweighted cognitive model and consistently improves MAE and QWK across the four most recent post-Gen-AI semesters.

title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
summary: Robot agents built on vision-language models depend on both the planner and its harness: the tools, feedback, memory, and recovery logic around it. Can improvements to a large teacher's harness be carried into a compact agent with lower inference compute cost? We present TinyAstral, a two-stage approach. We first freeze an open-weight teacher and improve its harness through recursive self-improvement (RSI): frontier LLM agents read the teacher's trajectories and propose harness edits, and each edit is accepted only if it passes a paired statistical test. We then freeze the final harness, collect teacher trajectories with reasoning and failure recovery, and distill a small student that replaces the teacher in the same harness. On RoboTwin, harness evolution raises the teacher's success from 33.4% to 63.6%; the final 4B student reaches 62.8%. Across four harness versions, distilled 4B students score close to their corresponding teachers, and later versions yield stronger students, showing that harness evolution gains carry into compact models. The harness gains also transfer to other frozen planners without retraining. On identical episodes, the final 4B student outperforms open 4B agents, the open 27B harness-RSI model SenseNova-RoboRSI, and our own teacher model placed in three competitors' harnesses. It stays close to its teacher on all three training benchmarks, and on three benchmarks never used for RSI or training it scores close to a 552B planner running the same harness. On the measured deployment episodes, it uses about one fifth of its teacher's accelerator time.

title: A Positional Realizability Theory of Length Generalization in Single-Head Attention
comments: 26 pages, 6 figures. Published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), October 2026. Code available at https://github.com/superajgklasjglaks/positional-realizability
summary: Why does length generalization (LG) depend so sharply on the positional encoding (PE)? Relative schemes extrapolate fixed offsets, absolute schemes fix positions, and neither handles growing offsets. We give a realizability theory for a deliberately controlled abstraction, a single positional-only attention head, that derives this well-documented empirical pattern and says precisely where it holds and breaks. The device is a simulation transfer operator $T_L$ that re-evaluates a selected length-$L_0$-realizing positional kernel on the longer grid, with a scalar $α_L \in [0,1]$ read off before any training from $(Φ, t_n)$ alone. Here $α_L$ serves as the computable witness of that taxonomy's derivation, not as a stronger empirical predictor. Our results are a relative-head deep-row characterization for kernels with a strict unique global maximizer (Theorem 2), an absolute/relative duality that derives the pattern (Proposition 4), a learned-absolute underdetermination result, and a static expressivity bound; a sufficiency theorem (Theorem 1) bridges $α_L$ to LG, and the general deterministic case is a precise open conjecture (correcting a tempting but invalid "outside-colspan" argument). Experiments confirm the structure: in the controlled single-head regime $α_L$ exactly separates the taxonomy's generalizing and non-generalizing (PE, task) cells (2625 trained-model measurements; stable at vocab 64/d=128). Together, these results turn the received PE taxonomy into a positional-kernel transfer theorem, and identify the content and depth mechanisms that escape it. The theory concerns the positional channel alone: tasks whose targets depend on token content, including the standard length-generalization suite such as addition and sorting, fall outside Theorem 2.
comment: 26 pages, 6 figures. Published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), October 2026. Code available at https://github.com/superajgklasjglaks/positional-realizability

title: Control-Layer Interpretation of Reactive Power Recovery Limits in EMT-RMS Model Benchmarking of Inverter-Based Resources
comments: Accepted for presentation at IEEE PES Grid Edge Technologies 2027, April 19-22, 2027, Salt Lake City, Utah, USA.5 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables
summary: EMT--RMS benchmarking is widely used to verify cross-platform consistency of inverter-based resource (IBR) dynamic models. This paper examines a 200 MW anonymized IBR represented in PSCAD and PSS/E. The EMT model separates inverter electrical capability from a plant-level power plant controller (PPC) recovery target, whereas the RMS model represents these functions through REECC and REPCA parameters. Directly assigning the PPC target of $\pm 0.2764$ pu to REPCA hard reactive limits is initialization-inconsistent at the original lagging operating point because the initial reactive command is 0.396273 pu. A second, near-unity-power-factor operating point initializes successfully with the same diagnostic limit, demonstrating that the conflict is operating-point dependent. Using the non-conflicting capability mapping removes the original hard-limit conflict, but the benchmark still shows 18.5--30.2 MVAr post-event POI reactive-power differences from PSCAD. A one-at-a-time REPCA $K_c$ sensitivity under matched benchmark initial conditions further shows that RMS recovery is parameter- and limit-dependent: at $K_c=0.05$ and 0.10 the aggregate machine reactive output reaches the configured capability bounds, while $K_c=0.15$ moves VDOWN, VUP, and HVRT off those bounds and changes their settled POI reactive power by 8.94, 18.00, and 3.17 MVAr, respectively. Machine-to-POI accounting further shows why machine-side saturation need not reproduce the POI-level PPC recovery magnitude. The results distinguish initialization feasibility from recovery equivalence and provide a control-layer diagnostic workflow beyond waveform comparison.

title: Corroborative Learning: Mutual Enhancement through Task-Response Reconstruction
summary: In pattern analysis, models trained independently for the same task often develop complementary capabilities through differences in architecture, data, and optimization. Exploiting complementarity while retaining independent deployment is central to collaborative learning. Most methods establish transfer by reducing differences in predictions, relations, or representations between target and collaborator, although these differences also underlie complementarity. This creates a structural trade-off between reducing differences for knowledge exchange and preserving them for complementarity. We therefore propose Corroborative Learning (CL). Each model forms task-driven responses, with cross-group support from its collaborator. Source-excluded reconstruction of response increments from collaborator representations separates fitting and evaluation across disjoint groups and selectively constrains directions by cross-group reconstructability. The process requires no direct output or feature matching or additional inference dependency. Furthermore, with linear reconstruction and fixed collaborator representations, the loss equals a positive semidefinite directional regularizer, constraining less reconstructable directions more strongly. Signal and noise conditions characterize when directional shrinkage reduces response-estimation error. Across six language tasks, 24 models, and 36 pairs, CL improves over capacity-matched independent adaptation on every task, with positive gains across most directed model combinations. Pairwise comparisons show broad advantages over transfer and mutual-learning methods and different gains from complementarity across collaboration rules. Low-label language and vision results support cross-domain applicability. Task-relevant differences can support mutual enhancement without eliminating disagreement.

title: RTL-Interact: Training EDA-Interactive Models for Multi-Task RTL Design
summary: Large language models offer a promising route to register-transfer-level (RTL) design, but reliable implementations require checking and revision based on electronic design automation (EDA) tools' feedback. Existing RTL-specialized models often lack learned interaction with such EDA tools or rely on separate generation and repair components. We introduce RTL-Interact, a multi-task post-training framework that trains a single RTL-specialized model to generate RTL, construct task-appropriate EDA checks, and revise implementations using tool feedback. The framework combines automatically constructed multi-task demonstrations with staged supervision from chain-of-thought to tool-integrated reasoning. We further introduce Pattern-Aware Policy Optimization (PAPO) for multi-task reinforcement learning. PAPO augments Group Relative Policy Optimization with correctness-gated rewards that favor concise successful checking while rewarding effective revision, and uses task grouping to preserve coverage across objectives. On CVDP, RTL-Interact-32B achieves 48.7% weighted Pass@1 and 68.9% Pass@5, surpassing its teacher model, DeepSeek-V3.2, while RTL-Interact-8B achieves 44.9% weighted Pass@1. Additionally, we show that PAPO can reduce average tool calls by 63.8% while improving Pass@1. Both models also outperform all RTL-specialized baselines on VerilogEval v2 and RTLLM v2, demonstrating the effectiveness of our method.

title: Imputing Missing Data in Longitudinal Life-Logging Athlete Data
summary: Long-term, diverse personal informatics data enables athletes to understand and act on their health and performance goals, whether assessing readiness right now, tracking how soreness relates to training load over time, or predicting how sleep affects next-day performance. However, the inherent missingness in longitudinal data, if handled inappropriately, can bias these analyses. To our knowledge, no prior work has systematically benchmarked classical and deep learning imputation methods on long-term self-tracking data from athlete populations. We evaluate six imputation methods across four missingness mechanisms at missingness rates spanning 10-80%. Using seven diverse long-term self-tracking datasets from 231 individuals, we assess both point accuracy and the preservation of temporal and multivariate structure. Our results show that no single method dominates across all conditions and reveal a critical trade-off: while PAIN is superior on point-wise accuracy, deep learning methods (BRITS, GRU-D, and GRIN) are better at preserving multivariate and temporal structure, particularly under higher missingness. Our findings offer a practical, goal-conditioned framework that guides researchers in selecting imputation strategies aligned with both the underlying missingness mechanism and the specific analytical goal of long-term self-tracking studies.

title: Delta-Seeker: Closed-Loop Generative Search for Novel Circuit Design Discovery
summary: Generative models are increasingly used for circuit synthesis and optimization by proposing topologies, sizing devices, and exploring large design spaces. We investigate whether they can instead support design discovery, where generated structures must depart from known designs while producing reproducible electrical behavior. We propose Delta-Seeker, a closed-loop circuit search framework that combines discrete diffusion for topology generation and mutation with structural checking, SPICE-in-the-loop sizing, Pareto selection, and feedback from prior search outcomes. The search controller uses progress and recurring structural failures to allocate evaluation effort and steer subsequent topology generation, while independent re-sizing and operating-corner analysis are performed only after search. In generator-only experiments, cross-generation feedback increases structurally valid children from 143 to 945 and reduces the faulty-candidate fraction from 0.925 to 0.761. In op-amp topology discovery at matched sizing cost, Delta-Seeker yields 54 designs that remain feasible in at least three of four independent re-sizings and 18 that additionally pass device-level checks and supply-temperature corner analysis, compared with 38 and 10 under fixed control. Removing cross-generation memory reduces independently robust discoveries from 54 to 43 and seven-corner robust discoveries from 40 to 27. In DC-DC converter search, nearest-parent analysis identifies a corpus-absent topology whose generated switching current path changes its nearest training-corpus parent from infeasible at all four operating corners to feasible at all four, while increasing median efficiency from 31.2% to 98.96%. These results show that closed-loop generative search can support circuit discovery beyond structural novelty by identifying new topologies with independently verified changes in circuit operation.

title: Evolution of Financial AI: From Statistical Models to Agentic AI
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) in finance has evolved from statistical learning and machine learning for structured prediction, through deep learning and foundation models for representation learning, language understanding, and reasoning, to retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-grounded reasoning and agentic AI for autonomous planning and execution. In this paper, we examine how researchers and practitioners can select and apply AI methods in finance. We first show that the major paradigms of financial AI address fundamentally different classes of problems, rather than forming a strict hierarchy of capability. We then review the current state of research on AI in finance and trace how these paradigms have reshaped financial data, financial tasks, decision support, and human-AI collaboration. Building on this, we propose practical guidelines for matching AI paradigms to task characteristics, and show that more advanced models, such as foundation models or autonomous agents, are not universally superior. We conclude by outlining open challenges for researchers and practitioners working toward reliable financial AI.

title: Coarse3D: Controllable and Faithful Sparse Structure Generation for Image-to-3D
summary: Coarse-to-fine 3D-native generation relies heavily on the first-stage sparse structure, which determines the global orientation and overall geometry for subsequent refinement. However, existing coarse generators suffer from two key limitations: their orientation is difficult to control due to ambiguous semantic canonicalization, and their structures are often inconsistent with input images due to weak 2D-3D grounding. We propose Coarse3D, a sparse-structure generation model that produces orientation-controllable and structurally faithful voxel geometry from arbitrary unposed images. Coarse3D introduces three designs: a first-frame anchored canonical space that aligns generation with the first input view while preserving object-centric normalization; a dual-tower DiT that couples generation with auxiliary feed-forward reconstruction to learn spatially grounded features; and spatial-prior guided attention that regularizes cross-attention with pixel-to-voxel correspondence. Coarse3D can directly replace the coarse stage of existing pipelines. Experiments show that it substantially improves sparse structure quality and consistently enhances final 3D generation, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: TRIDENT and SHAKTI: A Framework and Benchmark for Hindi AI-Text Detection
summary: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become increasingly multilingual, distinguishing human-written from AI-generated text is essential for maintaining information integrity. However, research remains English-centric, with limited benchmarks for low-resource languages such as Hindi. To address this gap, we introduce SHAKTI, a large-scale Hindi benchmark covering four genres, eight LLM families, multiple prompting strategies, and adversarial transformations. We evaluate its quality through human annotation and analyze linguistic, grammatical, and sentiment-based differences between human- and AI-generated texts. Building on these findings, we propose TRIDENT, a round-trip translation-based detection framework with three variants: TRIDENT-S (static threshold), TRIDENT-D (dynamic threshold), and TRIDENT-C (logistic regression using multi-distance RTT features). TRIDENT leverages semantic consistency between original and round-trip translated texts to identify AI-generated content. Extensive experiments show that TRIDENT outperforms conventional and supervised baselines, with TRIDENT-S achieving the best overall performance. Further evaluations across seven languages, adversarial settings, and unseen LLMs demonstrate its multilingual applicability and robustness, while highlighting sensitivity to the translation model.

title: CONSORT: Uncertainty-Constrained Multi-Robot Planning for Cooperative Localization in GPS-Denied Environments
summary: Centralized multi-agent path planning with cooperative localization in GPS-denied environments is generally computationally intractable when formulated in full belief space due to tightly coupled uncertainty dynamics. Prior work typically approximates belief dynamics or restricts inter-agent coupling. This work examines a multi-agent planning problem in which a primary agent must reach a goal in minimum time subject to a chance-constrained collision-avoidance requirement and a terminal bound on localization uncertainty. We obtain a tractable surrogate of the underlying belief-space problem by optimizing over the mean-state trajectories of all agents and propagating covariance for terminal constraint evaluation only. We propose CONSORT (Cooperative Navigation with Support-Optimized Routing and Trajectories), a discrete-to-continuous pipeline combining hexagonal-grid joint search with spline-based trajectory refinement. Across 50 randomized scenarios, the planners separate as the terminal uncertainty bound tightens, with CONSORT solving 80% of scenarios where the strongest baseline solves 54%, at comparable path length. In marine simulations, with the plans executed under feedback control on an independently developed factor-graph estimate, the trajectories remain collision-free and their terminal uncertainty falls within 6% of the planner's prediction.

title: Experts Exhibit Structured Redundancy: Structure-Preserving Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models
summary: Sparse MoE mechanism significantly improves the trade-off between model capacity and inference efficiency. However, practical deployment still requires storing all experts, resulting in substantial memory overhead. We show that expert outputs in MoE layers exhibit structured redundancy. Across different models and task categories, the stable rank and entropy effective rank of expert outputs are consistently far below the nominal number of experts, while expert output distributions also exhibit fewer effective modes. Motivated by these observations, we reformulate expert pruning as a structure-preserving expert subset selection problem and efficiently optimize it via a greedy strategy, rather than only independently scoring and ranking individual experts or exhaustively searching over expert combinations. We propose two expert pruning methods under the unified structure-preserving framework: Projection Energy Expert Pruning (PEEP), which preserves the functional subspace by maximizing weighted projection energy, and Distributional Coverage Expert Pruning (DCEP), which preserves the distributional geometry by minimizing weighted coverage error. Both methods incorporate router-derived weights as priors, enabling them to jointly preserve the global structural relationships among experts while accounting for the local importance of individual experts. Experiments on DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen3-30B-A3B demonstrate that, at the expert retention ratios of 75% and 50%, our methods outperform the state-of-the-art baselines on the majority of benchmarks and consistently achieve the best average performance across both general tasks and mathematical reasoning tasks.

title: Frequency-Calibrated Decision-Focused Learning for BESS Dispatch Under Renewable Uncertainty
summary: Battery energy storage system (BESS) flexibility depends on state of charge and intertemporal operating constraints. Renewable forecast errors of similar magnitudes can lead to different BESS dispatch results. An error may alter early charging or discharging decisions and reduce the flexibility available for subsequent regulation, while another may have little effect on the resulting schedule. To account for these unequal consequences, this paper proposes Frequency-Calibrated Decision-Focused Learning (FC-DFL), which trains renewable predictors using the realized operating costs of their induced BESS schedules. Gaussian smoothing and solver-based zeroth-order estimation provide training feedback without requiring differentiating through the non-differentiable mixed-integer BESS dispatch problem. The same decision feedback is further combined with prediction sensitivity to develop a decision-oriented XAI method that identifies the input features and forecast periods most consequential to BESS operation. Case studies using German wind and solar data show that FC-DFL reduces the integrated absolute frequency-deviation metric by 6.05% and decision regret by 23.92% relative to accuracy-based predict-then-optimize method. The XAI analysis further demonstrates that the identified high-impact forecast periods produce 2.84 times larger average absolute changes in realized operating cost than low-impact periods. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating downstream decision-making outcomes into renewable forecasting and demonstrate the value of FC-DFL in improving BESS regulation and providing operationally meaningful forecast explanations.

title: Generative SDEs with Trainable Diffusion and Density-Based Losses
summary: We develop a divergence-kernel method for jointly optimizing neural SDE drift and diffusion fields and the initial Gaussian distribution, using losses that depend directly on the terminal density. In two- and eight-dimensional Gaussian-mixture experiments, we learn time-independent fields and obtain far fewer off-mode samples than score-based generators with similar parameter counts. The drift attracts samples toward the modes, while the diffusion helps disperse excess probability between them.

title: A Unified Framework for Probability Estimation of Data-Dependent Events
summary:
We study the general problem of estimating $D(\dde(S))$, the probability that an unknown distribution $D$ assigns to an event determined by a sample $S$ of $n$ i.i.d.\ draws from $D$ through a known mapping $\dde$. The estimation algorithm knows $\dde$ and $S$ but does not have access to any additional samples from $D$. This formulation captures classical missing mass, the data-dependent targets of adaptive data analysis and post-selection inference, and the test error of a data-trained predictor, whose estimation was recently studied by \new{Gastpar et al.\ (2024a,b)}. Within this framework we examine the two classical approaches to estimation. The error of the empirical plug-in estimator is exactly a generalization gap, so generalization bounds transfer to it directly. The leave-one-out estimator, which recovers the Good--Turing estimator, is accurate for every mapping that is stable under the deletion of one sample point, including new structured examples such as neighborhoods of the sample and pierced sets.
  The main application of our framework is to error estimation for a predictor that combines a base classifier with memorized exceptions, a structure common in theory and in practice. For it, the test error is exactly the missing mass restricted to the error region of the base classifier, a region selected by the same sample. We formulate the general problem of \emph{adaptive missing mass estimation} to address such dependence and propose a natural hybrid estimator, the Good--Turing estimator restricted to the selected region. We show that the generalization of the base classifier alone does not guarantee the accuracy of this estimator, and derive two bounds on its error: the first one based on the VC dimension of possible error regions and another based on the mutual information of the selected region with the sample.

title: MEMIG: Self-evolving Memory Construction for Antibody Optimization
summary: Memory has become central to self-evolving LLM agents, which store and retrieve experience from past rollouts to guide future decisions. Existing systems represent this experience as free-form natural language and maintain it by rewriting, which fits tasks whose experience is narratable. However, in scientific discovery and optimization, experience is often a quantity measured by an oracle under a specific context. Rewriting it as text leaves no index for where a record should be, replaces a measurement with a description, and cannot express how interventions interact. To address this, we argue that agent memory for biomolecule optimization should instead be indexable, quantitative, and structured, and we introduce MEMIG. This memory construction framework realizes these three properties. In detail, MEMIG addresses each insight with a domain-grounded identifier and accumulates the quantitative effect measured by a property oracle, so that updates remain local and retrieval becomes an exact lookup. Next, MEMIG connects insights whose interventions are applied together and measures their epistasis by decomposing each evaluated set. Our results show that MEMIG improves performance in most settings across in silico antibody optimization tasks.

title: Equation informed time reparametrization for physics informed neural networks
summary: Physics Informed Neural Networks offer a mesh-free approach to solving differential equations, but their application to time-dependent problems remains challenging, particularly when the governing dynamics involve widely different time scales. With collocation points spread uniformly in time, short intervals of rapid change are under resolved. This work introduces an equation informed time reparameterization framework that modifies the temporal coordinate used during PINN training based on the local dynamics of the governing equation. The proposed method follows a two stage procedure. First, a pilot PINN training provides an approximate solution, which is used to linearize the governing differential operator and estimate its local response to small perturbations. These responses are combined into a time-dependent rate function, large where the dynamics are fast, that defines a strictly increasing transformation from physical time to a new computational time coordinate. A second PINN is then trained on the transformed governing equation, with uniformly sampled collocation points in the new coordinate producing a nonuniform distribution in physical time. Different combination rules and spatial reduction strategies are considered. With the cost of the pilot training included, the method reduces the error by a factor of 4 to 29 relative to the best alternative method on the Kachanov Rabotnov creep-damage model near rupture, and by a factor of 5 to 16 relative to every alternative method on the Frank-Kamenetskii equation near blow up.

title: Multi-Timescale Deliverability of Shared Hybrid Storage for AI Data Center Campuses
summary: Artificial intelligence data center (AIDC) campuses contain sustained power variations and subsecond power fluctuations, requiring both sufficient stored energy and fast response. A shared hybrid energy storage system (HESS) can mitigate aggregate AIDC power deviations, but interval-based schedules cannot capture the delay between commanded and delivered power at the campus point of common coupling (PCC). To this end, this paper proposes a multi-timescale scheduling model for mitigating AIDC power fluctuations with the shared HESS. First, it models electrical pooling at the campus bus and constrains the shared HESS to a single PCC injection. Second, a two-layer model passes five-minute scheduled power, energy state, and reserve capacity to a causal fast response model that distinguishes commanded power from delivered power. Case studies using the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) GenAI Power Profiles Dataset show reductions in both PCC and fast integral absolute error (IAE), while retaining most of the improvement available under ideal response.

title: A Good-Vorticity Low-Regularity Integrator for the Inviscid Oldroyd--B System with Stress Diffusion
summary: We establish sharp convergence results for a sequential semi-implicit good-vorticity integrator for the two-dimensional inviscid Oldroyd--B system with stress diffusion on the torus. For exact solutions satisfying $u\in C_tB^{1+α}_{\infty,1}$ and $τ\in C_tB^α_{\infty,1}\cap L^1_tB^{2+α}_{\infty,1}$, $0\leα\le2$, we prove convergence in the critical norms $B^1_{\infty,1}\times B^0_{\infty,1}$, uniformly over the time nodes on every finite interval where these regularity assumptions hold, including the critical endpoint $α=0$. For $0<α\le2$, we obtain the rate $O(h^{α/2})$ without any additional time Hölder assumption, reaching first order at $α=2$. These algebraic exponents are optimal for this Eulerian scheme over the stated solution classes, as shown by fixed-data lower bounds in the case $a=b=0$ with nonzero velocity mean. For a fixed shear solution at critical regularity, we establish matching logarithmic upper and lower bounds on the numerical error, ruling out every positive algebraic convergence rate. We also prove that the gain of one stress derivative at the time nodes is optimal when the velocity is controlled in $B^1_{\infty,1}$, even for smooth initial stress.

title: POST-MIMO: Partition-Oriented Semantic Transmission for MIMO Point Cloud Delivery
comments: 6 pages, 6 figures, 1 table. Accepted for IEEE GLOBECOM 2026
summary: Point clouds have become a fundamental data format for emerging three dimensional (3D) applications, while their wireless delivery remains challenging due to the large data volume and irregular geometric structure. Existing semantic point cloud transmission methods are mainly developed for single-input single-output systems, making them difficult to apply directly to multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. To address this issue, we propose a partition-oriented semantic transmission framework for MIMO (POST-MIMO) point cloud delivery. POST-MIMO partitions the input point cloud into spatially coherent blocks and aligns them with parallel MIMO streams. Based on this block-aligned representation, the transmitter employs a hierarchical encoder to capture both intra-block local geometry and inter-block global dependency, while the auxiliary side information is transmitted jointly to assist reconstruction. At the receiver, a progressive decoder reconstructs the block geometry in a progressive manner and restores the final point cloud with block-aware adjustment. Experiments demonstrate improved reconstruction quality and lower computational resource consumption than representative reference schemes under the considered MIMO setting.
comment: 6 pages, 6 figures, 1 table. Accepted for IEEE GLOBECOM 2026

title: Hawkeye: Reading Illegible Text with Vision Language Models
summary: While modern Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have been remarkably successful in general scene text recognition, they consistently struggle with the long-tail distribution of text that is degraded by motion blur or low resolution. These limitations are particularly apparent in egocentric applications like smart glasses, where text is often captured in noisy environments. In this paper, we introduce the \textbf{BSTRB} (Blurry Scene Text Recognition Benchmark), a novel benchmark of 8,398 noisy image samples with high-fidelity annotations derived from 1,699 real-world video sequences. To support this, we present \textbf{Hawkeye}, a VLM fine-tuned on BSTRB to read and reason about illegible text by leveraging contextual priors and pixel-level alignment. Our results show that \name matches much larger VLMs on BSTRB overall and exceeds them on text at or below 20 pixels, in a single pass suited to real-time deployment. We characterize the resolution at which current VLMs begin to fail.

title: ReVEAL: Eliciting Role-Aware Latent Visual Evidence from MLLMs for Reasoning Video Object Segmentation
summary: Reasoning video object segmentation (ReVOS) requires segmenting the target specified by an implicit query throughout a video. Existing MLLM-based methods typically require costly cross-model alignment, tying MLLM training to a downstream segmentation model. We present ReVEAL, a decoupled thinking-with-video framework for ReVOS that elicits role-aware latent visual evidence from MLLM reasoning to directly guide segmentation. ReVEAL introduces Visual Evidence Tokens (VETs) into video reasoning to associate necessary visual regions or entities with target, background, or distractor roles, while a Dynamic Attention Layer Router adaptively aggregates VET-to-video attention across layers into role-specific grounding evidence. We train the MLLM to perform VET-augmented reasoning on our constructed ReVEAL-47K dataset, with a Contrastive Attention Grounding Loss as auxiliary supervision to apply role-specific constraints to VET attention and optimize layer routing for reliable latent grounding. At inference, ReVEAL identifies the target through this thinking-with-video process and fuses the resulting role-specific evidence to guide a frozen SAM2 in predicting target masks. Experiments on five benchmarks show that ReVEAL outperforms alignment-free baselines and remains competitive with alignment-based methods.

title: SketchDirector: Complex Scene Sketching via Agentic Layout Reasoning and Detail Refinement
summary: Existing sketch generation methods often rely on image guidance and are largely limited to individual objects or simplified scenes, leaving text-guided complex scene sketching underexplored. We present SketchDirector, an agentic framework that mimics the human sketching workflow for automatic multi-concept scene sketching. Given a scene-level text prompt, SketchDirector first employs a large language model~(LLM) to decompose the scene into multiple draft assets, where each is represented by a set of Bézier curves. Then, an agentic reasoning loop iteratively plans and executes their spatial arrangement, guided by self-evolving memory. Finally, a detail refinement module leverages diffusion priors to enhance sketch quality while preserving geometric structure. To support future research and applications in multi-concept scene sketch generation, we further introduce the \textit{MCSketch8K} dataset, comprising editable vector assets, compositional layouts, and object-level manipulation annotations. Extensive experiments show that SketchDirector outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in semantic and compositional quality while effectively preserving overall contour organization during refinement. The project page is: \href{https://yiki77.github.io/SketchDirector/}{https://yiki77.github.io/SketchDirector/}.

title: Yesterday's Code, Today's Dependencies: How Dependency Selection Shapes PHP Migration Benchmarks
summary:
Migration benchmarks need projects whose tests pass before migration begins. Yet an old project can behave differently without any change to its code. Reinstalling it today may introduce newer libraries, changing both its initial test results and the failures observed during migration.
  We investigate this effect in PHP 7.4-to-8.3 migration. Using unchanged project source and saved package records, we compare two dependency policies. Modern selection allows all versions in the snapshot, while release-date selection allows only versions published by the project's release date. With Composer 2 fixed, release-date selection improves the PHP 7.4 pass rate by 7.1 pp across 3,660 releases. A separate comparison against committed locks shows that it also recovers recorded dependency versions more closely than modern selection.
  The choice matters after migration as well. Among projects that pass on PHP 7.4 under both policies, PHP 8.3 test outcomes differ in 15.0% of eligible pairs. We use a shared test runner and bypass Composer's platform check to isolate test behavior. The resulting candidate migration task sets overlap by only 58.5%. Most differences arise in Laravel projects, where older dependencies trigger deprecations that newer versions avoid. Targeted interventions show that removing these initial failures can restore passing tests or expose further incompatibilities.
  Thus, dependency selection changes not just whether an old project passes, but also which migration failures a benchmark can observe. Preserved locks provide the strongest available version reference; without them, release-date selection offers a historically grounded alternative. Migration benchmarks should make this choice explicit and report its effect on their results.

title: Rome Wasn't Built in One Turn: Replay-Grounded Reward Signals for Long-Horizon Freeciv Agents
summary: Training language-model agents to play long-horizon strategy games is hard because deterministic feedback is sparse and often arrives only at the end of a game. In-game scores can offer dense signals, but they do not reliably predict future outcomes: in 8-68% of position pairs across eight strategy games, the higher-scoring position leads to the worse outcome. We term this phenomenon scoreboard traps. In Freeciv, an open-source turn-based empire-building game where several players manage units, cities, and diplomacy over hundreds of turns, we look into better reward signals for gameplay agents. To facilitate this, we build CivHarness, an open system that saves current game states, branches on different decisions, and replays the game to future turns to provide measurable long-horizon feedback from saved positions. We use CivHarness to train CivTelescope, an LLM Judge that predicts which one of two game positions will yield the better outcome. On scoreboard-trap pairs, CivTelescope is 1.3-2.0 times more accurate than off-the-shelf language models, and it generalizes to new game starts, later turns, and unseen rules. We then train a Freeciv gameplay agent with CivTelescope as a dense reward, and call this recipe CivMarshmallow. When used in the middle stage of the game where scoreboard traps are common, CivMarshmallow reaches an average training phase gain of 8.94 points, 77% more than the best baseline, the end-of-game reward. Over the full 120-turn game, CivMarshmallow uses a hybrid reward that starts from the scoreboard or the end-of-game reward and shifts to CivTelescope as the game advances; this hybrid reward scores highest among the rewards we compare.

title: Input-dependent Neuromodulation Enhances Mixed-Signal Neuromorphic Hardware
comments: 5 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to IEEE ISCAS 2027
summary: Gating mechanisms allow a fixed neural network to adapt its computation to the current input by dynamically modulating its effective parameters. In the brain, neuromodulation uses this principle to move neural circuits between dynamical regimes, and deep learning exploits input-dependent gating, e.g., in gated recurrent networks and self-attention. Input-dependent modulation has also recently been shown to improve spiking neural networks, with particularly strong benefits in small, parameter-limited ones. This makes neuromodulation especially promising for neuromorphic processors at the edge, where area, memory and energy budgets constrain network size, while circuit physics limits parameter precision. Here we demonstrate input-dependent, within-trial neuromodulation of a spiking recurrent neural network on a mixed-signal neuromorphic processor. An off-chip modulator reads the on-chip network's input and activity and adjusts its population-level gains while the chip's analog circuits compute with the physics of the silicon. Neuromodulation raises binary spoken-digit classification accuracy by $+17.3 \pm 10.4$ percentage points, tested across five hardware network instantiations.
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to IEEE ISCAS 2027

title: From 1D Benchmarks to Complex 3D Geometries: Can Agents Reliably Specify Problems for Automated PDE Simulation?
summary: Turning an engineering request into a simulation requires consistent geometry, physics, boundary conditions, and numerical settings. Recent agent-assisted systems automate simulation setup, but successful execution alone does not establish whether the specification preserves the intended problem or correctly handles missing information. We study whether agents can reliably construct complete executable JSON specifications for automated geometry creation, meshing, PDE solving, and result export. Our workflow combines model extraction with deterministic scientific and capability checks, explicit clarification, and validated local patches that preserve unrelated accepted fields. We evaluate specification correctness, execution completion, and numerical verification separately. On 120 template-related requests, the full workflow achieves 98.3% correct first-turn specification and decision outcomes, compared with 92.5% for schema-assisted single shot and 82.5% for model-only: gains of 5.8 and 15.8 percentage points, respectively. It makes no false-ready decisions among the 42 requests requiring clarification or rejection. Component ablations identify contributions from scientific checks and conditional repair. Separate downstream studies cover 1D, 2D, and 3D steady and unsteady, linear and nonlinear problems, including flow and elasticity with complex three-dimensional wing geometries. A 30-case gallery demonstrates automated execution from retained JSON specifications, while 9 of 12 selected live user-to-results tests achieve joint specification, execution, export, and numerical-reference success (75.0%). These results support traceable, engineer-reviewed simulation assistance within the tested scope, while fresh-response regressions identify consistency as a priority for further improvement.

title: ANGLER: Verifier-Grounded Benchmarking with an Adaptive Attacker for Web Agents
summary: Web agents are increasingly deployed to complete tasks autonomously on real websites, where adversarially injected content can induce them to perform unauthorized actions. Existing evaluations primarily use fixed attacks or focus on a single attack type, and evaluate attacks at the text level rather than through real state changes, thus underestimating how vulnerable agents are to diverse attacks. To address the gap, we introduce REEF, a benchmark of red-teaming executable environments with faithful verification for measuring the security vulnerabilities of web agents. REEF covers 9 verifier-grounded websites spanning travel, commerce, productivity, media, and communication, and pairs every authentic benign task with a malicious objective delivered through 5 attack types at both the user and the environment level. REEF's state-based verifiers provide the execution feedback that drives ANGLER, an adaptive near-miss-guided lure evolution framework for red-teaming. Rather than evaluating a fixed attack set, ANGLER uses outcomes from prior rollouts to guide LLM-based attack mutation and candidate selection, prioritizing near-miss seeds during refinement. Across 8 VLM-based web agents, ANGLER achieves an end-to-end attack success rate (ASR) of 20.36%, compared with 15.24% for the non-adaptive setting. Compared with attack-free execution on the same benign tasks, attacks generated by ANGLER reduce benign task success rate (BSR) from 61.9% to 44.4%.

title: SPT-Flow: One Integration, Many Futures in Continuous-Time World Models
summary: Continuous-time world models generate a latent trajectory through a single ODE integration, but adding stochastic conditioning does not ensure that the model uses it. In our teacher-forced baseline, posterior means vary by only about 1% of the prior scale, and matched and swapped latents yield indistinguishable reconstruction PSNR at the reported precision. We study a supervision-shortcut hypothesis: ground-truth intermediate states can reduce the need for trajectory-associated latent information. We introduce SPT-Flow, which samples one latent per trajectory and matches a free-running ODE rollout to demonstration states at multiple readout times. Re-anchoring experiments support the proposed mechanism. On LIBERO, with both models trained for 30k optimizer steps, SPT-Flow improves best-of-10 PSNR over our retrained ODEWorld baseline by 2.0 and 2.4 dB at the mid-trajectory and final frames and reduces mean LPIPS by 23%, with comparable per-sample inference cost. The rollout control recovers most of the accuracy gain; learned latent conditioning adds diversity and best-of-K gains while reducing mean sample accuracy relative to this control. The diagnostics support trajectory-associated latent utilization; semantic mode coverage under matched conditions in the robotic setting remains unverified.

title: TRACE: Target-State Risk-Aligned Conditional Execution for Embodied Tracking
summary: Embodied visual tracking requires a robot to follow a language-specified person under occlusion, look-alike distractors, and ambiguous instructions. We show that improving tracking persistence can simultaneously increase safety violations. Using a compact 0.6B vision-language-action (VLA) tracker with a frozen backbone, we update only the planner head with proximal policy optimization (PPO). PPO improves success and following rates across all three EVT-Bench settings, but increases the collision rate on distracted tracking because episodes that previously ended in target loss can instead end in contact. We introduce TRACE, an execution-time target-state risk gate that preserves the learned policy and intervenes selectively. A lightweight risk head processes 84 cues, including candidate boxes, identity margins, a learned range-and-bearing probe, and the policy's commands. When the calibrated risk exceeds a threshold, TRACE rescales the translational component of the next waypoint while leaving yaw unchanged. The executed action is identical to PPO's on more than 98% of steps. In paired evaluations on identical episodes, TRACE reduces the distracted-tracking collision rate by 3.96 percentage points, while further improving success and following rates. Matched slowdown controls without target-state timing do not reproduce this improvement. Concurrent evaluation reproduces a collision reduction of 3.77 points, compared with 0.29 points for identical-arm null pairs, indicating that the effect exceeds evaluation variability. These results show that target-state-aware execution can recover the safety cost of policy post-training with minimal intervention.

title: Architectural Debt Enforcement under Incomplete Observation: A Controlled Study of Ratchets and Evidence Qualification
summary: Architectural debt gates must distinguish an allowed change from an incompletely observed one. We study a decision contract separating observation qualification, prohibited relation identity, inherited debt and authorized baseline updates. Across 240 fixed files from four repositories, the current observer and programmatic reference jointly qualify 166 files (69.17%), all with exact reference-relative edge agreement; 74 remain reference-UNKNOWN. Coverage varies from 13/60 to 59/60 by repository. On 480 constructed state scenarios sharing 60 source anchors, both the candidate ratchet and mature dependency-cruiser baseline match every expected outcome, whereas static and count-only baselines match 420 and 360. These results do not establish candidate superiority. Preserved failures include nine additional false-PASS probes and 120 unqualified full-tree timing attempts. A subsequent generic binding layer rejects 54 specified mismatches, accepts 54 current controls and permits legal repetition. Two bounded package scopes support 40 scenarios and 48 fresh-process functional checks; their costs remain tied to the measured implementations. Diagnostics explain residual uncertainty through type/runtime relations, installation context and generated-artifact provenance. TypeScript 5.9.3 and 6.0.2 yield identical outputs on ten paired emission witnesses, but neither that agreement nor verified release provenance changes the frozen UNKNOWN labels. The contribution is a controlled account of evidence-qualified enforcement and its limits, not language completeness, natural maintenance effectiveness or a new shrinking-baseline algorithm.

title: AuditFL: A Contract-Backed Clearing Layer for Open Federated Learning
comments: 9 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication at the 4th International Conference on Federated Learning Technologies and Applications (FLTA 2026). The final version will appear in the conference proceedings published by IEEE
summary: Federated learning (FL) keeps raw data local, but most deployments still rely on a trusted coordinator for client admission, checkpoint distribution, update collection, aggregation, and rewards. This paper presents AuditFL, a contract-backed clearing layer for auditable FL in open settings. AuditFL keeps training and aggregation off chain, stores model artifacts in an assumed reliable off-chain artifact store, and records only content identifiers and economic state on chain. Clients reserve update tickets with deposits, publish update identifiers, and later claim refunds or rewards; the task coordinator publishes global checkpoints and finalizes rounds through deterministic settlement rules. The design does not remove the aggregator, but makes its on-chain round decisions attributable, replayable, auditable, and economically constrained. We implement AuditFL as both a deterministic state-machine prototype and a Solidity contract on a local Ethereum-compatible Anvil chain. On full MNIST with Dirichlet non-IID splits, 12 rounds, and up to 200 clients, AuditFL preserves the Plain FL learning trajectory while its overhead follows closed-form control-plane models. At 200 clients, the contract run issues 5,026 transactions, stores 2,413 off-chain artifacts (144.9 MiB), and consumes 829.7M EVM gas, dominated by per-client reserve and publish calls. Controlled dropout, invalid-update, and artifact-unavailability stress tests reduce inclusion nearly linearly but still finalize rounds, with final-accuracy changes remaining within a few tenths of an accuracy percentage point even under high injected failure rates.
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication at the 4th International Conference on Federated Learning Technologies and Applications (FLTA 2026). The final version will appear in the conference proceedings published by IEEE

title: SciGraphSelect: Auditable Scientific Data Selection through Knowledge--Reasoning Graphs
comments: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Workshop: AI4Science
summary: Scientific data selection is typically driven by relevance or utility scores, providing limited insight into why a document is retained. We introduce SciGraphSelect, a reference-grounded framework for auditable scientific data selection. SciGraphSelect organizes domain-specific knowledge, reusable reasoning operations, and reference-attested relations into a typed knowledge--reasoning graph, then scores candidate documents using concept coverage, relation and path co-support, and directional alignment. To avoid over-interpreting document embeddings, rich relational structure is preserved on the reference side while candidate-side evidence is treated conservatively without assuming relation entailment. By exposing the reference-grounded evidence behind each selection, SciGraphSelect brings traceability to the upstream construction of scientific training corpora and complements downstream scientific verification.
comment: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Workshop: AI4Science

title: PsyInterviewee: Informational Invariance and Relational Adaptivity in Mental Health Interview Simulation
summary: LLM-based simulated interviewees support interviewer training and the evaluation of mental health interviewing systems. Existing studies have primarily focused on improving human-likeness through richer patient profiles and behavioral modeling. However, human-likeness alone does not establish their reliability. Reliable simulation requires preserving profile-grounded clinical facts (informational invariance) while adapting disclosure and interaction behavior to the interview (relational adaptivity). To this end, we introduce PsyInterviewee, which separates a protected truth channel from a dynamic interaction channel and verifies generated clinical claims against the profile. Specifically, asymmetric write permissions allow dialogue context to update disclosure and behavioral states without authorizing new clinical facts; these states guide what profile-supported information is revealed and how it is expressed. In an automated evaluation of interactions between LLM-based interviewers and interviewees, PsyInterviewee achieves higher scores than four representative baselines on most metrics across both axes, as assessed by two LLM judges. Ablations suggest that the two channels contribute to clinical grounding and response modulation, respectively.

title: SAT-ACT: Learning CDCL Branching from Outcome-Derived Action Preferences
summary: Learning-based approaches have increasingly been explored for SAT solving, with particular attention to improving branching decisions in conflict-driven clause learning (CDCL) solvers. These approaches derive branching guidance either from static structural properties of SAT formulas or from dynamic signals obtained through solver feedback and execution traces. However, these forms of supervision provide limited evidence about state-dependent branching effects, while different outcome measures may favor different branching choices. To address these limitations, we propose SAT-ACT, an outcome-derived learning framework for CDCL branching. We design three complementary outcome comparison criteria to extract action preferences from independent branching action rollouts initiated at the same solver state. The criteria identify preferences supported by the outcomes and leave comparisons unresolved when the evidence is insufficient or conflicting, instead of forcing an ordering using a predefined scalar metric. A state-conditioned network learns branching priorities from the extracted preferences and uses them to guide CDCL search directly without online action rollouts. We further introduce non-dominated heuristic action supervision, which retains the solver-selected action as a training target only when it remains non-dominated under these preferences. Solver-level experiments show that SAT-ACT consistently reduces CDCL search costs on three SAT families and improves PAR-2 on the SAT Competition benchmarks.

title: In-Model Context Compression with Agentic Soft Tokens for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: Long-horizon LLM agents play an important role in solving complex and sustained tasks, with ever-growing interaction contexts. However, these accumulated contexts will raise substantial computational cost and obscure key decision-relevant evidence. Existing methods typically train external compressors or context-management agents to rewrite context as shorter hard-token sequences, but such external selection may not align with the LLM's evolving representation and is necessarily lossy. In this paper, we introduce Agentic Soft-Token Compression (ASTC), a training-free compression method using soft tokens within LLM agent for long-horizon tasks. Specifically, ASTC uses the model's native recurrent dynamics to determine the already absorbed information, leveraging the commonly-used hybrid Gated Delta Network (GDN)-attention. It then carries this information forward as agentic soft tokens while retaining exact values as hard tokens. The resulting compact sequence reduces later-layer computation and yields reusable KV caches, extending the savings across the agent's trajectory. Extensive experiments on long-horizon tasks show that ASTC matches or exceeds the uncompressed agent's accuracy with up to 50.68% fewer end-to-end Attention Pairs, while trained compressors require 15.4 to 103.7 times more Attention Pairs per successful task. These findings highlight agentic soft tokens as a model-native way to carry absorbed context forward as the task representation evolves.

title: From Transcription to Reformulation: Defining and Benchmarking Grounded Generative Speech Recognition
summary: Speech language models have expanded automatic speech recognition (ASR) from transcription to general speech-to-text generation. Yet existing benchmarks still assume a single ground-truth transcript per utterance, an assumption that struggles when models produce readable, formatted, or structured outputs. In this work, we introduce Grounded Generative Speech Recognition (GSR), reformulating speech recognition as generating semantically grounded text instead of a single transcript. We define a grounded reformulation space that characterizes all valid textual realizations supported by the input speech, and establish a four-level hierarchy of reformulation capabilities, including literal transcription, canonical reformulation, semantic reformulation and speech-grounded structuring. Based on this formulation, we present GSR-Bench, the first comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate generative speech recognition systems beyond exact transcript matching. GSR-Bench covers diverse scenarios including refined meeting transcription, cross-dialect translation, context-aware speech understanding, and robustness under silent or noisy acoustic conditions. To address the limitations of word-level evaluation metrics, we develop a multi-dimensional evaluation framework combining speech grounding assessment and LLM-based semantic judgment, whose reliability is validated through human preference studies. Extensive experiments across representative architectures, ranging from conventional ASR systems to end-to-end Speech-LLMs, reveal fundamental trade-offs between transcription fidelity and generative reformulation ability. Our analysis further identifies critical failure modes, including acoustic hallucination, unsupported generation, and instruction drift, providing insights into the design and evaluation of future grounded generative speech systems.

AI.title_translation: 从转写到重构：定义并评测接地生成式语音识别
AI.tldr: 本文提出了“接地生成式语音识别”（GSR）范式及 GSR-Bench 评测基准，突破了单一标准转写的限制，从多维度系统评估语音模型的内容重构与生成能力。
AI.motivation: 语音语言模型已将语音识别从字面转写拓展到多样的文本生成任务，但现有基准仍默认每个音频仅有一个标准转写文本，难以有效评估模型生成的格式化、易读化或结构化输出。
AI.method: 1. 提出接地生成式语音识别（GSR）概念，定义了由输入语音支持的接地重构空间，并建立四级能力层级（字面转写、规范重构、语义重构、基于语音的结构化）；2. 构建包含多种复杂现实场景的 GSR-Bench 基准测试；3. 开发结合语音接地评估与大语言模型语义判断的多维度评估框架，并通过人类偏好实验验证其可靠性。
AI.result: 在传统 ASR 系统与端到端 Speech-LLM 上的实验表明，转写保真度与生成重构能力之间存在本质权衡，并揭示了模型常出现的声学幻觉、无支持生成和指令漂移等关键失败模式。
AI.conclusion: 本文重新定义了生成式语音识别并提出了综合基准 GSR-Bench，为未来接地生成式语音系统的设计、能力演进和可靠性评估提供了关键框架与指导。
AI.translation: 语音语言模型已将自动语音识别（ASR）从传统的字面转写扩展为通用的语音到文本生成。然而，现有基准仍然假设每个语音片段仅对应一个标准转写，当模型生成易读、格式化或结构化的输出时，这一假设便面临困境。在本文中，我们提出了接地生成式语音识别（GSR），将语音识别重新定义为生成语义接地的文本，而非单一的转录文本。我们定义了一个接地重构空间，用于刻画由输入语音所支持的所有有效文本表达，并建立了包含字面转写、规范重构、语义重构和基于语音的结构化在内的四级重构能力层级。基于这一形式化定义，我们推出了 GSR-Bench，这是首个旨在评估超越精确转录匹配的生成式语音识别系统的综合基准。GSR-Bench 涵盖了多样化的场景，包括精炼会议转录、跨方言翻译、上下文感知语音理解，以及在静音或噪声声学条件下的鲁棒性。为解决词级评估指标的局限，我们开发了一个结合语音接地评估和基于大语言模型语义判断的多维度评估框架，并通过人类偏好研究验证了其可靠性。在涵盖传统 ASR 系统到端到端 Speech-LLM 等代表性架构的广泛实验中，我们揭示了转录保真度与生成重构能力之间的根本权衡。我们的分析进一步指出了关键的失败模式，包括声学幻觉、无支持生成和指令漂移，为未来接地生成式语音系统的设计与评估提供了深刻见解。
AI.summary: 针对现有语音识别基准单一标准转录的局限性，本文提出了接地生成式语音识别（GSR）及其评测基准 GSR-Bench。通过建立四级重构能力层级和结合 LLM 评判的多维评估指标，该研究系统性评测了 Speech-LLM 的生成能力，揭示了保真度与重构力之间的权衡及核心失效模式。
AI.keywords: 生成式语音识别, 语音语言模型, GSR-Bench, 语音重构, 评测基准
AI.comments: 该研究切中当前语音大模型（Speech-LLM）评估的核心痛点。长期以来，ASR 评测过度依赖单一标准答案的字错率（WER），严重限制了能够进行格式整理、结构化输出和口语规范化的现代生成式语音系统的发展。本文创新的四级重构体系和 GSR-Bench 为超越字面匹配的生成式语音理解提供了清晰的评估框架与基准，识别出的声学幻觉和指令漂移等缺陷对未来模型优化具有很高的指导价值。

title: Assortativity and the Distribution of Spectral Gaps in Directed Networks
summary: This paper studies how the distribution of spectral gaps of a weighted directed network varies with its assortativity. We prove that the sum of the distances of each of the eigenvalues from the Perron root along the real axis, which we call the `spectral depth', decreases as the network is rewired to be less assortative. The result is conditional on the network's Perron vectors ordering the rewired vertices in the same way as their strengths do. We also develop a method to determine whether a particular spectral gap contracts or expands under a rewiring that changes the network's assortativity. It turns out that the direction of any one gap depends on far more than the network's assortativity. In computational experiments on heavy-tailed networks, disassortative rewiring lowers the spectral depth by about two fifths, contracts most strongly the gaps in the middle of the spectrum, and collapses a growing part of the spectrum to zero. The experiments also show that a sequence of disassortative rewirings tends to narrow the first spectral gap, while a sequence of assortative rewirings widens it.

AI.title_translation: 有向网络中的同配性与谱隙分布
AI.tldr: 本文研究有向网络中同配性如何影响谱隙分布和“谱深度”，发现去同配性重连能降低谱深度，并开发了分析单个谱隙变化的方法，实验证实了这些理论。
AI.motivation: 研究加权有向网络中谱隙分布如何随其同配性变化。
AI.method: 通过理论证明，定义并分析了“谱深度”与同配性之间的关系，并开发了一种确定特定谱隙在重连下收缩或扩张的方法。通过在重尾网络上进行计算实验来验证理论发现并观察谱隙行为。
AI.result: 理论证明，当网络被重连为去同配性时，“谱深度”（特征值到Perron根的距离之和）会减小，但需满足Perron向量与节点强度对重连顶点排序方式一致的条件。研究发现，单个谱隙的收缩或扩张方向不仅取决于网络的同配性。计算实验表明，在重尾网络中，去同配性重连使谱深度降低约五分之二，最强烈地收缩了谱中间的间隙，并使谱中越来越多的部分趋于零。去同配性重连序列倾向于缩小第一个谱隙，而同配性重连序列则会扩大它。
AI.conclusion: 有向网络的同配性显著影响其谱隙分布和谱深度。去同配性重连通常能降低谱深度并改变谱隙的结构，但单个谱隙的变化受多种因素影响，而非简单地由同配性决定。
AI.translation: 本文研究加权有向网络的谱隙分布如何随其同配性变化。我们证明，每个特征值沿实轴到Perron根的距离之和（我们称之为“谱深度”）会随着网络被重连以降低同配性而减小。该结果的前提是网络的Perron向量对重连顶点的排序方式与它们的强度一致。我们还开发了一种方法来确定在改变网络同配性的重连下，特定谱隙是收缩还是扩张。结果表明，任何一个间隙的方向远不止取决于网络的同配性。在对重尾网络进行的计算实验中，去同配性重连使谱深度降低了约五分之二，最强烈地收缩了谱中间的间隙，并使谱中越来越多的部分归零。实验还表明，一系列去同配性重连倾向于缩小第一个谱隙，而一系列同配性重连则会扩大它。
AI.summary: 这篇论文探讨了加权有向网络中同配性如何影响谱隙的分布。作者定义了“谱深度”并证明其在去同配性重连下会减小，但需满足特定条件。论文还提出了一种分析单个谱隙在重连下收缩或扩张的方法，并指出其变化受多重因素影响。计算实验进一步证实，去同配性重连能显著降低谱深度，并对谱隙结构产生特定影响，例如缩小第一个谱隙。
AI.keywords: 有向网络, 同配性, 谱隙, 谱深度, 特征值
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过引入“谱深度”概念，为理解有向网络中同配性与谱性质的关系提供了一个新的量化视角。其结合理论证明和计算实验的方法增强了研究的严谨性。特别是对单个谱隙行为的深入分析，揭示了谱性质变化的复杂性，超越了简单同配性变化的解释。

title: Self-Improvement with Auxiliary Rewards: Learning from Verified Traces and Evaluating Transfer
summary: Answer-level rewards cannot distinguish reasoning traces with equally correct outcomes. We study whether auxiliary trajectory preferences improve small-language-model self-improvement and transfer under limited supervision. We compare confidence-based (SC) and entropy-based metrics (UID-Conj.), which combines global entropy variation and local smoothness, through online reward augmentation and offline training on correct responses. Online experiments adapt Qwen3-1.7B on 30 AIME problems without reference answers; offline experiments use historical AIME problems. UID-Conj. improves the online macro-average across the adaptation benchmark and three transfer benchmarks by 2.08 percentage points over unmodified TTRL. The strongest evidence comes from offline weighted SFT: UID-Conj. exceeds uniform weighting on the same response pool by 1.93 points, with a paired prompt-bootstrap 95\% CI of [0.44, 3.44]. Benefits are task-dependent: SC rewards judged trace quality and instruction following, while UID-Conj. rewards yield stronger training outcomes in several settings. We find that auxiliary preferences can expose learning value among equally correct traces not captured during inference time, motivating their evaluation through downstream gains.

AI.title_translation: 基于辅助奖励的自我改进：从验证轨迹中学习与评估迁移
AI.tldr: 通过引入基于熵和置信度的辅助轨迹奖励，有效区分得出相同正确答案的推理轨迹，显著提升小模型的自我改进与迁移泛化能力。
AI.motivation: 仅基于最终答案层面的奖励无法区分具有相同正确结果的不同推理轨迹，因此需要研究在有限监督下，辅助轨迹偏好是否能够提升小语言模型的自我改进与迁移能力。
AI.method: 对比基于置信度（SC）与基于熵（UID-Conj.，结合全局熵变化与局部平滑度）的度量指标，通过在线奖励增强以及对正确回复的离线加权监督微调（SFT）进行实验。在线实验在无参考答案的30道AIME题目上适配Qwen3-1.7B，离线实验则采用历史AIME题目。
AI.result: 在在线实验中，UID-Conj.在适配基准及三个迁移基准上的宏平均准确率相比未修改的TTRL提升了2.08个百分点。在离线加权SFT中，UID-Conj.在相同回复池上较均匀加权提升了1.93个百分点（配对prompt-bootstrap 95%置信区间为[0.44, 3.44]）。此外，SC奖励在评估轨迹质量和指令遵循上表现较好，而UID-Conj.奖励在多个设置下能带来更强的训练效果。
AI.conclusion: 辅助偏好能够揭示推理轨迹中在推理阶段无法捕获的学习价值（即使这些轨迹均能得出正确答案），从而有效推动小模型的自我提升与泛化，这也为其通过下游收益进行评估提供了充分依据。
AI.translation: 答案层面的奖励无法区分得出相同正确结果的推理轨迹。本文研究在有限监督条件下，辅助轨迹偏好是否能够改善小型语言模型的自我改进与迁移能力。我们通过在线奖励增强和针对正确回复的离线训练，对比了基于置信度（SC）与基于熵的度量指标（UID-Conj.，结合全局熵变化与局部平滑度）。在线实验在无参考答案的30道AIME问题上对Qwen3-1.7B进行适配；离线实验则使用历史AIME问题。结果表明，UID-Conj.在适配基准及三个迁移基准上的在线宏平均指标相比未修改的TTRL提升了2.08个百分点。最强有力的证据来自离线加权SFT：在相同回复池下，UID-Conj.比均匀加权高出1.93个百分点，配对prompt-bootstrap 95%置信区间为[0.44, 3.44]。这种增益具有任务依赖性：SC奖励擅长判定轨迹质量和指令遵循，而UID-Conj.奖励在多个设置中带来更强的训练效果。我们发现，辅助偏好可以揭示出在推理期间无法捕获的、相同正确轨迹中潜在的学习价值，从而促使通过下游增益对其进行评估。
AI.summary: 本文针对仅凭答案无法区分推理轨迹优劣的问题，提出利用基于置信度（SC）和基于熵（UID-Conj.）的辅助轨迹奖励指导小模型自我改进。实验表明，UID-Conj.在在线增强和离线加权微调中均显著优于基线，证明了辅助轨迹奖励能够挖掘正确轨迹中的潜在学习价值并提升迁移性能。
AI.keywords: 辅助奖励, 自我改进, 推理轨迹, 熵指标, 迁移学习
AI.comments: 本研究创新性地探讨了在答案均正确的情况下，如何利用辅助奖励（特别是结合全局熵变化与局部平滑度的UID-Conj.指标）挖掘推理轨迹的学习价值。这突破了传统仅依赖结果奖励的局限，为小语言模型在弱监督甚至无参考答案设置下的自我改进提供了新思路；不过结果也表明收益具有任务依赖性。

title: Toward Low-Burden Image-Based Dietary Assessment Through Human-AI Collaborative Correction
summary: Image-based dietary assessment can automate initial food logging, but meal photographs often leave food identity, hidden ingredients, preparation, and portion uncertain, making correction a recurring part of use. We introduce Human-AI Collaborative Correction, which reframes correction as communicate intent $\rightarrow$ regenerate $\rightarrow$ verify: users express what should change through text, voice, or guided clarification, the AI regenerates the linked dietary record, and users verify the result. In a within-participant study with 30 participants, compared with conventional Manual Search-and-Edit Correction, collaborative correction was associated with lower workload (Raw TLX: 35.83 vs. 55.00; p < .001), 21.0% lower recorded usage time, 51.1% fewer recorded clicks, and more favorable user-experience ratings; 90.0% preferred it overall. An exploratory nutrient analysis also found lower energy MAE. These findings support intent-driven regeneration as a promising interaction pattern for reducing correction burden while preserving user verification and making image-based dietary tracking easier to sustain.

AI.title_translation: 通过人机协作纠错实现低负担的基于图像的饮食评估
AI.tldr: 提出一种人机协作的饮食记录纠错方法，通过“意图表达-AI再生-用户验证”模式显著减少了用户的操作负担和工作量。
AI.motivation: 基于图像的饮食评估虽然能自动化初始的食物记录，但照片常导致食物身份、隐藏成分、烹饪方法和分量不确定，使得纠错成为不可或缺且繁琐的环节，因此需要减少纠错带来的负担。
AI.method: 引入了“人机协作纠错”机制（通过文本、语音或引导澄清表达意图 $\rightarrow$ AI重新生成膳食记录 $\rightarrow$ 用户验证），并通过包含30名参与者的内试实验（within-participant study），将其与传统的“手动搜索和编辑”纠错方式进行了对比。
AI.result: 与传统的手动搜索编辑纠错相比，人机协作纠错具有更低的工作负载（Raw TLX: 35.83 对 55.00；p < .001）、使用时间减少21.0%、点击次数减少51.1%、更佳的用户体验评分，90.0%的用户总体上更偏爱该方法，且能量预测的平均绝对误差（MAE）更低。
AI.conclusion: 基于意图驱动的重新生成是一种很有前景的交互模式，能有效降低饮食记录纠错负担，同时保留人工验证，使基于图像的饮食追踪更易于长期坚持。
AI.translation: 基于图像的饮食评估可以使初始食物记录自动化，但餐食照片往往使食物身份、隐藏成分、烹饪方法和分量变得不确定，这使得纠错成为使用中的一个常见部分。我们引入了“人机协作纠错”机制，将纠错重新定义为：表达意图 $\rightarrow$ 重新生成 $\rightarrow$ 验证。用户通过文本、语音或引导澄清表达应更改的内容，AI重新生成相关的饮食记录，然后用户验证结果。在一项有30名参与者的内试研究中，与传统的手动搜索和编辑纠错相比，协作纠错具有更低的工作负载（原始TLX：35.83对55.00；p < .001）、记录使用时间减少21.0%、记录点击次数减少51.1%以及更佳的用户体验评分；90.0%的参与者总体上更偏爱该方法。探索性营养分析还发现更低的能量平均绝对误差（MAE）。这些发现支持意图驱动的再生作为一种有前景的交互模式，能够在减轻纠错负担的同时保留用户验证，使基于图像的饮食追踪更容易坚持。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了“人机协作纠错”（Human-AI Collaborative Correction）方法，旨在解决图像饮食评估中因照片模糊不清而需要繁琐修正的问题。该方法通过“表达意图-重新生成-验证”的交互模式，显著减轻了用户的工作负荷和操作步骤，提升了用户体验和营养估计的准确性。
AI.keywords: 基于图像的饮食评估, 人机协作, 意图驱动纠错, 膳食记录, 用户体验
AI.comments: 本文提出了一种人机协作的饮食记录纠错方法，将传统的繁琐手动搜索编辑转化为“表达意图-重新生成-验证”的模式，显著降低了用户的认知和操作负担，对图像饮食评估的实际应用具有重要推动作用。

title: Subliminal Reinforcement Learning: traits travel through a judge's scores
comments: 37 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables, 2 Extended Data figures, 6 Extended Data tables; Supplementary Information included. Code and data: https://github.com/kkt94/subliminal-rl
summary: Subliminal learning, the transfer of a model's trait through data with no semantic trace of it, has been shown for students trained on a teacher's text. Post-training relies on group relative policy optimization with a language-model judge, where the student learns only from its own outputs and one judge's scores. We show this suffices: a student writes invented syllables or numbers, a judge made to prefer one animal scores them, and the student's preference moves toward that animal relative to a run whose judge prefers another. Of 48 design cells, two fail the validity gate and 17 establish the trait at 5% false-discovery rate, numbers-only cells included; elsewhere, our account gives the reason. Removing only the reward difference between judges removes transfer. We establish the principle as a chain of four stages: the trait must show in the judge's scores, favour strings that move the student, accumulate and reach the answers. Judges with the same preference built from other data, or on another model, place it on other strings, and transfer is not detected. Carried unchanged to AI-safety dispositions, the chain holds: undesirable dispositions reach the student's answers, and stages measured before training anticipate where, helping to prevent part of this risk.
comment: 37 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables, 2 Extended Data figures, 6 Extended Data tables; Supplementary Information included. Code and data: https://github.com/kkt94/subliminal-rl

AI.title_translation: 潜意识强化学习：特征通过裁判的分数进行传播
AI.tldr: 本论文证明了在强化学习中，即使没有语义痕迹，语言模型裁判的评分也能将特定特征隐蔽地传递给学生模型，这对AI安全防范具有重要警示。
AI.motivation: 探索在后训练阶段中，仅通过语言模型裁判的分数，模型之间是否能够发生没有语义痕迹的特征转移（即潜意识学习）。
AI.method: 通过让学生模型输出自创的音节或数字，并由偏好某种动物的裁判进行打分，利用组相对策略优化（GRPO）观察学生模型的偏好变化，并在48个设计单元中进行验证。
AI.result: 在48个设计单元中，有17个在5%的误报率下成功确立了特征转移，证明了即使只使用数字或无语义符号，奖励差异也能导致特征的传递。
AI.conclusion: 潜意识强化学习可以通过语言模型裁判的分数将特征转移给学生模型，这对于理解和防范AI安全风险具有重要意义。
AI.translation: 潜意识学习是指在没有语义痕迹的数据中传递模型的特征，这已经在基于教师文本训练的学生模型中得到了展示。后训练依赖于使用语言模型裁判的组相对政策优化，学生仅从其自己的输出和一个裁判的分数中学习。我们证明这已经足够：学生写出虚构的音节或数字，偏好某种动物的裁判对它们进行打分，并且相对于由偏好另一种动物的裁判运行的结果，学生的偏好向该动物移动。在48个设计单元中，有2个未通过有效性检验，17个在5%的误报率下确立了该特征，其中包括纯数字单元；在其他地方，我们的解释给出了原因。仅去除裁判之间的奖励差异就会消除转移。我们将该原则确立为四个阶段的链条：特征必须在裁判的分数中显示出来、偏好推动学生的字符串、积累并到达答案。由其他数据或在另一个模型上构建的具有相同偏好的裁判将其放在其他字符串上，并且未检测到转移。原封不动地应用到AI安全倾向中，这个链条仍然成立：不良倾向到达学生的答案，并在训练前测量的阶段预示着位置，有助于防范部分此类风险。
AI.summary: 该论文研究了强化学习中的潜意识学习现象，证明了通过语言模型裁判的奖励分数，即使输入数据没有语义痕迹，模型的特征（如偏好）也能成功转移给学生模型，这为理解AI安全风险提供了新的视角。
AI.keywords: 潜意识强化学习, 奖励机制, 语言模型裁判, 特征转移, AI安全
AI.comments: 该论文揭示了强化学习中潜意识学习（Subliminal Learning）的存在，即即使没有语义痕迹，模型的特征也可以通过裁判的分数进行传递。这对AI安全警示我们，不良倾向可能通过奖励机制隐蔽地转移给学生模型。

title: Scaled-Gradient Hard Thresholding Algorithms for Sparse Signal Recovery
summary: Thresholding methods provide a simple iterative framework for sparse signal recovery by combining a search direction with a thresholding operation. Gradient-based search directions are computationally efficient because they require only first-order information for the error metric. We incorporate componentwise gradient scaling into this framework by preserving large-magnitude components and attenuating the remaining components of the gradient of error metric. Combining this strategy with hard thresholding yields scaled-gradient hard thresholding (SGHT) and its pursuit variant SGHTP. Under suitable restricted isometry conditions, we establish recovery error bounds for both methods that account for measurement noise and deviations from exact sparsity. Numerical experiments indicate that SGHTP achieves recovery performance comparable to established pursuit methods on the tested ECG signals.

AI.title_translation: 用于稀疏信号恢复的缩放梯度硬阈值算法
AI.tldr: 本文提出了结合梯度缩放与硬阈值的新型稀疏信号恢复算法，在理论误差界和数值实验中均表现出色。
AI.motivation: 为了提供一种既计算高效（仅需一阶梯度信息）又能保持良好恢复性能的简单迭代框架，以解决稀疏信号恢复问题。
AI.method: 将分量梯度缩放策略（保留大振幅分量并衰减其余分量）与硬阈值相结合，提出了缩放梯度硬阈值（SGHT）及其追踪变体（SGHTP）算法，并在特定受限等距条件下推导了恢复误差界。
AI.result: 在合适的受限等距条件下，证明了这两种方法对于包含测量噪声和非精确稀疏偏差的信号具有收敛的恢复误差界，且在ECG信号的数值实验中表现出与主流追踪方法相当的性能。
AI.conclusion: 论文提出的基于梯度缩放的硬阈值算法（SGHT和SGHTP）在满足受限等距条件下能有效恢复稀疏信号，并在实验中表现出与现有追赶方法相当的性能。
AI.translation: 阈值方法通过将搜索方向与阈值操作相结合，为稀疏信号恢复提供了一个简单的迭代框架。基于梯度的搜索方向计算效率高，因为它们只需要误差度量的阶信息。我们将分量梯度缩放合并到这个框架中，通过保留误差度量梯度的最大幅度分量并衰减其余分量。将此策略与硬阈值相结合，产生了缩放梯度硬阈值（SGHT）及其追踪变体SGHTP。在适当的受限等距条件下，我们为这两种方法建立了恢复误差界，这些误差界考虑了测量噪声和与精确稀疏性的偏差。数值实验表明，SGHTP在测试的ECG信号上实现了与既定追踪方法相当的恢复性能。
AI.summary: 该文提出了一种结合分量梯度缩放与硬阈值的稀疏信号恢复算法（SGHT和SGHTP），通过理论证明和数值实验验证了其在噪声和非精确稀疏条件下的有效性和高性能。
AI.keywords: 稀疏信号恢复, 硬阈值算法, 梯度缩放, 受限等距性质, 测量噪声
AI.comments: 该论文通过引入分量梯度缩放策略改进了传统的硬阈值算法，在稀疏信号恢复领域具有一定的创新性与计算高效性。未来的研究可以进一步在更大规模的真实数据集上进行验证。

title: rl_rob: A transparent, from-scratch Python library for teaching reinforcement learning from tabular methods to deep policy gradients
summary: rl_rob is an open-source Python library for teaching reinforcement learning. It implements the arc of a modern course, from tabular temporal-difference learning through linear function approximation to deep value-based and policy-gradient methods, with every algorithm written from first principles so that its update rule is visible in a few lines of code. All agents share one interface, so learners can compare methods directly across stages and trace a deep reinforcement learning update from the temporal-difference error to the weight change. The library supports teaching and assessment in which students implement, modify and explain update rules, rather than only produce working code.

AI.title_translation: rl_rob：一个用于教授从表格方法到深度策略梯度强化学习的透明、从零开始的 Python 库
AI.tldr: rl_rob 是一个开源的 Python 强化学习教学库，通过从零实现、代码透明且接口统一的算法，帮助学生深入理解从传统表格方法到深度强化学习的更新规则。
AI.motivation: 为了解决现有的强化学习库往往过于黑盒、代码庞大复杂，不便用于展示从基础表格方法到深度强化学习演进过程的教学痛点，开发一个透明、易教、易学的开源库。
AI.method: 从第一原理出发，使用纯 Python 从头实现了一系列强化学习算法（从表格型时间差分学习到线性函数近似、深度基于价值的方法以及策略梯度方法），并为所有智能体提供统一的接口。
AI.result: 成功开发了 rl_rob 库，实现了跨越传统到现代深度强化学习算法的统一接口与可视化更新规则，支持学生直接修改、实现和解释更新规则的教学与评估活动。
AI.conclusion: rl_rob 作为一个专为教学设计的强化学习库，通过透明的代码实现和统一的接口，有效弥合了基础理论与深度强化学习之间的鸿沟，提升了教学和评估的效果。
