title: Rapid co-design of Buoyancy-assisted robots for Challenging Locomotion using Gaussian Evolutionary Specialists
summary: Designing high-performance legged robots requires jointly optimizing morphology and control. Model-free reinforcement learning (RL) enables learning complex controllers during co-design, but repeatedly training policies across candidate morphologies makes design optimization computationally expensive. Existing approaches can amortize policy learning across morphologies, but a single shared policy tends to converge toward one control strategy regardless of morphology, which we refer to as behavioral diversity collapse. We introduce Gaussian Evolutionary Specialists (GES), an RL-based co-design framework that maintains a population of specialist policies whose design-space territories evolve according to their relative control performance. We evaluate GES on the Buoyancy-Assisted Light Legged Unit (BALLU) robot for obstacle traversal and ramp walking over design spaces of up to four dimensions. GES achieves higher best design performance than Monolithic and Mixture-of-Experts baselines, with gains of 5.0-9.0 cm in obstacle height and 10.0-12.7 points in ramp grade. For the same 200 design-optimization evaluations, GES reduces wall-clock co-design time by 67.4% compared with retraining a policy for every candidate. Finally, teleoperated hardware experiments evaluate the optimized BALLU morphology, which traverses obstacles of up to 24 cm, compared with 8 cm on the original design.

title: Imputation of Public Opinion Data with Large Language Models
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are widely evaluated as simulators of survey responses, yet applied survey research mostly faces item nonresponse. Imputation fills in those missing values to restore the overall structure of a partially observed dataset and has its own well-defined evaluation criteria, which differ fundamentally from prediction accuracy. We present the first evaluation of LLM imputation against proper multiple-imputation metrics and statistical baselines on more than 5 million imputed responses from four public opinion surveys under various missingness mechanisms. We evaluate in-context learning (ICL) for this task by investigating 84 ICL configurations and comparing the best-performing configurations on six open-weight LLMs. The strongest ICL approach improves on zero-shot persona prompting but remains, at best, competitive with statistical baselines (MICE PMM, TabPFN). ICL approaches are sensitive to survey topics and consume 2-3 orders of magnitude more compute. Moreover, prediction metrics commonly used in LLM survey simulation (macro-F1, TVD) do not reliably track imputation quality. Our findings highlight the importance of fit-for-purpose evaluation for LLM imputation, where established multiple imputation remains the better default.

title: How Do Video Foundation Models Encode Intuitive Physics? Probing Across Pretraining Paradigms
comments: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on World Models in Physical AI
summary: Do video foundation models encode a usable sense of how the physical world works, and does intuitive physics emerge naturally from large-scale video pretraining? In this work, we study whether pretrained video foundation models encode intuitive-physics information in their frozen representations, and how its accessibility varies across pretraining paradigms, layers, backbone variants, and probe types. Using frozen-feature probing on IntPhys2 and Minimal Video Pairs (MVP), we compare predictive joint-embedding models (V-JEPA), masked reconstruction models (VideoMAE), and diffusion-based video generators (LTX-Video). We find that across linear, MLP, and temporal attentive probes, physics-relevant information is generally weakest in early layers and most accessible at intermediate to late depth. On MVP, temporal attentive probes substantially outperform linear readouts, with V-JEPA achieving 95.0% pair consistency. On IntPhys2, linear probes recover more signal, and VideoMAE attains the strongest temporal attentive result at 73.9% violation-of-expectation accuracy. On both benchmarks, attentive probe performance on LTX consistently underperforms compared to the other two pretraining paradigms. Together, these results suggest that intuitive-physics is broadly decodable from video foundation models, but it is not represented as a single, uniform capability. Its accessibility, and especially its temporal grounding, depends much more on the benchmark and readout than on a simple hierarchy of pretraining objectives or model scale.
comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on World Models in Physical AI

title: A Lightweight Fiducial-Based Pipeline for 3D Hyperspectral Mapping of ex-vivo Lumpectomy Specimens
summary: Hyperspectral Imaging (HSI) is a promising modality for intraoperative assessment of resection margins in Breast-Conserving Surgery (BCS), but its clinical translation requires aligning the inherently 2D spectral information onto the 3D shape of the excised tissue so that suspicious regions can be precisely localized for targeted follow-up. We present a fully automated, calibration-free pipeline that produces a 3D hyperspectral point cloud of an ex-vivo lumpectomy specimen from a set of consumer-camera RGB images and a single top-down HSI acquisition. The 3D geometry is reconstructed with a deep-learning Structure-from-Motion backbone, stabilized in a metric reference frame by a custom bundle adjustment that enforces consistency on the corners of four ArUco markers placed around the specimen. The HSI cube is then registered to the reconstruction without recovering the HSI camera pose: the markers, visible in both modalities, define 16 corner correspondences that drive a planar homography, and 3D coordinates are recovered by lookup on an orthographically rendered depth map. Evaluated on two ex-vivo lumpectomy specimens, the pipeline achieves a median 3D registration error below 1 mm and a 2D reprojection error below 0.02 mm, with a total per-specimen processing time under 4 minutes on accelerated hardware. These results support the feasibility of integrating HSI-guided spatial localization into intraoperative margin assessment workflows for breast-conserving surgery.

title: How to Score Experts for One-Shot MoE Expert Pruning: A Systematic Formulation and Selection Principle
summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models reduce per-token computation through sparse expert activation, yet deployment still requires storing the full expert pool, making one-shot expert pruning a practical approach for reducing memory usage. Although effective, existing criteria are largely heuristic, and no single criterion is universally optimal. Thus, establishing a principle for selecting pruning criteria suited to different deployment objectives remains an important yet largely underexplored problem in one-shot expert pruning. To this end, we introduce a systematic formulation for one-shot MoE expert pruning organized around three factors: routing frequency, gate weighting, and activation strength. The formulation yields a criteria selection principle: task-agnostic pruning should favor routed-token-averaged, gate-free activation-based criteria, whereas task-specific pruning can benefit from retaining routing-frequency and gate-weight information. Beyond this principle, the formulation also provides a systematic view of existing heuristic criteria and gives rise to two new task-agnostic criteria, Mean Activation Norm (MAN) and Mean Squared Activation Norm (MSAN). Across four representative MoE models and 16 diverse benchmarks, MAN and MSAN are consistently strong in the task-agnostic setting, obtain the top-two average ranks, and improve average performance by 4.0 points on average and up to 8.8 points over the strongest baseline.

title: AME: A Multi-Type Contributor Attribution Framework in Generative AI Markets
comments: We have decided to withdraw this manuscript because the research has undergone substantial revisions in its problem formulation, scope, and evaluation. As a result, the current version no longer adequately represents the revised study. We therefore withdraw this earlier version to avoid potential misunderstandings regarding the research findings
summary: Generative AI enables value creation through multi-stage collaboration among heterogeneous contributors, including training data, base models, fine-tuning behaviors, and prompts. However, how to fairly allocate the data value remains largely unexplored. This paper formulates multi-stage generative AI value allocation as a new research problem and identifies three core challenges: heterogeneous data contribution valuation, data rights mapping, and trustworthy execution. We propose AME (Attribution-Mapping-Execution) framework, a unified framework that integrates data contribution valuation, data rights mapping, and trustworthy execution into a single workflow. Experimental results demonstrate that AME framework achieves data value allocation outcomes more consistent with human reference judgments while maintaining low-cost trustworthy execution. Our work provides an initial foundation for value assessment and revenue allocation in generative AI data markets.

As a result, the current version no longer adequately represents the revised study. We therefore withdraw this earlier version to avoid potential misunderstandings regarding the research findings

title: MIRAGE: Auditing Anti-Muslim Bias in Frontier LLMs Across Reasoning, Agentic, and Time-Coupled Conditions
comments: arXiv admin note: This submission has been withdrawn because it does not meet arXiv's research content quality standards
summary: Five years after the discovery of persistent anti-Muslim bias in large language models, most evaluations remain confined to single-turn prompt completion, a setting that no longer reflects how frontier LLMs are deployed. We introduce \textbf{MIRAGE} (Muslim-Identity Reasoning and Agentic Generation Evaluation), a benchmark of 1{,}200 prompts spanning three deployment-realistic conditions: direct completion, chain-of-thought reasoning, and simulated agentic decision-making across content moderation, lending triage, refugee claim summarization, and hiring screens. Across six frontier models, we find that (i) chain-of-thought reasoning \emph{amplifies} rather than suppresses Muslim-violence associations by 12--34\% relative to direct completion, (ii) agentic decisions exhibit a 9--22 percentage-point asymmetry between Muslim and matched non-Muslim cases on identical evidence, and (iii) bias is sharply time-coupled to retrieved news context, increasing 18--27\% under recent-conflict retrieval. Existing prompt-based mitigations transfer poorly across our three conditions, suppressing direct-completion bias while leaving agentic asymmetry largely intact. We release MIRAGE and an open evaluation harness to support targeted mitigation research.

title: VEGA: Learning Navigation VLAs from In-the-Wild Egocentric Video with Geometric Trajectory Supervision
summary: We introduce VEGA, an approach for training navigation VisionLanguage-Action (VLA) models from unlabeled egocentric navigation videos. Internet-scale egocentric videos provide a scalable source of navigation-relevant visual observations, capturing cluttered scenes, close-range obstacles, and natural human motion through real-world spaces. However, these videos are not directly usable for policy learning because they do not provide obstacle-aware trajectories conditioned on explicit navigation goals in the robot's coordinate frame. VEGA addresses this gap by reconstructing local scene geometry from monocular video, sampling navigation goals (represented as text, image, or spatial waypoints) and generating obstacle-aware trajectories using the constructed geometry. The resulting trajectory distribution is then used to train a flow-matching VLA navigation policy. By using geometry exclusively during training, VEGA distills obstacle-aware planning directly into a vision-based policy. Furthermore, we introduce VEGA-Bench, a benchmark containing 250k scenes and approximately 5 million navigation goals paired with scene geometry, designed to evaluate goal progress, collision avoidance, and obstacle clearance of VLAs. Our evaluation shows that VEGA achieves competitive goal progress while reducing collisions by 33.0% and improving obstacle clearance by 17.9% over the strongest baseline on VEGABench, while improving success by at least 150.0%, reducing collisions by at least 66.7%, and improving obstacle clearance by at least 60.0% in real-world trials. Ultimately, we demonstrate that video-derived geometric supervision provides a scalable and effective signal for training obstacle-aware navigation VLAs. The code and benchmark will be released at the time of publication.

title: Low-vocality Engagement and Participation Dynamics on Bluesky
comments: Published in EPJ Data Science as "Low-vocality engagement and participation dynamics on Bluesky"
summary: Online participation is often measured through visible expression, especially posting, yet many consequential forms of engagement occur through less vocal actions such as liking and following. Here we study how users inhabit Bluesky by reconstructing participation profiles from more than three billion activity records produced by a near-complete sample accounting for more than 80\% of registered users. We aggregate behavior into monthly user-level observations and distinguish two dimensions that are often conflated in platform analytics: intensity, capturing how much users engage, and style, capturing how engagement is expressed across actions. We find that vocal production is highly concentrated, but low-posting behavior does not imply absence from platform participation. High-intensity engagement is most strongly associated with liking rather than posting, while posting-oriented participation is more common among low-intensity users, indicating that visibility and sustained engagement should not be conflated. Transition patterns suggest that high-intensity likers and posters could be described as attractors; network-building redirects users within the active space; whereas observed inactivity acts as a persistent boundary that selectively limits re-entry. Higher-order motifs further show that inactivity often interrupts rather than erases prior regimes, and that low-intensity liking can precede durable high-intensity engagement. These results show that online participation is structured by differentiated low-vocality practices, calling for a shift from post-centered measures of activity toward dynamic accounts of platform presence. We identify a broader challenge for computational social science: platform participation cannot be adequately understood through the behavior of vocal minorities alone.
comment: Published in EPJ Data Science as "Low-vocality engagement and participation dynamics on Bluesky"

title: PRISM: Feed-Forward Single-Image 3D Reconstruction via Geometric Warp-Residual Modeling
summary: Reconstructing 3D scenes from a single image is a fundamental challenge in computer vision, with broad applications in virtual reality, robotics, and content creation. Recent methods achieve outstanding performance by leveraging camera-controlled video diffusion models, but rely on iterative diffusion sampling, which greatly limits their practical deployment. We observe that geometric forward warping alone can cover the majority of a target view directly from the input image, with only a compact residual left for the encoder to correct. Motivated by this observation, we propose PRISM, a feed-forward framework that decomposes multi-view latent prediction into a parameter-free geometric prior and a learned residual correction, with no diffusion sampling required at inference. To enable generalization from purely synthetic training data, we devise a two-stage training strategy combining latents supervised distillation for geometric generalization and perceptual fine-tuning for appearance quality optimization. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks demonstrate that PRISM achieves competitive reconstruction quality compared with diffusion-based methods, while reducing inference time dramatically to only 36 seconds per scene. Our code is available at https://github.com/microjie372/PRISM.

title: TileMaxSim: Roofline Regimes and Compression Limits for Fused GPU MaxSim Scoring
summary: MaxSim scoring dominates the cost of multi-vector retrieval. Several groups built fused GPU kernels for it independently during 2026, and all report one measure of success: the fraction of peak memory bandwidth reached. That measure assumes the operator is limited by the bytes it moves. We show the assumption fails in two ways, and that two other quantities decide performance: which side of the roofline ridge a shape falls on, and how many dependent gathers the scoring path performs. We first locate the boundary. Fused arithmetic intensity is Nq*Nd /(Nq + Nd) FLOP per byte, against an H100 dense-FP16 ridge of 295.4. The operator is therefore memory-bound at ColBERT shapes and compute-bound at ColPali-scale query lengths. Published analyses report one side each and do not reconcile them. We measure the crossover at three document lengths, and a closed form predicts it inside the measured bracket each time. Past the crossover, percent of peak bandwidth falls to 4% while percent of peak FLOPs rises above 40%. The reported measure is therefore defined on only one side of a boundary that real workloads cross. We also validate the underlying traffic model against DRAM counters, to 0.003%. We then show that moving fewer bytes does not make the kernel faster. Fusing product-quantized asymmetric distance computation into the kernel moves 15.9x fewer bytes than exact FP16 on tensor cores and runs 3.0x slower. Counters rule out the usual causes: it reaches 1.23% of peak DRAM throughput at 98.2% occupancy. The limit is 6.5*10^9 dependent gathers, a count that does not fall when the codes get smaller. A hand-written CUDA version with a staged table recovers 4.7x and remains slower than exact scoring. Finally, we give the first head-to-head comparison of three fused MaxSim kernels, over 28 shapes, with every result checked against an exhaustive FP32 reference.

title: GPUSparse: Fast and Exact Learned Sparse Retrieval on a GPU-Resident Inverted Index
summary: Learned sparse models such as SPLADE match the quality of dense bi-encoders and keep the exact-match behavior of lexical retrieval. They are served on CPUs, using inverted-index traversal algorithms such as WAND. These algorithms are fast because they prune: they skip documents that cannot enter the top-k. Pruning makes the result approximate, and its control flow is sequential and datadependent, which suits a CPU and not a GPU. We argue that a GPU should not run a faster traversal. It should remove traversal altogether. A GPU has enough memory bandwidth to score every posting, so exactness need not be traded for speed. We present GPUSparse, which keeps the inverted index in GPU memory and scores queries with one fused scatter-add kernel. Nothing is pruned. GPUSparse searches all 8.8M MS MARCO passages in 1.27 ms per query, at 787 queries per second on one H100. Its results are exact: Recall@10, @100 and @1000 against an exhaustive FP32 reference are all 1.000, and quality at full scale matches Pyserini's exact SPLADE retrieval to three decimals. Exactness costs hardware rather than latency. Under core pinning, one H100 is worth about seven CPU cores. GPUSparse is 5.6x faster than one core and 2.8x slower than a 32-core socket. A CPU socket is therefore cheaper for approximate serving. The GPU is the better choice when exactness is required, where GPUSparse is 3.0x faster than exact CPU block-max pruning. We also decompose GPU latency. Traversal takes 55 to 80% of it and selection 18 to 38%, and the split moves with scale, which reconciles three conflicting published reports.

title: QueenBee: A Recursively Self-Improving Harness for Communication Topology Design in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
summary: LLM-based multi-agent systems show great potential for complex tasks through role specialization and collaborative reasoning. However, existing automated workflow design methods primarily focus on one-off search and candidate optimization, lacking sustained accumulation and reuse of structural design experience to meet evolving coordination demands. We propose QueenBee, an experience-guided framework for multi-agent workflow evolution. QueenBee represents workflows as executable programs that generate temporal communication DAGs and maintains Structural Feedback and Transition Bank (SFT-Bank), a persistent structural memory of execution diagnoses, design hypotheses and validation outcomes, and historical programs. This accumulated experience guides subsequent workflow generation, validation, and optimization, enabling the co-evolution of collaboration programs and design experience. Experiments on Silo-Bench show that QueenBee outperforms fixed communication baselines across team sizes and achieves the highest mean task score among recent automated multi-agent workflow optimization methods. Ablation studies further show that SFT-Bank components provide complementary performance gains, while evolution dynamics reveal a consistently improving average trend in the quality of the best collaboration structures found across independent runs as structural experience accumulates.

title: Beyond IID: How General Are Tabular Foundation Models, Really?
comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Datasets and Benchmarks Track. v2: NeurIPS camera-ready version
summary: Foundation models for predictive machine learning on tabular data have recently gained significant traction in academia and industry. Research communities across disciplines are increasingly evaluating tabular foundation models on diverse datasets and tasks. However, these task- and discipline-specific evaluations remain largely inaccessible to model researchers because benchmark software and evaluation protocols are fragmented. As a result, model researchers rely on standard benchmarks, which are mostly defined for tasks where tabular foundation models already excel. The most challenging scenarios are excluded, limiting meaningful progress in the field by focusing on marginal improvements on IID data rather than on broader, more demanding challenges. To overcome this, we introduce BeyondArena, the first unified holistic benchmark for tabular data that supports diverse task types (IID, temporal, grouped), across sample size and feature dimensionality scales, with diverse feature types (with text, with high cardinality) from a broad range of disciplines. To enable unified benchmarking beyond standard benchmarks, we introduce DataFoundry, a Python framework and metadata schema for curating tabular datasets for predictive machine learning. Our results across 11 models and 142 curated datasets show that current open-source tabular foundation models are competitive or excel on datasets up to 100k rows, while traditional tree-based and deep learning models still dominate on grouped or large data. BeyondArena guides model research for the most demanding challenges in tabular data, enabling progress towards truly foundational tabular models.

title: Sequential Planning via Anchored Robotic Keypoints
summary: Changes to what a robot can see do not necessarily mean that there is a change in the problem it is trying to solve, and many language-conditioned manipulation systems struggle with this distinction. When something in a scene moves, the robot might need to execute its actions in different places, but its manipulation plan can stay the same. We propose Sequential Planning via Anchored Robotic Keypoints (\spark), which describes a task as a symbolic behavior tree that we only anchor to the current 3D observations when each action is called. By verifying the plan at runtime we can recover from failures locally and anchor the objects to the scene again. We ask for a new plan only if this fails. We isolate this concept by taking a fixed plan and moving objects in the scene while executing. When displacing objects by $10$\,cm we were still able to complete $66.7\%$ of trials with scene-diff verification and layered recovery, and we did not have to change the plan. We test our full system on \libpro with these conditions. There is no practice on the tasks being tested and no access to simulator states during rollouts, and as in \rats and \capx a success check after each attempt decides whether to retry. We use one open-weight 27B planner with 4-bit weights. Under this protocol \spark achieves a mean success of $66.8\%$ across the 6 position and task settings and $66.8\%$ on the held-out language and object settings. We also achieve a $68\%$ success rate across 11 physical task-embodiment settings on 3 different robots. Our work demonstrates that for an important class of failures the robot does not need to ask for a new plan for its task. It can be enough to update the system's view of the world. Code and videos can be found at https://cwru-aism.github.io/spark-page/

title: Soft Mixture-of-Recursions: Going Deeper with Recursive Vision Transformers
summary: Vision Transformers are typically scaled by increasing depth or width, at the cost of more unique parameters. We explore recursion as an alternative scaling axis that increases effective computational depth through parameter reuse. Yet simply increasing recursion depth does not reliably improve performance because representations from different recursion stages are not fully utilized. We propose Soft Mixture-of-Recursions (SoftMoR), which learns token-wise weights to combine representations across recursion steps, and instantiate it as the Soft Recursive Vision Transformer (SR-ViT). Experiments on ImageNet-1K, COCO, and ADE20K show that SR-ViT can benefit from deeper recursion while adding few parameters. On ImageNet-1K, increasing recursion depth from T=1 to T=3 improves top-1 accuracy from 79.83% to 82.45% with only 1.1M additional parameters. At matched effective depth, SR-ViT also outperforms independently parameterized counterparts with substantially fewer parameters. These results support recursive deepening as an effective, parameter-efficient scaling axis for Vision Transformers. The code is available at https://github.com/sangin-lee/sr-vit .

title: On the Design Space of Discrete Diffusion Online Adaptation for Molecular Optimization
comments: Accepted at the Fortieth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
summary: Molecular optimization often starts from a pretrained generative model that captures a broad prior over valid molecular structures. At test time, however, the goal is not to sample from this prior, but to use a limited oracle budget to shift generation toward task-specific high-reward molecules. We study this adaptation problem for discrete diffusion models. Each online round couples several choices. The loop must decide which candidates to evaluate, how rewards become model updates, which feedback to reuse, and how far to move beyond the pretrained prior. These choices have mostly been studied in isolation, leaving open whether they complement one another, become redundant, or interfere inside a full online adaptation loop. We conduct controlled studies across six small-molecule binding-affinity tasks and three protein-fitness tasks. We find that acquisition, reward shaping, and model debiasing provide complementary routes to higher reward, especially for small molecules. Replay further stabilizes learning, while validity penalties keep small-molecule exploration on the valid molecular manifold. Together, these findings point to a practical recipe for feedback-efficient molecular optimization: online fine-tuning with acquisition, reward shaping, debiasing, replay, and validity control. This recipe outperforms offline fine-tuning and inference-time search baselines under matched oracle-call budgets and GPU-hour accounting. The gains are largest when high-reward candidates require larger shifts from the pretrained prior.
comment: Accepted at the Fortieth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

title: Towards Diverse and Comprehensive Benchmarks for Mutual Information Estimation
summary: Mutual information estimation is a central problem in machine learning and statistics; however, existing benchmarks typically evaluate estimators on simplified, low-dimensional distributions, leaving their performance on complex, realistic data largely unexplored. We address this gap with a comprehensive benchmarking framework grounded in a unified copula-theoretic perspective that subsumes existing benchmarks as special cases. Within this framework, we propose two complementary families of tests: a copula-first family that systematically varies ground-truth mutual information, dimensionality, and marginal complexity using synthetic and flow-based transformations; and a marginals-first family that couples real-world image data with controlled dependency structures, extending the classic same-class-pairing paradigm. We use this suite to extensively evaluate three classes of estimators: non-parametric, variational, and generative. Contrary to prevailing assumptions, our results indicate that there is no universal winner: each category can systematically outperform all other estimators under specific setups. By analyzing these cases, we identify fundamental estimation barriers and propose new tests that more effectively stress these specific limitations. We share the open source code at https://github.com/VanessB/mutinfo.

title: Fields of the Planet: Field Boundary Mapping Beyond 10m
summary: Field-boundary accuracy depends on the model, sensor resolution, label discretization, and evaluation procedure. Measuring the contribution of sensor resolution therefore requires a controlled comparison across sensors. We present Fields of the Planet (FTP), a 3 m PlanetScope companion to Fields of The World (FTW) containing 133,168 co-registered patch-window targets across 24 countries. FTP preserves FTW's vector polygons, seasonal windows, and dataset splits, enabling direct comparison with 10 m Sentinel-2. We first quantify the resolution ceiling by rasterizing and vectorizing the same ground-truth parcels at each resolution to determine which fields the label grid can represent. We evaluate predicted parcels with polygon-level and boundary metrics. With identical PRUE+ training and post-processing across sensors, plus an upsampled Sentinel-2 control, we isolate gains from image content. PlanetScope raises panoptic quality (PQ) from 21.0 to 35.5, improves PQ on sub-$0.5$ ha fields from 5.8 to 15.7, and reduces matched-boundary error from 18.6 m to 7.4 m. Pixel-level metrics understate this improvement, so field-boundary benchmarks should account for sensor resolution.

title: Physics-Audited Agentic Discovery in Scientific Machine Learning
summary: Agentic discovery can yield mechanics surrogates with low validation error that nonetheless violate physical requirements. We present Physics-Audited Agentic SciML (PA-SciML), a framework combining large language model agents with physics auditing. Physical requirements, encoded as contracts such as superposition, boundary conditions, and causality, are fixed before candidate search and tested on predicted fields without reference solutions, including through an adversarial search. Audit results guide later proposals and model selection but are reported separately from validation error. Single-edit tests document reusable design changes. Four solid-mechanics problems of increasing complexity, from parametric elasticity to heterogeneous stiffness fields and cyclic plasticity with combined hardening, reveal causality, zero-input, and stress-bound violations in surrogates selected by error alone. In elastodynamics, two surrogates reach nearly equal error, but only the audit-enabled one is causal by construction. Audit-enabled surrogates pass the required checks at sampled inputs while matching or exceeding audit-disabled accuracy in most comparisons.

title: NanoVSR: Towards Real-Time Video Super-Resolution on Edge Devices
summary: Recent Video Super-Resolution (VSR) methods rely heavily on transformers and explicit optical flow, creating computational overhead and custom operations that hinder deployment on hardware accelerators like TensorRT. To address this, we introduce NanoVSR, a scalable, fully convolutional architecture designed for resource-constrained edge devices. Using structural reparameterization, NanoVSR collapses into standard convolutions during inference, ensuring seamless hardware compatibility and negligible runtime overhead. Furthermore, despite lacking explicit motion compensation, it maintains competitive restoration quality by implicitly learning spatio-temporal alignments through progressive training. Evaluated on the REDS4 benchmark, NanoVSR demonstrates an exceptional balance between accuracy and computational efficiency, significantly improving the trade-off for compact architectures. Our NanoVSR-644k baseline yields 28.64 dB PSNR while delivering 27.2 FPS on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 16GB (25W), offering massive speed gains over heavier models. The scaled NanoVSR-1.7M variant reaches 29.15 dB with a throughput of 19.58 FPS, providing superior, edge-optimized upscaling. Code is available at https://github.com/filippawlicki/nanovsr.

title: A Twin gradient method for unconstrained optimization
summary: We propose a new strategy for gradient-based unconstrained optimization, involving two parallel sequences of iterates that cooperate to determine their stepsizes via a \textit{Twin-Step} principle. Rather than minimizing the objective function individually, the algorithm selects steplengths that minimize the Euclidean distance between the two gradient based processes occurring simultaneously at each iteration. The theoretical analysis shows that the convergence of the mutual distance is governed by the angle between the search directions. In particular the effectiveness of the overall process degrades as the directions approach parallelism. To ensure robustness against collinearity, we introduce a hybrid framework, Twin-ABB$_{\min}$, which switches to the Adaptive Barzilai--Borwein method when the geometric cooperation becomes ineffective. Extensive and very promising numerical results evidence that the Twin phase creates favorable initial conditions for subsequent BB-type iterations.

title: More than a Manipulator: Planning Propellant-Free Attitude Maneuvers for Free-Floating Spacecraft
comments: Presented at International Conference on Space Robotics (iSpaRo), November 3-6, 2026
summary: Spacecraft attitude control is traditionally achieved using momentum exchange devices or propellant-consuming thrusters. Meanwhile, a growing number of missions require robotic manipulators, which are typically treated as disturbance sources to be rejected rather than as actuators for spacecraft reorientation. This work investigates the use of manipulator motions for propellant-free attitude control by formulating a trajectory optimization problem with critical joint and collision avoidance constraints. Using an interior-point solver for the resulting nonlinear program, complex slew and detumble trajectories are computed for a range of spacecraft-manipulator systems, demonstrating rest-to-rest slew maneuvers of up to 90$^\circ$ and detumble maneuvers with a 40% reduction in angular velocity. The achievable control authority is also compared directly with that of reaction wheel arrays via momentum and torque envelopes, demonstrating the potential for manipulators to serve as redundant or even primary attitude control systems. This work provides a framework for using manipulators as multipurpose attitude control actuators, with particularly promising applications in in-space assembly and manufacturing when grasping payloads with high relative mass fractions.
comment: Presented at International Conference on Space Robotics (iSpaRo), November 3-6, 2026

title: DAUPNet: Domain-Aware Uncertainty Modeling for Reliable Prototype Discrimination in Cross-Domain Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation
summary: Cross-domain few-shot semantic segmentation (CD-FSS) has predominantly been formulated as learning domain-invariant representations or improving support-query correspondence. Nevertheless, large domain shifts still make prototype matching unreliable: inconsistent hierarchical responses corrupt the support representation, deterministic prototypes cannot express boundary and appearance ambiguity, and treating prototypes with different reliability equally during optimization weakens foreground-background separation. We therefore propose DAUPNet, a unified framework that reformulates cross-domain prototype matching as uncertainty-aware prototype discrimination. DAUPNet first harmonizes hierarchical support-query features to provide stable evidence, then represents foreground and background prototypes probabilistically, and finally uses their estimated uncertainty to regulate contrastive optimization. On four standard target domains, DAUPNet achieves 72.6% and 76.7% average mIoU in the 1-shot and 5-shot settings, respectively, including substantial gains on the two medical domains. These results demonstrate that modeling prototype uncertainty and incorporating it into optimization provides a robust and interpretable approach to CD-FSS under severe domain shift. The code is available at https://github.com/madness-Lei/DAUPNet

title: Idle Cycles Are Not Wasted Cycles
summary: Idle network service cores are treated as wasted compute. This assumption motivates increasingly sophisticated mechanisms that reclaim idle cores at microsecond timescales. We argue that this view no longer matches modern server hardware. On contemporary multicore processors, active cores compete for a shared package-level power and thermal budget. Once that budget becomes the limiting resource, an idle core that waits efficiently returns compute capacity that hardware can redistribute to productive work. Measurements on a recent AMD EPYC processor show how waiting strategy, processor topology, and idle duration determine this trade-off. Our results suggest that reclaiming idle cores often yields less benefit than commonly assumed while introducing substantial scheduling complexity. We propose a budget-centric view of service-core systems in which power, rather than core occupancy, becomes the fundamental resource and waiting policy becomes a first-class systems design choice.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Meta-Policies for Temporal Knowledge-Graph Memory under Partial Observability
comments: Accepted at ISWC 2026 (Research Track), LNCS 17126, pp. 191-209. v5: accepted-manuscript notice on the first page, wider margins
summary: Partially observable reinforcement learning requires deciding what to retain, retrieve, and forget over time. We introduce a neuro-symbolic meta-policy that learns which symbolic memory heuristic to apply at each decision point while keeping execution symbolic. Our setting uses temporal knowledge-graph memory in RoomKG, where hidden state and observations are represented as Resource Description Framework (RDF) graphs and memory is augmented with temporal RDF triple annotations. The model combines knowledge-graph encoding of memory contents with value heads for question answering, exploration, and forgetting, yielding a controller that is both adaptive and inspectable. This gives the work a direct Semantic Web grounding through RDF-based representation, annotation-compatible graph semantics, and graph-based symbolic operations over explicit memory state. On train/test room splits at long-term memory capacity of 512, the qualifier-aware StarE-GNN configuration achieves the best held-out performance among the compared symbolic, neural, and neuro-symbolic systems while preserving step-level traceability of memory-management decisions.

title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
comments: 29 pages, 5 figures, 16 tables. v2: Windowed draft attention is merged upstream in SGLang (PR #32673). Code: https://github.com/avalliappan-nvidia/windowed-mtp-b200
summary:
Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by having a draft propose tokens that a target verifies in parallel. Frontier models increasingly ship a built-in Multi-Token-Prediction (MTP) draft head, assumed to be cheap beside verification. A shipped full-attention MTP head can become disproportionately expensive beside a hybrid target at long context. The head attends over the full KV cache for each of $γ$ draft forwards per decode step, while only 9-25% of target layers retain full attention, so a single draft layer can issue context reads at a rate comparable to the whole target. On hard, low-acceptance workloads, deep native MTP becomes net-negative: slower than no speculation.
  We apply a StreamingLLM-style window plus attention sink to the draft only (Windowed-MTP); target verification remains full-context, so the target distribution is preserved. The intervention is training-free and drop-in. On three models from two hybrid families (Gated DeltaNet and Mamba2) at 1M context on one GPU in SGLang, it provides an acceptance-free 1.28-1.44x per-decode-step speedup over native MTP. The speedup grows with context; at matched acceptance, TPOT improves by the same factor. The window removes most of the draft's working set, and a compact ring buffer converts that reduction into physical capacity: it reclaims the otherwise dead draft pool, a measured 7.7-11.1% of total KV at 1M, making room for one additional concurrent 1M request in the Qwen-35B batch sweep.

title: IR275K: A Benchmark for Infrared Multi-Frame Super-Resolution Toward Efficient Remote Sensing
summary: Infrared multi-frame super-resolution (MFSR) exploits complementary observations to recover spatial detail, but its evaluation remains fragmented across datasets and protocols. A common benchmark is needed to evaluate reconstruction under weak texture, varying thermal contrast, and noise in the source imagery. It should also characterize reconstruction performance across different inter-frame displacement ranges. We introduce IR275K, a curated benchmark containing 594 in- frared video sequences and 275,196 frames. It provides sequence- level train/validation/test splits and a reproducible x4 evaluation protocol. Evaluation spans single-frame and multi-frame recon- struction using seven learned baselines, the CGMamba reference model, and bicubic interpolation. All learned methods are evalu- ated under both bicubic degradation and synthetic mixed sensor noise.EDVRleadstheoverallrankingunderbicubicdegradation, whereas MSDTGP leads under mixed sensor noise. DBSR leads thehigh-displacementUAVsubsetunderbothsettings.Controlled ablations using CGMamba show that real neighboring frames improve PSNR over center-frame repetition by 1.04 dB under bicubic degradation and 0.95 dB under mixed sensor noise. Center-frame conditioning also improves reconstruction under both settings. The benchmark thus reveals how reconstruction rankings and the benefits of neighboring frames depend on evaluation conditions. The complete IR275K dataset is publicly available at: https://github.com/InfraRecon7/IR275K.

title: Bayesian Complete-Pooling in Cross-Subject Classification for Motor Imagery Electroencephalogram
summary: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have long sought calibration-free operation, yet classifiers are typically benchmarked on discrimination alone. Discrimination is blind to calibration, a meaningful gap given that electroencephalogram (EEG) signals are nonstationary and point-estimate classifiers can become overconfident under distribution shift. We conducted a large-scale study contrasting Bayesian complete-pooling models against frequentist baselines for cross-subject, left-hand versus right-hand motor imagery EEG classification across 20 datasets. Each of six frequentist pipelines was paired with an analogous Bayesian pipeline sharing identical, deterministic feature extraction, so that only the classifier was Bayesian. Bayesian classifiers were fit via Markov chain Monte Carlo. Our primary metric was the Brier score, decomposed into reliability and resolution, alongside the area under the ROC curve for discrimination and Shannon entropy for sharpness. For each metric we fit a random-effects meta-analysis with Knapp-Hartung adjustment, verified by leave-one-out influence analysis. Bayesian complete-pooling produced statistically significant improvements in reliability and increases in predictive uncertainty (lower sharpness), with 95% confidence intervals of [-0.0029, -0.0001] for reliability and [0.0022, 0.0220] bits for entropy. Still, neither effect held statistical significance when datasets with flagged posterior sampling were excluded. Brier score, resolution, and discrimination showed no significant differences. Between-study heterogeneity was low across all metrics. Bayesian pipelines consumed roughly thirteen times more energy than their frequentist counterparts, a cost that remains modest relative to common household appliances. This modest cost makes partial-pooling across subjects and sessions, the structure complete-pooling omits, a feasible next step.

title: A genetic algorithm for student academic resource allocation
summary: The optimal allocation of academic resources to individual students is essential for addressing learner diversity and fostering equitable educational outcomes. Within the framework of the Erasmus+ KA220-SCH project, this paper models the selection of educational materials for high school mathematics students as a 0--1 binary combinatorial optimization problem subject to strict study time constraints. Given the NP-hard complexity of the formulation, exact solution methods become computationally intractable as resource catalogs scale. To address this challenge, we propose a Genetic Algorithm integrated with a specialized constraint repair mechanism to effectively search the binary decision space. Experimental evaluation across 10 independent runs demonstrates fast convergence, high solution quality, and strong algorithmic stability across different base seeds. These results confirm the practical utility of metaheuristic approaches for real-time decision-support systems in secondary education.

title: MS-GPT: Rethinking MS/MS De Novo Structure Elucidation as Spectrum-Induced Posterior Querying of a Molecule-Language Model
comments: 18 pages, 13 figures, and 11 tables, including appendices. Source code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/VIKI623/MS-GPT
summary: Molecular structure elucidation from tandem mass spectra (MS/MS) is a central inverse problem in analytical chemistry. Most existing approaches to MS/MS identification remain tied to reference libraries or predefined candidate sets, whereas de novo methods aim to generate structures directly from spectra. A common de novo route predicts a molecular fingerprint from the spectrum and then decodes structures from it, enabling decoder pretraining on large molecule-only corpora. However, this paradigm creates a training-inference mismatch: the decoder is trained on oracle fingerprints computed from molecules, but at inference it is queried with a noisy spectrum-induced fingerprint posterior that is typically collapsed to a single thresholded fingerprint. We introduce MS-GPT, which recasts fingerprint-mediated de novo elucidation as spectrum-induced posterior querying of a conditional molecule-language model. MS-GPT conditions a molecule-language model on fingerprints and formulas, then converts the spectrum-induced posterior into a band of fingerprint queries near the oracle-fingerprint manifold through active-bit density calibration. Candidates sampled across this band are pooled and ranked by generation frequency and posterior similarity. A lightweight LoRA adapter further mitigates domain-specific posterior bias while preserving the pretrained molecular prior. On NPLIB1 and MassSpecGym, MS-GPT sets a new state of the art, reaching Top-1/Top-10 exact-match accuracy of 17.1%/27.6% and 10.2%/13.2%, respectively, and candidate-pool scaling improves recovery with a near-linear increase in inference cost. The source code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/VIKI623/MS-GPT.
comment: 18 pages, 13 figures, and 11 tables, including appendices. Source code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/VIKI623/MS-GPT

title: Multimodal User Authentication via Keystroke-Triggered Fusion of Glove-Based Finger Pressure and Hand Kinematics
comments: 13 pages, 11 figures, 6 tables. Published in IEEE Access, vol. 14, pp. 163209-163221, 2026. v2: final published version (updated title, Leave-One-Impostor-Out evaluation, and results). Code: https://github.com/Issei-hyakuda/multimodal-keystroke-glove-authentication
summary: Keystroke dynamics constitute a cost-effective behavioral biometric, but their timing features degrade under environmental and hardware variation. We replace these features with 19 dimensions of finger pressure and hand kinematics, sampled around each keystroke by a custom data glove - ten piezoresistive pressure sensors and a nine-axis inertial measurement unit (IMU). The two modalities are encoded by separate convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) branches and joined only at the embedding. We collected typing data from ten participants, one enrolled as the genuine user. Training uses a desktop keyboard and evaluation a laptop keyboard recorded on a later day; the held-out impostor is excluded from training, and each of the nine takes that role in turn (Leave-One-Impostor-Out). Under this condition the method attains a mean Equal Error Rate (EER) of $0.53 \pm 0.42$% after three consecutive keystrokes, about 0.77 s of typing at the measured median pace, and $0.18 \pm 0.22$% after five. Results depend strongly on which impostor is held out. A per-modality ablation finds the fused model significantly better than both single-modality models at every smoothing window. The pressure-level channels carry that advantage and have to be scale-matched to deliver it, by separate encoders or by standardization indifferently.
comment: 13 pages, 11 figures, 6 tables. Published in IEEE Access, vol. 14, pp. 163209-163221, 2026. v2: final published version (updated title, Leave-One-Impostor-Out evaluation, and results). Code: https://github.com/Issei-hyakuda/multimodal-keystroke-glove-authentication

title: CogBattery: Human-Referenced Evaluation of Cognitive Task Behavior and Structure in Language Models
comments: 13 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables. Code at https://github.com/dengzhe-hou/CogBattery. Renamed from CogArena to avoid confusion with an unrelated benchmark of the same name
summary: Human cognitive tasks let us compare language models with humans under controlled conditions. Yet a model can reproduce the direction of a human effect while making different errors. CogBattery evaluates 54 open-weight language models on text adaptations of 13 cognitive paradigms, comparing each with human data from its source study. Like humans, models respond more to n-back lures than to controls, yet they make far more false alarms on ordinary non-targets. Most models' reported confidence separates correct from incorrect answers less well than humans' does, and most always choose the same wager, including models that classify accurately. These patterns span many model families. Across tasks, model scores share two dimensions. The first is closely tied to scale, yet larger models are not consistently closer to humans. Predefined cognitive groupings show no reliable predictive advantage over random groupings of the same size. These results show that matching human effect directions does not establish human-like behavior. CogBattery provides condition-level human references for testing errors and confidence reports in new models.
comment: 13 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables. Code at https://github.com/dengzhe-hou/CogBattery. Renamed from CogArena to avoid confusion with an unrelated benchmark of the same name

title: Decompose and Reorganize: Planning with Primitives and Visuomotor Policies Learned from Demonstrations
summary: Successfully automating dexterous, long-horizon bimanual manipulation requires frameworks capable of both high-level reasoning and fine-grained execution. Traditional task and motion planning (TAMP), while excellent at symbolic planning, is often brittle in contact-rich operations. Simultaneously, imitation learning (IL), while effective in manipulation tasks with visual feedback, is limited by its low capability in spatial generalization and multi-stage operation. To reconcile their complementary strengths and limitations, we propose DR-LfD (Decomposed and Reorganized Skills Learned from Demonstrations), a framework that integrates visuomotor policies into a TAMP-gated decision-making system. Based on contact relationships, DR-LfD decomposes human demonstrations into atomic skills, which are reproduced as visuomotor policies or object-centric primitives. The initiation, termination, and constraints of the visuomotor policies are carefully modeled and implemented in a TAMP-compatible form, enabling reorganization of skills learned from different sources. DR-LfD transforms the learning problem from one requiring exponential demonstration data over possible skill sequences to one whose demonstration burden scales with the number of distinct skill types, with limited data for each skill. Real-world and simulation benchmarks demonstrate data-efficient skill composition under unseen setups and physical constraints. On two DexMimicGen tasks, DR-LfD with 100 demonstrations outperforms diffusion-based imitation policies with 1000.

title: Evaluating Rollout-Verified Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of a Reasoning Model for Multi-Zone Variable-Air-Volume Control
comments: Revised and expanded version. 46 pages, 18 figures. Published in Energy and AI
summary: Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems account for a large share of building energy use. High-performance control often requires building-specific modeling or training, limiting scalability. We investigate whether a frontier reasoning model -- a large language model trained to use additional inference-time computation -- can coordinate multi-zone variable-air-volume control without building-specific training, and whether rollout-verified reinforcement fine-tuning can improve a smaller, locally deployable model. Five controllers were evaluated over five summer days in a physics-based four-zone emulator. Across three runs, GPT-5 used 6.8-7.4% less electricity than a Guideline 36-based baseline, but used less outdoor air and had lower CO$_2$ compliance. GPT-5 provided a capability reference for fine-tuning the smaller model. A trained reinforcement learning controller used 4.5% less electricity than the baseline while improving temperature and CO$_2$ compliance. To assess this controller's critic as a lower-cost verifier, we compared its estimates with deterministic rollout returns. Across 470 candidates, their correlation was 0.9995, yet the critic selected the best action in only 7 of 30 states. High overall correlation did not ensure reliable ranking at the same state. We fine-tuned gpt-oss-20b using rollout returns as rewards. One 200-step run produced no sustained improvement in the returns of sampled actions and no improvement in closed-loop performance. Analysis of the model's reasoning traces and quantitative tests showed that its next-state predictions of temperature and CO$_2$ were unreliable both before and after fine-tuning. Because next-state prediction is important for decision-making, these findings motivate testing whether supervised fine-tuning on next-state prediction improves subsequent rollout-verified reinforcement fine-tuning.
comment: Revised and expanded version. 46 pages, 18 figures. Published in Energy and AI

title: UniCross: Unified Cross-Skill Dexterous Manipulation Synthesis
summary: Many dexterous manipulation tasks require the object to remain securely held throughout the interaction. From the perspective of hand-object relational motion, such manipulation comprises four canonical skills: grasping, relocation, in-hand rotation, and in-hand translation. Human hands flexibly compose these skills to accomplish complex tasks. Existing approaches, however, model these skills separately with skill-specific action constraints, objectives, or even dedicated hand morphologies, which breaks the compatibility and continuity required for long-horizon composition. In this work, we present a unified framework that models all four skills in a single formulation instantiated with desired relational targets. The formulation preserves cross-skill compatibility and enables distillation of a single policy without skill identifiers, which achieves strong per-skill performance and generalizes to unseen objects. The compatibility further supports the policy to perform long-horizon skill chaining and execute relational targets unseen during training. The framework also applies across different hand morphologies. Together, these results suggest that distinct dexterous manipulation skills can be modeled as instantiations of a shared relational task formulation. Project page: https://zdchan.github.io/UniCross/

AI.title_translation: UniCross：统一的跨技能灵巧操作合成
AI.tldr: UniCross通过统一的手-物关系目标公式将抓取、重定位与掌内操作四类技能整合进单一策略，实现了无技能标识的长程连续灵巧操作与跨形态泛化。
AI.motivation: 人手可以通过灵活组合基本技能完成复杂操作，但现有方法通常对各项技能单独建模（采用各自独立的动作约束、目标函数或专用手部构型），破坏了长程任务技能组合所需的兼容性与连续性。
AI.method: UniCross提出了一个将四种基本技能（抓取、重定位、掌内旋转、掌内平移）归纳为期望手-物关系目标的统一定式。该公式保留了跨技能兼容性，能够将多技能蒸馏为一个不需要技能标识符（skill identifier）的单一策略，且能适应不同的手部构型。
AI.result: 所训练的单一策略在各项单独技能上均达到很强性能，并能泛化至未见过的物体；同时展现了长程技能串联组合能力，可执行训练中未见的关系目标，并在不同手部构型上均有效适用。
AI.conclusion: 研究表明，抓取、重定位和掌内操作等不同灵巧操作技能可以被统一建模为共享关系任务定式的具体实例化，从而为长程、多形态和未知场景下的灵巧操作提供高度兼容的通用范式。
AI.translation: 许多灵巧操作任务要求物体在整个交互过程中始终保持被稳固握持。从手-物相对运动的角度来看，此类操作包括四种典型技能：抓取、重定位、掌内旋转和掌内平移。人手可以灵活地组合这些技能以完成复杂任务。然而，现有方法通常使用针对特定技能的动作约束、目标乃至专用的手部构型来分别建模这些技能，这破坏了长程任务组合所需的兼容性与连续性。在本文中，我们提出了一个统一框架，通过期望的关系目标实例化，在单一公式中对所有四种技能进行建模。该公式保留了跨技能的兼容性，并支持在无需技能标识符的情况下蒸馏出单一策略，既能取得强大的各单项技能性能，又能泛化到未见过的物体。这种兼容性进一步支持该策略执行长程技能链式组合，并执行训练中未见过的关系目标。该框架还适用于不同的手部构型。综合来看，这些结果表明不同的灵巧操作技能可以被建模为共享关系任务定式的具体实例。
AI.summary: 针对灵巧操作技能建模割裂、难以长程组合的问题，本文提出UniCross框架。该框架基于手-物关系目标建立了包含抓取、重定位与掌内操作在内的统一建模体系，蒸馏出无需技能标识的单一策略，成功实现了优异的跨技能兼容性、未知物体泛化以及跨构型长程操作执行。
AI.keywords: 灵巧操作, 跨技能合成, 技能链式组合, 策略蒸馏, 手物交互
AI.comments: 该工作从手-物相对运动的核心视角出发，创新性地将传统上孤立建模的四类灵巧操作技能归纳为统一的关系目标定式。这种设计不仅消除了技能切换时的不连续性难题，还无需依赖技能显式标识符，实现了单策略多技能的端到端执行与长程编排，对于构建通用、高柔性的具身灵巧手控制系统具有重要价值。

title: ReBRAC-v2: The Return of the King
summary: Recent offline reinforcement learning methods increasingly rely on expressive generative policies and specialized value guidance. We ask how far systematic modernization of a conventional behavior-regularized actor-critic can go while preserving algorithmic simplicity. ReBRAC-v2 directly trains an exact-likelihood normalizing-flow actor with likelihood, MSE, and MAE behavior regularization, classification-based residual critics, staged optimization, and multi-sample inference. We develop one shared configuration through roughly 600 Bayesian proposals on six OGBench tasks, then adapt only two behavior-regularization coefficients using a 16-point grid for the main comparisons. Across ten common OGBench categories, ReBRAC-v2 averages 74.8 versus 52.3 for the next-best method and ranks first in eight categories. Without structural changes, it also obtains the strongest compared averages on D4RL AntMaze (90.2) and Adroit (33.6). Motivated by these results, we extend evaluation to all 235 state-based single-task problems across the 47 dataset variants in the original OGBench suite. To our knowledge, this is the first complete evaluation in this setting; no compared baseline reports results across the full suite. Per-task scores and configurations establish ReBRAC-v2 as a reference baseline for future work beyond the common task subset. The complete cloning objective retains the highest average after coefficient retuning of its alternatives, while further ablations characterize training, capacity, and inference choices. These results demonstrate the strength of systematic engineering within a minimalist offline RL foundation.

AI.tldr: ReBRAC-v2通过系统现代化行为正则化Actor-Critic方法，在离线RL任务中取得了显著的SOTA性能，并在OGBench和D4RL上进行了广泛评估。
AI.motivation: 该研究旨在探讨在保持算法简单性的前提下，传统行为正则化Actor-Critic方法在多大程度上能够通过系统现代化来提升性能，以应对当前离线强化学习对表达性生成策略和专门价值指导的依赖。
AI.method: ReBRAC-v2直接训练一个精确似然归一化流Actor，结合似然、MSE和MAE行为正则化、基于分类的残差Critic、分阶段优化和多样本推理。通过贝叶斯提议开发共享配置，并对行为正则化系数进行精细调整。评估扩展到OGBench的235个单任务问题及D4RL基准。
AI.result: ReBRAC-v2在十个常见OGBench类别中平均得分74.8（次优为52.3），并在八个类别中排名第一。在D4RL AntMaze（90.2）和Adroit（33.6）上也获得了最强的平均值。其性能在OGBench完整套件中建立了新的参考基线。
AI.conclusion: 研究结果证明了在极简离线RL基础内进行系统工程的强大能力。ReBRAC-v2凭借其强大的性能和全面的评估，被确立为未来工作的参考基线。
AI.translation: 最近的离线强化学习方法越来越依赖于表达性生成策略和专门的价值指导。我们探讨了在保持算法简单性的同时，传统行为正则化Actor-Critic方法能够进行系统现代化到何种程度。ReBRAC-v2直接训练一个精确似然归一化流Actor，使用似然、MSE和MAE行为正则化，基于分类的残差Critic，分阶段优化和多样本推理。我们通过在六个OGBench任务上进行大约600次贝叶斯提议开发了一个共享配置，然后仅使用16点网格调整了两个行为正则化系数进行主要比较。在十个常见的OGBench类别中，ReBRAC-v2平均得分74.8，而次优方法为52.3，并在八个类别中排名第一。在没有结构性变化的情况下，它还在D4RL AntMaze（90.2）和Adroit（33.6）上获得了最强的比较平均值。受这些结果的启发，我们将评估扩展到原始OGBench套件中47个数据集变体中的所有235个基于状态的单任务问题。据我们所知，这是在此设置下的首次完整评估；没有比较基线报告了完整套件的结果。每个任务的得分和配置将ReBRAC-v2确立为超越常见任务子集的未来工作的参考基线。在对其替代方案进行系数重新调整后，完整的克隆目标保留了最高的平均值，而进一步的消融研究则表征了训练、容量和推理选择。这些结果证明了在极简离线RL基础内系统工程的强大能力。
AI.summary: ReBRAC-v2通过对传统行为正则化Actor-Critic方法进行系统性现代化，在保持算法简洁性的同时，显著提升了离线强化学习的性能。该方法采用精确似然归一化流Actor、多种行为正则化、残差Critic、分阶段优化和多样本推理。ReBRAC-v2在OGBench和D4RL基准测试中均取得了最先进的平均表现，并在OGBench的广泛任务中确立了新的参考基线。研究强调了在极简离线RL框架内进行系统工程的有效性。
AI.keywords: 离线强化学习, 行为正则化, Actor-Critic, ReBRAC-v2, OGBench
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过对现有行为正则化Actor-Critic框架进行系统性工程优化，而非引入复杂的新范式，展示了在保持算法简洁性的前提下，传统方法仍有巨大潜力。其在OGBench和D4RL上的全面评估，尤其是在OGBench完整套件上的首次完整评估，为未来的离线RL研究提供了宝贵的基准。这种“王者归来”的叙事也暗示了对现有范式深度挖掘的价值。

title: GUI-Lens: Enabling Precise GUI Grounding for Off-the-Shelf VLMs via Coarse-to-Fine Cropping
summary: GUI grounding maps natural-language instructions to click locations and is essential for reliable GUI agents. The task remains difficult on high-resolution, densely populated interfaces because a vision-language model (VLM) may recognize a requested control without locating it precisely enough for interaction. Most existing methods provide various forms of localization assistance, but still rely on a direct click prediction, allowing visual ambiguity or an inaccurate initial estimate to propagate to the final result. In this paper, we introduce GUI-Lens, a coarse-to-fine grounding framework that allows a general-purpose VLM to determine the target through active visual observations. Specifically, GUI-Lens extracts OCR text and detected UI components from the screenshot and presents their positions as coordinate references. Using the instruction, the current view, and these references, the VLM selects the region and scale of the next view, which is cropped and enlarged to provide finer visual details. This process continues over successively focused views until the target is determined. Proposed crops and clicks are checked against the instruction throughout the process, and the final local position is mapped back to the original screen coordinates. Experiments on five GUI grounding benchmarks and six general-purpose base models show that GUI-Lens consistently improves grounding accuracy, achieving up to 9.3 times the accuracy of direct grounding on ScreenSpot-Pro.

AI.title_translation: GUI-Lens：通过粗到细裁剪实现现成VLM的精确GUI接地
AI.tldr: GUI-Lens是一个粗到细的框架，通过主动视觉观察和迭代裁剪，显著提高了VLM在复杂GUI上的精确接地能力，避免了现有方法的定位不准确问题。
AI.motivation: 现有的GUI接地方法在处理高分辨率、密集界面时，由于VLM难以精确识别点击位置，或初始估计不准确，导致最终结果不准确。
AI.method: GUI-Lens是一个粗到细的接地框架。它从屏幕截图中提取OCR文本和检测到的UI组件，并将其位置作为坐标参考。VLM根据指令、当前视图和这些参考，选择下一个视图的区域和比例，然后裁剪和放大该视图以提供更精细的视觉细节。此过程在连续聚焦的视图上重复进行，直到确定目标。建议的裁剪和点击在整个过程中都会根据指令进行检查，最终的局部位置会映射回原始屏幕坐标。
AI.result: GUI-Lens在五个GUI接地基准和六个通用基础模型上持续提高了接地精度，在ScreenSpot-Pro上实现了高达9.3倍于直接接地的精度。
AI.conclusion: GUI-Lens通过其粗到细的接地框架和主动视觉观察，显著提升了通用VLM在复杂GUI界面上的精确接地能力。
AI.translation: GUI接地将自然语言指令映射到点击位置，对于可靠的GUI代理至关重要。在高分辨率、密集界面的任务仍然很困难，因为视觉语言模型（VLM）可能识别出请求的控件，但无法精确地定位它以进行交互。大多数现有方法提供各种形式的定位辅助，但仍依赖于直接点击预测，这使得视觉模糊或不准确的初始估计传播到最终结果。在本文中，我们引入了GUI-Lens，一个粗到细的接地框架，允许通用VLM通过主动视觉观察确定目标。具体来说，GUI-Lens从屏幕截图中提取OCR文本和检测到的UI组件，并将其位置作为坐标参考。VLM使用指令、当前视图和这些参考，选择下一个视图的区域和比例，该视图被裁剪和放大以提供更精细的视觉细节。这个过程在连续聚焦的视图上继续进行，直到确定目标。在整个过程中，建议的裁剪和点击都会根据指令进行检查，最终的局部位置会映射回原始屏幕坐标。在五个GUI接地基准和六个通用基础模型上的实验表明，GUI-Lens持续提高了接地精度，在ScreenSpot-Pro上实现了高达9.3倍于直接接地的精度。
AI.summary: 本文提出了GUI-Lens，一个创新的粗到细接地框架，旨在解决现有视觉语言模型（VLM）在复杂高分辨率图形用户界面（GUI）中难以精确识别和定位交互元素的问题。GUI-Lens通过迭代地裁剪和放大视图，结合OCR文本和UI组件的位置参考，使VLM能够进行主动视觉观察，从而逐步聚焦并精确确定目标。实验证明，GUI-Lens显著提升了VLM的接地精度，在多个基准测试中表现优异。
AI.keywords: GUI接地, 视觉语言模型, 粗到细裁剪, 精确定位, GUI-Lens
AI.comments: GUI-Lens的创新之处在于其“粗到细”的迭代裁剪和主动视觉观察机制，这有效解决了现有VLM在GUI接地任务中精度不足的问题。通过将定位过程分解为多个聚焦步骤，并结合上下文参考，它显著降低了视觉模糊和初始估计误差的影响。这项工作对于开发更可靠、更精确的GUI自动化代理具有重要意义。

title: Adaptive-WAM: Quality-Guided Early-Exit Planning from Intermediate Video-Diffusion Features
summary: Large video diffusion models provide rich spatiotemporal priors for autonomous driving, but existing world-action models often inherit the cost of iterative future-video generation even though deployment only requires an ego trajectory. We ask a more basic question: how much of a video diffusion model must be executed to make a reliable driving decision? Through a controlled study of video denoising timesteps and Diffusion Transformer (DiT) depth, we find that planning performance is largely insensitive to the tested video-noise levels, whereas strong trajectories can already be decoded from intermediate layers. Based on this observation, we introduce Adaptive-WAM, a quality-aware multi-exit planner built on a Wan2.2-5B backbone. Trajectory diffusion heads are attached to selected DiT blocks, and a lightweight trajectory-quality scorer terminates inference once the best trajectory decoded so far satisfies a quality threshold; otherwise, computation continues from the cached hidden state to a deeper exit. The deployed planner therefore avoids the iterative classifier-free denoising loop and VAE decoding required for future-video synthesis, while dynamically allocating backbone depth according to trajectory quality. On NAVSIM, the adaptive single-trajectory planner achieves 90.8 PDMS; a separate fixed-exit variant reaches 92.6 PDMS with 64 proposals. It further obtains 89.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, yielding the best reported results among the compared front-view video world-model planners. Without target-domain fine-tuning, Adaptive-WAM transfers to nuScenes with 0.88 m average L2 error and a 0.08\% collision rate. On an A100, adaptive routing improves PDMS from 90.62 to 90.79 while averaging 170 ms end-to-end planning latency, approximately 10\% below the 190 ms fixed block-15 planner and 47\% below the 320 ms fixed full-depth planner. Code will be released.

AI.title_translation: Adaptive-WAM：基于中间视频扩散特征的质量引导提前退出规划
AI.tldr: 论文提出了Adaptive-WAM，利用视频扩散模型的中间特征进行质量引导的动态提前退出规划，在大幅降低计算延迟的同时实现了领先的自动驾驶规划性能。
AI.motivation: 现有的基于视频扩散模型的世界-动作模型虽然能提供丰富的时空先验，但由于继承了迭代式未来视频生成的巨大计算成本，导致部署效率低下，而实际自动驾驶部署仅需要自车轨迹。
AI.method: 基于Wan2.2-5B骨干网络构建了Adaptive-WAM，在选定的DiT块上附加轨迹扩散头，并引入轻量级轨迹质量评分器，当解码出的轨迹满足质量阈值时提前终止推理，否则继续利用缓存的隐藏状态向更深层退出。
AI.result: 在NAVSIM上取得了90.8的PDMS（固定出口变体达92.6 PDMS），在NAVSIM v2上取得了89.9 EPDMS，在nuScenes上零样本迁移实现了0.88米的平均L2误差和0.08%的碰撞率，端到端延迟降低至170毫秒。
AI.conclusion: Adaptive-WAM通过质量引导的动态提前退出策略，成功打破了视频扩散世界模型在自动驾驶规划中必须进行全量视频生成的固有开销，实现了高效且高性能的轨迹规划。
AI.translation: 大型视频扩散模型为自动驾驶提供了丰富的时空先验，但现有的世界-动作模型往往继承了迭代式未来视频生成的成本，尽管实际部署仅需要自车轨迹。我们提出了一个更基本的问题：为了做出可靠的驾驶决策，必须执行多少视频扩散模型？通过对视频去噪时间步长和扩散Transformer（DiT）深度的控制研究，我们发现规划性能对所测试的视频噪声水平基本不敏感，而强大的轨迹已经可以从中间层解码。基于这一观察，我们推出了Adaptive-WAM，这是一个建立在Wan2.2-5B骨干网上的质量感知多出口规划器。轨迹扩散头附加到选定的DiT块上，轻量级轨迹质量评分器在迄今解码的最佳轨迹满足质量阈值时终止推理；否则，计算从缓存的隐藏状态继续到更深的出口。因此，部署的规划器避免了未来视频合成所需的迭代无分类器去噪循环和VAE解码，同时根据轨迹质量动态分配骨干网深度。在NAVSIM上，自适应单轨迹规划器实现了90.8的PDMS；一个单独的固定出口变体在64个候选下达到了92.6的PDMS。它还在NAVSIM v2上获得了89.9的EPDMS，在所比较的前视视频世界模型规划器中取得了最佳报告结果。在没有目标域微调的情况下，Adaptive-WAM迁移到nuScenes时平均L2误差为0.08米，碰撞率为0.08%。在A100上，自适应路由将PDMS从90.62提升至90.79，端到端规划延迟平均为170毫秒，比190毫秒的固定第15块规划器低约10%，比320毫秒的固定全深度规划器低47%。代码将开源。
AI.summary: 论文提出了Adaptive-WAM，一种基于中间视频扩散特征的质量引导提前退出规划方法。该方法通过在Diffusion Transformer的不同深度附加轨迹头并结合轻量级质量评分器，动态分配网络深度，避免了迭代式视频去噪循环和VAE解码，在保证优异规划性能的同时大幅降低了计算延迟。
AI.keywords: 自适应规划, 视频扩散模型, 自动驾驶, 提前退出, 扩散Transformer
AI.comments: 该论文通过观察发现视频扩散模型的中间层特征已经足够用于生成高质量的自动驾驶轨迹，从而创新性地提出了Adaptive-WAM，跳过了全量视频生成和VAE解码的巨大开销，实现了质量引导的动态提前退出，大幅提升了自动驾驶世界的规划效率和性能。

title: HOPE: Hand-Object Pressure Estimation from Monocular Videos
summary: Estimating physical pressure from vision is essential for understanding contact-rich hand-object interaction. However, prior vision-based pressure estimation methods are largely limited to planar surfaces and single image input, making them difficult to apply to dynamic hand-object interaction with diverse objects. We instead formulate pressure estimation as a hand-centric video prediction problem with monocular video as input. This formulation predicts temporally evolving per-vertex normal pressure and contact directly on the hand mesh, yielding a unified output space independent of object shape and sensor layout. Building on this formulation, we propose \textbf{HOPE}, a framework with two key components. First, we lift tactile-glove pressure, planar-sensor pressure, and distance-based hand-object contact annotations into a shared hand vertex space, allowing bare-hand contact data to regularize pressure learning where labels are unavailable. Second, we introduce a vertex-anchored video transformer that treats each vertex as a persistent token, aggregates visual features and hand pose over time, and uses a contact-gated pressure head to suppress pressure predictions in regions with low contact probability. Experiments on OpenTouch, PressureVisionDB, and hand-object contact benchmarks validate HOPE across object-pressure, surface-pressure, and contact-supervised HOI settings. Despite using pressure supervision primarily from gloved-hand videos, HOPE generalizes to bare-hand egocentric and in-the-wild videos, producing joint contact and pressure predictions beyond the scope of contact-only or planar-pressure baselines.

AI.title_translation: HOPE：基于单目视频的手部-物体压力估计
AI.tldr: 提出一种名为HOPE的新框架，首次能够仅通过单目视频预测动态手物交互中手部顶点的物理压力和接触。
AI.motivation: 现有的基于视觉的压力估计方法大多局限于平面表面和单图像输入，难以应用于具有多样化物体的动态手物交互。
AI.method: 提出HOPE框架，将多种触控数据和距离接触标注转换到统一的手部顶点空间，并通过顶点锚定的视频变换器（vertex-anchored video transformer）结合接触门控压力头来预测压力和接触。
AI.result: 在OpenTouch、PressureVisionDB和手物接触基准测试上的实验验证了HOPE在各种设置下的有效性，能够泛化到裸手第一人称和野外视频中。
AI.conclusion: HOPE框架成功实现了从单目视频中对动态手物交互过程中的手部表面压力和接触进行准确预测，具有强大的泛化能力。
AI.translation: 从视觉中估计物理压力对于理解富含接触的手物交互至关重要。然而，先前的基于视觉的压力估计方法大都局限于平面和单张图像输入，使其难以应用于具有多样化物体的动态手物交互。为此，我们将压力估计构想为一个以手为中心的视频预测问题，以单目视频作为输入。该构想直接在手部网格上预测时间演化的每个顶点法向压力和接触，从而产生一个独立于物体形状和传感器布局的统一输出空间。在此基础上，我们提出了HOPE框架，包含两个核心组件。首先，我们将触觉手套压力、平面传感器压力和基于距离的手物接触标注提升到一个共享的手部顶点空间，从而允许在缺乏标签的情况下利用裸手接触数据来正则化压力学习。其次，我们引入了一个顶点锚定的视频变换器，将每个顶点视为持久标记，随时间聚合视觉特征和手部姿态，并利用接触门控压力头来抑制低接触概率区域的压力预测。在OpenTouch、PressureVisionDB和手物接触基准上的实验验证了HOPE在物体压力、表面压力和接触监督的HOI设置下的有效性。尽管其压力监督主要来自戴手套的手部视频，但HOPE仍可泛化至裸手第一人称视角及野外视频，产生超越仅接触或平面压力基线方法的联合接触与压力预测。
AI.summary: 论文提出了HOPE框架，通过将单目视频输入转化为手部顶点的压力和接触预测，解决了现有方法局限于平面和单图的痛点，并在多个数据集上取得了良好的泛化和预测效果。
AI.keywords: 手物交互, 压力估计, 视频预测, 手部网格, 变换器模型
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将手部物理压力估计建模为手心视角的视频预测问题，突破了以往仅限于平面和单图输入的限制，并通过统一的手部网格输出空间和多源数据融合实现了裸手视频的压力预测。

title: The No-Meaning Falsity: The Structural Impossibility of the Arbitrary Sign in Classical Arabic
summary: This paper investigates whether the postmodern claim of unrestricted semantic indeterminacy, and its foundational Saussurean axiom of the arbitrary sign, are compatible with the structural architecture of Classical Arabic. We develop a formal mathematical model of Arabic non concatenative morphology in which lexical meaning is determined by the interaction between an invariant root and a morphosyntactic pattern. Within this framework, we establish a Morphological Correspondence Theorem, demonstrating that every lexical item is uniquely generated by a root pattern pair, and a Semantic Localization Theorem, proving that lexical meaning is determined at the derivational level prior to surface realization. To address Saussurean weaker notion of relative arbitrariness, we formalize it via conditional Kolmogorov complexity, defining arbitrariness algorithmically as the no rule property. We prove that general relative arbitrariness is formally undecidable, while Arabic relative arbitrariness is decidable and provably less than 1 for its motivated signifiers (Levels W and M), establishing a strict system complexity asymmetry over Indo-European languages.

AI.title_translation: 无意义的虚假性：古典阿拉伯语中任意符号的结构不可能性
AI.tldr: 本论文通过数学建模证明了古典阿拉伯语的形态和语义结构排除了索绪尔“任意符号”的假设，显示出与印欧语系截然不同的系统复杂度。
AI.motivation: 探究后现代语义不确定性主张及索绪尔“任意符号”的基石公理是否与古典阿拉伯语的结构架构相容。
AI.method: 开发了阿拉伯语非级联形态学的形式化数学模型，证明了形态对应定理与语义定位定理，并利用条件柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂度将相对任意性形式化为算法上的“无规则属性”来进行判定。
AI.result: 证明了每个词条都由根式-模式对唯一生成，词义在衍生层面先于表层实现决定；同时证明了一般的相对任意性是不可判定的，而阿拉伯语的相对任意性是可判定的且对于受动机支配的能指严格小于1，确立了其与印欧语系的系统复杂度不对称性。
AI.conclusion: 古典阿拉伯语的形态和语义结构在数学上排除了完全的语义不确定性与任意性，证明了闪米特语系与印欧语系在系统复杂度上的根本差异。
AI.translation: 本文研究了后现代关于无限制语义不确定性的主张及其索绪尔关于任意符号的基础公理是否与古典阿拉伯语的结构架构相容。我们开发了一个阿拉伯语非级联形态学的形式化数学模型，其中词义由不变的根式与形态句法模式之间的相互作用决定。在此框架内，我们确立了形态对应定理（证明每个词条都由根式-模式对唯一生成）和语义定位定理（证明词义在表层实现之前的衍生层面就被决定）。为了解决索绪尔关于相对任意性的较弱概念，我们通过条件柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂度将其形式化，从算法上将任意性定义为“无规则属性”。我们证明了一般的相对任意性在形式上是不可判定的，而阿拉伯语的相对任意性是可判定的，并且对于其受动机支配的能指（W和M级别）证明小于1，从而确立了其相对于印欧语系的严格系统复杂度不对称性。
AI.summary: 本文通过建立形式化数学模型，探讨了古典阿拉伯语形态学与索绪尔“任意符号”公理的相容性。研究证明，阿拉伯语的词义由根式与形态模式的交互在衍生阶段唯一确定，其相对任意性可判定且小于1，从而在结构上否定了该语言中存在无限制的任意符号。
AI.keywords: 古典阿拉伯语, 索绪尔任意性, 非级联形态学, 柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂度, 形式化语言学
AI.comments: 该论文运用形式化数学模型和算法复杂度理论，严格证明了古典阿拉伯语的非级联形态学不符合索绪尔“能指的任意性”公理，为语言学结构类型差异提供了开创性的形式化证据。

title: You Only Pass Once: Answering and Abstaining Together in a Single Forward Pass of a Frozen Language Model
comments: 31 pages. Ziyang Luo and Zhongyao Chu contributed equally
summary: A frozen language model under-uses the evidence in its hidden states and answers confidently when the context contains no answer. We fix both on the residual stream without changing any weight. For accuracy, a small trained network (the probe) adds an input-dependent vector to the residual at several middle layers; it raises Qwen2.5-1.5B on $α$NLI from 51% to 73% accuracy. For abstention, a fixed vector (the direction), the mean hidden state of contexts that contain the answer minus that of contexts that do not, scores the hidden state; a low score abstains. On four QA datasets with human answerability labels (Qwen2.5-7B), moving the direction to a dataset it was not fit on costs under 3 points of decision accuracy (from 0.83 in domain) on average and still beats asking the model whether its context suffices; the same judgment trained as a classifier into the probe's activation edit or into LoRA weights loses 16 and 22 points and ends below asking. We set out to put both functions on a single forward pass, and found that the probe's edit changes the very hidden state the direction scores, degrading it. A small map -- trained without labels, only to reconstruct the unedited hidden state from the edited one -- removes 63% of that interference on 1.5B. Refit on the hidden-state pairs of LoFiT or LoReFT, the same recipe repairs those methods too: the steering module is replaceable. The resulting system, YOPO, answers and abstains in one forward pass. On $α$NLI it raises three-way accuracy from 0.38 to about 0.75 on 1.5B, and stays within 0.02 of a two-pass reference on 1.5B, 3B and 7B, at half the cost. We also observe improvements on the four QA datasets, where answerability is human-labeled and answers are generated as free-form text. Near-parity with the two-pass reference holds across nine backbones spanning six model families without backbone-specific hyperparameter tuning.
comment: 31 pages. Ziyang Luo and Zhongyao Chu contributed equally

AI.title_translation: 单次前向传播即可：在冻结语言模型的单次前向传播中同时实现回答与弃权
AI.tldr: YOPO利用残差流编辑与特征重建映射，在冻结语言模型的单次前向传播中以减半的成本同时实现了高准确率回答和稳健的拒答判断。
AI.motivation: 冻结的语言模型未能充分利用其隐藏状态中的证据，在上下文不包含答案时仍会过度自信地回答；而现有的回答增强方法（激活编辑）与弃权检测结合在单次前向传播中时，编辑操作会干扰弃权评分所需的隐藏状态。
AI.method: 1. 准确率提升：在中间若干层的残差流中，通过小型训练网络（探针/probe）添加与输入相关的向量；\n2. 弃权决策：计算包含答案与不包含答案上下文的平均隐状态差值作为固定方向向量，对隐状态打分以决定是否弃权；\n3. 单次传递整合（YOPO）：针对探针编辑污染隐状态评分的问题，训练一个无标签的小型映射模块，从编辑后的隐状态中重建未编辑状态以消除干扰，实现单次前向传播中回答与弃权的并行。
AI.result:
1. 准确率方面：使Qwen2.5-1.5B在αNLI上的准确率从51%提高到73%，三分类准确率从0.38升至约0.75；
2. 弃权决策方面：方向向量在域外迁移时准确率损失低于3点（域内0.83），明显优于分类器与直接询问模型；
3. 融合效果：无标签映射消除了1.5B模型上63%的编辑干扰；
4. 效率与泛化：YOPO在1.5B/3B/7B模型上以双传递参考基准一半的计算成本达到与其相差0.02以内的性能，且在无需针对性调参的情况下泛化至6个模型家族的9种主干网络。
AI.conclusion: YOPO成功证明了无需修改原始模型权重，仅通过轻量级残差流操作与无标签重建映射，即可在冻结语言模型的单次前向传播中同时实现高效准确的回答与稳健的拒答（弃权），在显著降低推理开销的同时保持了卓越的性能。
AI.translation: 冻结的语言模型未能充分利用其隐藏状态中的证据，并在上下文不包含答案时过度自信地作答。我们在不改变任何权重的情况下，在残差流上修复了这两个问题。为了提高准确率，一个经过训练的小型网络（探针）在数个中间层的残差中添加一个与输入相关的向量；它将 Qwen2.5-1.5B 在 αNLI 上的准确率从 51% 提升至 73%。为了实现弃权，一个固定向量（方向向量）——即包含答案的上下文的平均隐藏状态减去不包含答案的上下文的平均隐藏状态——对隐藏状态进行评分；得分低则弃权。在四个带有高质量人工可回答性标签的问答数据集上（Qwen2.5-7B），将该方向向量迁移到未拟合的数据集上平均仅损失不到 3 个百分点的决策准确率（域内为 0.83），并且依然优于直接询问模型上下文是否充分；而通过将相同判断作为分类器训练至探针的激活编辑或 LoRA 权重中，准确率则分别下降了 16 和 22 个百分点，且最终表现不如直接询问。我们着手将这两个功能整合到单次前向传播中，却发现探针的编辑改变了方向向量所需评分的隐藏状态本身，从而降低了其效果。一个无需标签即可训练的小型映射——仅用于从编辑后的隐藏状态中重建未编辑状态——消除了 1.5B 模型上 63% 的此类干扰。在 LoFiT 或 LoReFT 的隐藏状态对上重新拟合，相同的方案也能修复这些方法：引导模块是可替换的。最终构建的系统 YOPO 能够在一次前向传播中同时完成回答和弃权。在 αNLI 上，它将 1.5B 模型的三分类准确率从 0.38 提高到约 0.75，并且在 1.5B、3B 和 7B 模型上，以一半的成本与两次传播的参考基准差距保持在 0.02 以内。我们还在四个问答数据集上观察到了性能提升，其中可回答性经人工标注，答案以自由文本形式生成。在无需针对特定主干进行超参数微调的情况下，该方法在涵盖 6 个模型家族的 9 个主干模型中均保持了与两次传播参考基准接近的性能。
AI.summary: 本文提出YOPO框架，旨在不修改冻结语言模型权重的前提下，通过单次前向传播同时完成高准确率回答与可靠弃权。方法利用残差探针增强答案生成，利用均值差方向向量评估可回答性，并通过小型无监督重建映射消除了编辑对弃权判别的表征干扰，在多个问答基准和模型架构上验证了其兼顾低成本与高性能的优势。
AI.keywords: 冻结语言模型, 弃权判断, 残差流编辑, 单次前向传播, 隐藏状态重建
AI.comments: 该研究针对语言模型“幻觉”和“过度自信”问题提出了一种极具实用价值的轻量级推理方案。其主要创新在于揭示并解决了单次传递中残差激活编辑与隐状态特征检测之间的表征干扰问题，通过引入无监督逆映射实现了回答生成与弃权判断的解耦与合并，既节约了推理成本，又保持了强大的跨模型、跨任务泛化能力。

title: Porting and Benchmarking Chapel on Emerging RISC-V Hardware: An HPC Viability Study
summary: The Chapel programming language recently added support for the RISC-V architecture. Here we discuss what changes were needed for Chapel to work on RISC-V as well as lessons learned from the porting process. We use some of Chapel's extensive benchmark suite to gain further insight into the suitability of the RISC-V architecture for future HPC use. We compare performance on SiFive P550 and Unmatched boards and a Sophon SG2042 with a variety of other recent HPC CPU platforms. Various portability and performance anomalies arose on different architectures and are discussed. While the RISC-V machines represent smaller preliminary offerings and not HPC-class hardware, these results still provide hope that RISC-V hardware can become viable for HPC in the near future.

AI.title_translation: 将Chapel移植并在新兴RISC-V硬件上进行基准测试：一项HPC可行性研究
AI.tldr: 本文研究了Chapel语言向RISC-V架构的移植及其性能基准测试，评估了RISC-V在未来HPC应用中的可行性。
AI.motivation: 为了解Chapel在RISC-V上的适配需求以及总结移植经验，同时通过基准测试深入评估新兴RISC-V架构未来用于高性能计算（HPC）的适宜性和可行性。
AI.method: 将Chapel编程语言移植到RISC-V架构上，在SiFive P550、Unmatched开发板以及Sophon SG2042等硬件上运行Chapel的基准测试套件，并将其性能与其他近期HPC CPU平台进行对比。
AI.result: 识别并讨论了不同架构上出现的各种可移植性和性能异常，虽然测试的RISC-V机器是较小的初步产品而非HPC级硬件，但结果显示出其未来在HPC中具备可行性的希望。
AI.conclusion: 尽管目前的RISC-V硬件尚未达到HPC级别，但其初步成果表明该架构未来在高性能计算领域具有巨大的可行性。
